missing_in_r.name: Default narrowing result-type rules (float_type_for / sum_type_for / int_type_for / unsigned_type_for)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia ALWAYS casts every reduction/eltwise result to a default narrowed storage type when no `type=` is given (operations.jl:57-186, reduction_result_type for each op). E.g. Sum/Mean/Var/Std/Median/Quantile/GeoMean of a Float32 input -> Float32 result; Mean/Var/Std of an Int32 input -> Float32 result; Sum of Int8/UInt8/Bool -> Int32/UInt32; Abs -> unsigned_type_for. R has no Float32 / unsigned / sized-int storage, so op_dispatch.R only calls .cast_to_type when an explicit `type=` is present (query_eval.R:2759-2761, 2867-2869); otherwise the result is left Float64/double. For Float64/double inputs the value is identical, so this is cosmetic there. But for a Float32-typed stored matrix/vector, Julia rounds the reduction result to Float32 precision while R keeps full Float64 -> the two answers differ in the low ~29 bits of the mantissa. This is the largest systematic divergence in the subsystem and is a genuine (small-magnitude) value difference, not just a storage-class label.

missing_in_r.name: Significant dense->sparse promotion
missing_in_r.detail: Julia Significant returns a SparseMatrixCSC / SparseVector whenever it zeros out any entry of a dense input (operations.jl:963-967 for matrix, 980-985 for vector). R's .op_significant keeps a dense input dense (operations.R:849-857 returns a plain matrix; the vector branch returns a plain vector) and only preserves sparsity for dgCMatrix input. Values are identical; the result's storage class (dense vs sparse) differs. Observable if a downstream op or test inspects sparsity/issparse, or if a later chained operation has a sparse-specific fast path with slightly different float accumulation order.

missing_in_r.name: parse_int_type_value query exposure
missing_in_r.detail: Julia exports parse_int_type_value (operations.jl:277-288, itself marked UNTESTED) which restricts a `type=` tag to integer types only. No DAF builtin currently uses it (Convert/Sum/Count use parse_number_type_value; Round uses parse_number_type_value too, NOT parse_int_type_value), so there is no observable query-DSL path that exercises an int-only restriction. R has no analogue but also no op needs one. Listed only for completeness of the exported surface.

narrowed.name: Round default output type
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia Round with no `type=` uses int_type_for(eltype): Float32->Int32, Float64->Int64, Int8->Int8, etc. (operations.jl:99-119, 504). R's .op_round hardcodes Int64 as the default for any non-integer numeric input (operations.R:285-299), backed by bit64::integer64. So `% Round` of a Float32 column gives Int32 in Julia but integer64 in R. Values match for in-range integers; the storage width / class differs and a subsequent `% Round type Int8`-style InexactError boundary at 2^31 would only trip in Julia (Int32 result) not in R (Int64 result).

narrowed.name: Count default type
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia Count defaults to UInt32 (operations.jl:1052-1054). R's .op_count returns length(x) as a plain double/integer with no UInt32 cast unless `type=` is given (operations.R:234-237). Value identical for any realistic count; storage class differs (no UInt32 in R).

narrowed.name: Convert/Round/Sum to UInt* and Int64/UInt64 storage
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia keeps true UInt8/16/32/64 and Int64 storage. R maps Int8/16/32 and all UInt* narrower-than-64 onto R's 32-bit `integer`, and Int64/UInt64 onto bit64::integer64 (operations.R:346-357). UInt64 values above 2^63 cannot be represented faithfully by integer64 (signed). Range/inexact checks use .INT_TYPE_RANGES with UInt64 upper bound 2^64-1 stored as a double (operations.R:483), but the actual stored value would wrap/lose precision past 2^53. So `% Convert type UInt64` of a value in (2^53, 2^64) silently loses precision in R where Julia is exact.

narrowed.name: Significant `low` lower-bound check
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia query parser rejects low<0 with 'not negative' but the keyword constructor asserts low>0 (operations.jl:904 `@assert low > 0`). The query path (the one reachable from a query string) allows low==0 (operations.jl:920 checks `low < 0`). R's .op_significant query path also allows low==0 (operations.R:772 checks `low < 0`). Matched on the query path; the keyword-ctor-only `low>0` assertion is not reachable from a query so not a real gap. Listed to flag the asymmetry was checked and is NOT a divergence on the DSL path.

divergences.name: Exp / Sqrt extra eltwise ops in R only
divergences.julia_behavior: Neither Exp nor Sqrt exists in DataAxesFormats.jl operations.jl (confirmed: no struct/export anywhere in src/*.jl). A query `% Exp` or `% Sqrt` raises an 'unknown operation' parse error in Julia.
divergences.r_behavior: dafr registers Exp (operations.R:277-280) and Sqrt (operations.R:281-284) as builtin eltwise ops with .dafr_builtin labels and op_dispatch.R:114-119 metadata (type_param='float'). `% Exp` / `% Sqrt` run and return results in R. Extra capability, not a missing feature, but it means a query that is an error in Julia silently succeeds in R - a divergence in the registered op surface.

divergences.name: Sum / arithmetic integer overflow semantics
divergences.julia_behavior: Sum casts the result to sum_type_for(eltype): Int8/Int16/Int32 -> Int32, UInt8/16/32 -> UInt32 (operations.jl:121-154, 1156). A column of Int32 whose true sum exceeds 2^31-1 wraps (two's-complement) into the Int32 result; sum over Int8 input accumulating past 2^31 wraps in the Int32 sum type.
divergences.r_behavior: R sums in Float64 (sum(x) on integer-stored-as-double) and only casts at the end if `type=` is given. So `>- Sum` of a wide Int32 column gives the true (non-wrapped) value as a double in R, where Julia would return a wrapped Int32. With explicit `>- Sum type Int32` R routes through .check_inexact_int (operations.R:517-541) which RAISES InexactError for an out-of-range sum, whereas Julia silently wraps. Different result (R errors / R returns true value; Julia wraps).

divergences.name: Var / Std small-int and Float32 result precision
divergences.julia_behavior: Var/Std/VarN/StdN of a Float32 input return Float32 (float_type_for, operations.jl:1596-1598); of an Int* input return Float32 (small int) or Float64 (Int64). The Float32 cast truncates the variance/std to single precision.
divergences.r_behavior: R computes .var_uncorrected in Float64 and returns Float64 unless `type=` given (operations.R:875-884). Value differs from Julia in the low mantissa bits whenever the input column was Float32-typed.

Compare get_query result to ~7 significant digits. Julia Mean = Float32(mean) (single precision); R = full Float64. Expect divergence around the 7th-8th significant digit.

probes.targets_finding: Default narrowing result-type rules / Var-Std Float32 precision

probes.query_or_snippet: Int32 vector 'big' = fill(2_000_000_000, 3) (sum = 6e9 > 2^31-1). Query '/ cell : big >> Sum type Int32'. Julia: silently returns a wrapped negative Int32. R (.cast_to_type -> .check_inexact_int): raises 'InexactError: Int32(6e+09)'.
probes.expects: Julia returns a (wrapped) finite Int32; R raises InexactError. Crash-vs-silent mismatch.

probes.description: Convert to UInt64 of a value in (2^53, 2^64): Julia exact, R loses precision via bit64::integer64 (signed) / double bound.

Julia stores exact UInt64; R routes to bit64::as.integer64 which is signed 64-bit and cannot hold > 2^63-1, and the .INT_TYPE_RANGES UInt64 upper bound is a double approximation.

If 'f' is Float32-typed: Julia rounds to Int32 -> InexactError/wrap at 3e9; if Float64-typed: Julia -> Int64 (fine). R always defaults to Int64 (operations.R:285-299) -> fine regardless. probes.description: Median / Quantile on a sparse (dgCMatrix) column with many implicit zeros and even count: confirm R's kernel_quantile_csc tie/interpolation matches Julia's TanayLabUtilities sparse_quantile (unverifiable by source read).

confirmed_parity: All 14 reductions exist in R with matching names and the correct type-param policy: Sum/Count accept any number type; Mean/Median/Var/Std/VarN/StdN/GeoMean/Quantile accept float-only; Min/Max/Mode accept no `type` (op_dispatch.R:39-120 .OP_META mirrors operations.jl reduction_result_type/parse_*_type_value).

All 7 documented eltwise ops exist: Abs, Clamp, Convert, Fraction, Log, Round, Significant, with matching parameter names and defaults (Abs/Round/Convert `type`; Clamp min/max; Log base(default e)/eps(default 0)/type; Fraction `type`; Significant high/low(default high)).

Parameter defaults match: Log base default e and eps default 0; Significant low defaults to high; Clamp min default -Inf, max default Inf; GeoMean/VarN/StdN eps default 0; Quantile p has no default (required, errors if missing) - all match Julia.

Required-parameter errors match Julia wording: Convert with no type -> 'missing required parameter: type'; Significant no high -> 'missing required parameter: high'; Quantile no p -> 'missing required parameter: p' (operations.R) mirror parse_parameter_value's missing=missing template (operations.jl:368-378).

Type-tag validation parity: invalid `type=` raises 'invalid value: ".."\nvalue must be: a number type / a float type\n...' matching error_invalid_parameter_value (operations.jl:198-213); float-only ops reject Int/UInt type tags; lowercase aliases (float32/int8/...) accepted same as cased (DTYPE_BY_NAME parity, operations.R:436-468).

Unknown-parameter and undeclared-param errors match: 'the parameter: X does not exist for the operation: Y'; Round rejects `digits` and Clamp rejects `low`/`high` in the query DSL (op_dispatch.R:88-104).

Named constants e and pi accepted as numeric parameters (Log base e, Significant high pi, eps pi) via parse_number_value's e/pi special-case (operations.jl:328-332) mirrored in .resolve_named_numeric (operations.R:625-633).

NaN/Inf propagation parity: Log/Significant/Fraction/Var/Std/Median/Mean propagate NaN to output rather than erroring (operations.R guards with isTRUE() around comparisons; .var_uncorrected returns NaN not NA when input has NaN); Median preserves NaN where stats::median would coerce to NA (operations.R:931-942).
DomainError parity for log of negative input in Log and GeoMean: 'DomainError with <min>:\nlog was called with a negative real argument'; log(0) -> -Inf permitted (operations.R:262-271, 971-976).

Fraction parity: per-column (matrix) or whole-vector fraction; zero-sum column/vector -> zeros; scalar input -> 'applying Fraction eltwise operation to a scalar' error; sparse dgCMatrix preserved (operations.R:664-712 vs operations.jl:706-740).

Mode supports strings/factors with first-appearance-max-count tie-break matching StatsBase.mode and is wired through both scalar and grouped paths; Count supports strings and is used in grouped counting; both supports_strings ops (Mode, Count) flagged accepts_string_input=TRUE while all numeric ops reject String input with 'unsupported input type: String' (op_dispatch.R:170-184).
Uncorrected (population) variance/std: both use n (not n-1) divisor - R fast paths multiply matrixStats var by (n-1)/n and the kernels use corrected=false matching operations.jl:1581 corrected=false.

Significant value semantics match: all-below-high column -> all zeros; otherwise zero entries below low; low==high uses the single mask (operations.R:714-729 .significant_vec vs operations.jl:988-1003 significant!).
Convert rejects String/factor input ('unsupported input type: String') and requires an explicit type, matching Julia Convert having no default type (operations.jl:628-637).

register_query_operation / register_eltwise / register_reduction / get_eltwise / get_reduction / registered_* provide the custom-op registry surface analogous to @query_operation + Registry, with conflicting-registration error wording mirrored (op_dispatch / operations.R:44-139).
notes:
Operations is one of the highest-parity subsystems for VALUES in the dominant Float64/double case: every documented Julia op exists in R, parameter names/defaults/required-ness and the error-message templates were ported byte-for-byte, and NaN/Inf/DomainError/empty edge cases were deliberately matched (the R code is littered with explicit 'Julia parity' guards). 

The one systematic, unavoidable divergence class is STORAGE/RESULT TYPE: Julia's float_type_for / sum_type_for / int_type_for / unsigned_type_for pick a narrowed default output type (Float32, Int32, UInt32, sized ints) whenever no explicit `type=` tag is given, and R has no Float32 / unsigned / sized-int storage so it stays Float64/double (mapping UInt*/small ints to 32-bit integer, Int64/UInt64 to bit64::integer64). For Float64/double inputs this is invisible. For Float32-typed stored data it is a genuine low-bit value difference (Julia truncates each reduction/eltwise result to single precision; R keeps double). The team already half-mitigated the downstream consequence with a Float32 round-trip inside .check_inexact_int (operations.R:509-541), which only fixes the 'Float32 result feeds an integer Convert' case, not direct value comparison. Whether OPS-01 actually fires depends on whether any test fixture stores genuine Float32 matrices/vectors and whether the harness compares below ~1e-7 relative tolerance.

Secondary divergences: Significant doesn't promote dense->sparse (values fine, class differs); Exp/Sqrt are R-only extra ops (a query that errors in Julia succeeds in R); Sum/Convert to a too-narrow integer type errors in R (InexactError) where Julia silently wraps (two's complement); UInt64 above 2^63 can't be faithfully stored in R's signed integer64.

I could NOT read TanayLabUtilities' sparse_quantile / sparse_median / sparse_var implementations (not present in the available source tree), so the exact sparse interpolation / tie-handling for Median/Quantile/Var on dgCMatrix columns is asserted-by-default-type-7 only - OPS-07 is the probe to confirm it. Dense Quantile/Median use stats::quantile/matrixStats type=7 which matches Julia Statistics default.

narrowed.name: || (IfMissing) bare-type token allowlist
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia consumes ANY following value token as the type via maybe_next_value_token, then validates it against DTYPE_BY_NAME (operations.jl:215-241, which includes the alias "auto" -> nothing). R's .parse_if_missing (query_parse.R:377-395) only consumes the next token as a type if it is in a HARDCODED allowlist {Bool,String,Int,Int8..Int64,UInt8..UInt64,Float32,Float64 + lowercase}. That allowlist OMITS "auto" (and "string"). So `. x || 0 auto` parses in Julia (type=nothing because DTYPE_BY_NAME["auto"]=nothing, value stays the raw string "0") but in R "auto" is not recognised as a type, falls through as the next operation token, and R errors `expected operator, got value 'auto'`. Also, for a non-type junk token like `|| 5 garbage` Julia consumes it as a type and errors with `garbage / a number type`, while R leaves it and errors with `expected operator, got value`.
narrowed.evidence: Julia: queries.jl:1053 maybe_next_value_token grabs any value token; queries.jl:1058-1065 then parse_number_type_value (operations.jl:254-266) validates against DTYPE_BY_NAME (operations.jl:240 has "auto"=>nothing). R: query_parse.R:377-395 hardcoded allowlist has no "auto"/"string"; .JULIA_TYPE_CANONICAL (operations.R:455-460) also lacks them.

divergences.name: Regex-pattern escaping after ~ / !~ (IsMatch/IsNotMatch)
divergences.julia_behavior: `~` and `!~` take EXACTLY ONE value token as the pattern (QUERY_OPERATIONS_DICT "~"=>(IsMatch,true) requires_operand=true -> next_value_token, queries.jl:1110). Regex metacharacters that are also query operators (^, [, ], etc.) MUST be backslash-escaped, e.g. `~ \^\[A-U\]` (Julia test queries.jl:820). An unescaped `~ ^HOX` ERRORS because `^` is an operator token, not a value (`expected: value`). Julia's canonical IsMatch form ALSO escapes the pattern: show() prints `escape_value(string(comparison_value))` (queries.jl:2430), so pattern ^MT- canonicalises to `~ \^MT\-`.
divergences.r_behavior: `.parse_match_cmp` (query_parse.R:422-445) GREEDILY collects ALL following tokens (operator and value alike) until a `]` token or end-of-input, then concatenates their .value with NO separator. So `~ ^HOX` is accepted as pattern `^HOX` (dafr's own tests rely on this: test-query-eval-masks.R:26,184 use unescaped `@ gene [ symbol ~ ^HOX ]`). Two consequences: (a) over-consumption - outside a `[...]` mask, `: type ~ ^X : other` swallows the trailing `: other` into the pattern (`^X:other`) because only `]` breaks the loop; (b) adjacent value tokens lose separating whitespace (paste collapse=""). R's IsMatch canonicaliser does NOT escape the pattern (query_ast.R:78 `paste0("~ ", n$pattern)`), so R canonical strings with regex metachars are not Julia-parseable.
divergences.evidence: Julia single-operand: queries.jl:2393-2395 (IsMatch struct), 2828 ("~"=>(IsMatch,true)), 1109-1110 (requires_operand->next_value_token). Julia escapes canonical: queries.jl:2430. Julia tests escape: test/queries.jl:820,824 `\^\[A-U\]`. R greedy collect: query_parse.R:422-445. R unescaped tests: test-query-eval-masks.R:26,184. R canonical unescaped: query_ast.R:78-79.

divergences.name: Operation-parameter canonical form: colon vs space
divergences.julia_behavior: Operation (eltwise/reduction) named parameters are serialised SPACE-separated with NO colon: show_computation_operation prints `field_name SPACE field_value` (queries.jl:1959-1974). Canonical examples from Julia tests: `% Clamp min 1 max 0`, `% Log base 2`, `>| Quantile p -0.5`, `% Log base 2 eps 1 type Float32` (test/operations.jl:87,232-233,421). Julia's parser also only accepts the space form: parse_operation_parameters (queries.jl:1168-1187) breaks the param loop on ANY operator token, and `:` tokenises as the LookupVector operator - so a colon between key and value terminates parameter parsing.
divergences.r_behavior: dafr canonicalises params with a COLON: `.canonicalise_reduction`/`.canonicalise_eltwise` emit `<k>: <value>` (query_ast.R:330,347). Tests assert this: `>> Quantile p: 0.5`, `% Clamp ...`, `>| Quantile p: 0.5` (test-builders-reductions.R:196,202,403). dafr's parser makes the `:` OPTIONAL (.parse_op_params query_parse.R:269-275) so it accepts BOTH the Julia space form and its own colon form on input. Net: dafr accepts Julia queries on input, but its canonical OUTPUT (`% Clamp min: 1 max: 0`) is NOT parseable by Julia (Julia breaks at `:`, treats `:` as LookupVector). The AST param values are equal but canonical strings diverge, breaking cross-engine round-trip. (Note: slice-10a-exit.md:71-72 claims .canonicalise_eltwise was rewritten to space form, but the current code still emits colons - the note is stale or was reverted.)
divergences.evidence: Julia space form: queries.jl:1959-1974 (no colon printed); test/operations.jl:87,232-233,421. Julia parser breaks on operator/colon: queries.jl:1174-1177. R colon canonical: query_ast.R:330,347; tests test-builders-reductions.R:196,202,403. R optional-colon parse: query_parse.R:269-275. Stale note: dev/notes/slice-10a-exit.md:69-72.

divergences.name: Double-quoted "..." string value tokens (R-only extension)
divergences.julia_behavior: tokens.jl has NO double-quote string-literal support. `"` is not in is_value_char (tokens.jl:102-110) and not in the operator regex, so a bare `"` in a query is reported as `unexpected character: '"'`. Values with special chars must use backslash escaping or `''` for empty.
divergences.r_behavior: .scan_value (query_tokens.R:71-90) treats a leading `"` as the start of a quoted string, consuming everything (including spaces and operator chars) up to the closing `"`, with `\X` escapes inside, and errors `unterminated quoted value` if unclosed. So `: "foo bar"` yields a single value token `foo bar` (with an embedded space) in R, while Julia rejects it. R is a strict input superset here. unescape_value also keeps a legacy double-quote branch (query_ast.R:157-159). escape_value itself does NOT emit quotes (uses backslash, query_ast.R:126-129), so this only affects input acceptance, not canonical output.
divergences.evidence: Julia no quote support: tokens.jl:102-110 (is_value_char), tokens.jl:84,91 (VALUE_REGEX has no `"`), tokens.jl:263-268 (unexpected character). R quote handling: query_tokens.R:71-90; legacy unescape: query_ast.R:157-159.

divergences.name: Tokenizer/parse error message format
divergences.julia_behavior:
Errors use a distinctive multi-line format with the squashed query and a caret marker, e.g. `unexpected character: 'X'
in: <query>
at:    ▲` (tokens.jl:263-268) and `error_at_token` (tokens.jl:274-288) builds `<message>
in: <query>
at: <indent>▲▲▲` pointing at the offending token. Token-shortfall errors say `expected: value` / `expected: operator` (queries.jl:1191,1198,1200).
divergences.r_behavior: R errors are single-line and worded differently: `unexpected character 'X' at position N in query 'Q'` (query_tokens.R:54-57), `expected operator, got value 'X' at position N in query 'Q'` (query_parse.R:128-131), `expected axis name after '@' at position N ...` (query_parse.R:148). Some paths DO match Julia wording (`.parse_cmp` emits bare `expected: value`, query_parse.R:233), so the wording is inconsistent across R parse paths. No `in:/at:/▲` caret diagnostic is produced.
divergences.evidence: Julia format: tokens.jl:263-268, tokens.jl:274-288, queries.jl:1191-1202. R format: query_tokens.R:54-57,86-89; query_parse.R:122-131,148-151,233. The jl-parity tests use loose regexps so they pass despite the wording gap (test-queries-jl-parity.R:54,58,62).

probes.description: `auto` bare-type token in IfMissing: valid in Julia, rejected by R.

confirmed_parity: Operator tokenizer regex is byte-for-byte identical: Julia QUERY_OPERATIONS_REGEX (queries.jl:2791) == R .QUERY_OP_REGEX (query_tokens.R:7) after accounting for R string-literal backslash doubling.

All 29 operator tokens in Julia's QUERY_OPERATIONS_DICT (queries.jl:2795-2829) have a corresponding R parser branch in .parse_next (query_parse.R:90-121): ? @ . : :: [ ] & | ^ < <= = != > >= ~ !~ @- @| >| >> >- / -/ |/ * % || ?? =@, plus the inline `!` NotModifier and `[ !`/`& !`/`| !`/`^ !` negated-mask forms.

escape_value / unescape_value now use Julia's backslash convention (query_ast.R:117-165), matching tokens.jl escape_value/unescape_value (tokens.jl:52-72): special chars get `\X`, `''` is the canonical empty-string token, round-trip invariant holds (test-tokens-jl-parity.R:46-54,97-105).
Empty-string value token `''` and the escape `\'\'` to write a literal two-quote string are handled identically (query_tokens.R:33-39 and .scan_value; matches tokens.jl:208-212).

Latin-1 supplement chars (0x80-0xFF, e.g. é ñ ü) are rejected as unexpected characters in bare value tokens; only codepoints > 0xFF (CJK/emoji) pass through unescaped - R .scan_value [^\x00-\xFF] (query_tokens.R:111) matches Julia VALUE_REGEX (tokens.jl:91), which also rejects raw Latin-1 because encode_expression does not encode unescaped non-ASCII (tokens.jl:121).

Backslash escaping of operator chars inside value tokens works the same: `ACTG\:Plate1` -> value `ACTG:Plate1` (R .scan_value `\\.` branch, query_tokens.R:111,125; Julia via encode/decode_expression).
Comment syntax `# ... <eol>` and whitespace squashing are equivalent (R query_tokens.R:16-29 vs Julia SPACE_REGEX tokens.jl:81).
Negative-number and decimal value tokens (`-0.5`, `+1.2e3`-style runs of [0-9a-zA-Z_.+-]) tokenise as single value tokens in both; bare `-`/`+`/`.` are value chars, not operators, in both regexes.

Optional-operand operators (?? IfNot, =@ AsAxis, . : :: bare lookups) and required-operand operators are dispatched with matching arity in R (.parse_if_not, .parse_as_axis, .parse_lookup) vs Julia (requires_operand false/true in QUERY_OPERATIONS_DICT).

Repeated-parameter and unknown-parameter detection at parse time match Julia wording: `repeated parameter: <k> for the operation: <op>` and `the parameter: <k> / does not exist for the operation: <op>` (R query_parse.R:277-282,309-313 vs Julia queries.jl:1143-1160).
Both public exports of tokens.jl (escape_value, unescape_value) are present in dafr NAMESPACE (lines 143,214); the tokenize/parse internals are private in both implementations.
notes:
Scope: I audited the tokenizer + parser surface (tokens.jl + queries.jl operator dict/regex/parse_query against R query_tokens.R, query_parse.R, query_ast.R). The operator-set and escaping core are at genuine parity - this subsystem is in good shape. The findings are concentrated in three real behavioral divergences plus two cosmetic ones:

1. STRONGEST: `~`/`!~` regex-pattern handling. dafr greedily collects multiple tokens until `]` (query_parse.R:422-445) and does NOT escape the pattern in canonical output (query_ast.R:78), while Julia takes exactly one value token requiring metachars to be backslash-escaped and escapes them in canonical output (queries.jl:2430). dafr's own tests rely on the unescaped form (`~ ^HOX`), which Julia rejects. This also causes over-consumption of trailing operations outside a `[...]` mask. This is the highest-value probe target.

2. Operation-parameter canonical form: dafr emits colon `min: 1` (query_ast.R:330,347; asserted by tests), Julia emits space `min 1` (queries.jl:1959-1974). dafr ACCEPTS both on input (optional `:`), so it is input-compatible with Julia, but its canonical OUTPUT is not Julia-parseable. Note slice-10a-exit.md:71-72 claims this was fixed to space form - that note is stale; current code still emits colons.

3. `|| <default> auto` (and arbitrary junk type tokens): Julia consumes any following value token as the type then validates (DTYPE_BY_NAME includes "auto"); R uses a hardcoded type allowlist that omits "auto"/"string", so it diverges in both accept/reject and error wording.

Things the existing parity docs likely cover and I did NOT flag as gaps: escape/unescape backslash convention (now correct), Latin-1 rejection (correct), `''` empty token, operator regex. The double-quote `"..."` value extension and error-message format are real but lower-severity.

All probes are designed to run through both engines' parse_query/get_query; P5 is a control to confirm the param divergence is output-only. I could not execute R or Julia (read-only mandate), so the expected behaviors are derived from source reading and the committed test fixtures (which corroborate the colon-form and unescaped-regex forms on the R side, and the space-form/escaped-regex forms on the Julia side)."

missing_in_r.name: full_vector_query
missing_in_r.detail: Julia exports full_vector_query(axis_query, vector_query, vector_name) (queries.jl:5711) and the internal patch_query that splices an `@ __axis__` operator with the axis sub-query. No R equivalent is exported or defined (grep across R/ finds nothing). The `__axis__` placeholder is handled only in the view layer via a literal gsub('__axis__', base_axis, query) at view_daf.R:570 (string substitution, not Query-object splicing), and does NOT feed the get_dataframe/frame column path. So programmatic composition of an axis query with a vector-suffix query is not a first-class function.

missing_in_r.name: q"..." / @q_str macro
missing_in_r.detail: Julia exports the @q_str string macro (queries.jl:11, 1285) so `q"..."` parses a raw query literal. R has no macro system; there is no q_str() helper either. Low impact (R users call parse_query()/get_query() directly), but it is part of the documented public surface.

missing_in_r.name: get_frame name-prefix default + axis-query forms
missing_in_r.detail: Julia get_frame(daf, axis, columns=nothing) with columns omitted returns ALL vector properties sorted alphabetically AND inserts a leading "name" column holding the axis-entry strings (queries.jl:5657-5660: `insert!(columns, 1, "name")`). R's get_dataframe/get_dataframe_query default returns the axis vectors (format_vectors_set order) with axis entries only as data.frame rownames, no explicit `name` column. Also Julia accepts an arbitrary axis Query (e.g. q"@ cell [ age > 1 ]") and validates is_axis_query; R get_dataframe takes a bare axis name string and builds `@ <axis>` itself (get_dataframe_query takes the query). This `name` default-column gap is exactly the open API1 item in dev/notes/2026-05-03-queries-jl-parity-divergences.md.

narrowed.name: get_dataframe_query column-query suffix (full_vector_query semantics)

narrowed.name: CountBy result element type
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia types the count matrix as the smallest UNSIGNED int that holds n_values: UInt8/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64 (queries.jl:4560-4565 count_by_values). R builds the matrix via base::table() which yields R `integer` (Int32-equivalent), and the count-variants test pins values as `1L`. Functionally identical for in-memory use, but the stored dtype differs (Int32 vs UInt8/16/...), which matters if the count result is written back into a daf or compared by storage type.
narrowed.evidence: queries.jl:4560-4579 (matrix_type loop picks UInt8..UInt64); R/query_eval.R:4141-4176 .finalize_pending_count uses as.matrix(table(...)) -> integer; tests/testthat/test-query-count-variants.R asserts 1L

divergences.name: GroupBy / CountBy result ordering is locale-dependent (not bytewise)
divergences.julia_behavior: Group/count axis labels are ordered by sort!(unique(values)) which for Vector{String} is BYTEWISE: uppercase before lowercase, ASCII before non-ASCII (e.g. 'Z' < 'b', 'B1' < 'a1'). queries.jl:3940, 4523, 4706, 4795.
divergences.r_behavior: R uses factor(labels, levels = sort(unique(labels))) (query_eval.R:3057) and table()/factor() for counts (query_eval.R:4156-4168). R's sort() on character vectors honours LC_COLLATE, so under the default en_US.UTF-8 locale it produces DICTIONARY order ('b' < 'Z'). The comparator path was fixed for this via .cmp_ordering forcing C locale (query_eval.R:1807), but the GroupBy/CountBy sort was NOT. Result vectors/matrices come back with rows/cols in a different order (and thus different name->value association after positional use) than Julia whenever group labels mix case or include non-ASCII.
divergences.evidence: R/query_eval.R:3056-3060 (factor + sort(unique)), 4156-4168 (table); Julia sort! bytewise at queries.jl:3940,4523

divergences.name: Canonical reduction/eltwise parameter string uses ':' separator
divergences.julia_behavior: Base.show for a reduction/eltwise prints `>> Sum type Int64` and `% Clamp min 40 max 60` - parameter name and value SPACE-separated, no colon (show_computation_operation, queries.jl:1948-1977).
divergences.r_behavior: .canonicalise_reduction / .canonicalise_eltwise emit `>> Sum type: Int64` and `% Clamp min: 40 max: 60` - a colon after each param key (query_ast.R:322-354). The R parser accepts the optional colon so both forms parse, but canonical_query() output (and DafrQuery@canonical / cache keys) diverges character-for-character from Julia's string(query). Cross-implementation cache-key/string-roundtrip comparisons will mismatch.
divergences.evidence: R/query_ast.R:330-336 emits 'k: v'; Julia queries.jl:1962-1964 prints field name then ' ' then value (no colon); confirmed in tests/testthat/test-query-parse.R:103 ('>| Sum type: Int64')

divergences.name: Introspection (is_axis_query / query_axis_name / query_result_dimensions) is pure-AST, not data-validated
divergences.julia_behavior: is_axis_query, query_axis_name, query_result_dimensions run the full query state machine (with_for=:is_axis / :result_dimensions / :axis_name) and ERROR (`invalid query`, assertion) on syntactically malformed or non-terminal queries (queries.jl:1845-1897). is_axis_query also requires the final state be a VectorState whose property_name=='name' and property_axis_name==entries_axis_name.
divergences.r_behavior: All three are static AST walks (queries.R:290-359). query_result_dimensions('@ cell @ gene') returns 1L instead of erroring; is_axis_query() only checks the last node op is Axis/EndMask (queries.R:296) so it can mis-classify; query_axis_name counts outer-scope Axis nodes and returns NA on 0/2+ rather than asserting. This is the documented-but-open B8/B9 leniency. Wrong/over-lenient answers on malformed introspection input rather than an error.
divergences.evidence: R/queries.R:290-359 (pure AST); Julia queries.jl:1845-1897 runs the state machine; dev/notes/2026-05-03-queries-jl-parity-divergences.md B8/B9

notes: The R query subsystem is a full re-architecture (AST + recursive .apply_node dispatcher in query_eval.R), NOT a port of Julia's PHRASES stack machine, but it covers essentially the entire documented query grammar. Most items the prior parity note (dev/notes/2026-05-03-queries-jl-parity-divergences.md) listed as OPEN (E3-E11, API1 column-query, E5/E6/E7/E8/E9) are now CLOSED in 0.4.4 - I verified the implementations in query_eval.R and the parity test now carries only 2 skips (both E11/T-class kernel type-strictness). Genuinely-still-divergent items I found: (1) GroupBy/CountBy result ORDERING is locale-dependent because the C-locale fix applied to comparators (.cmp_ordering) was never propagated to the group/count factor-sort - this is a silent-wrong-answer for mixed-case/non-ASCII labels and is NOT in the note; (2) CountBy result dtype is Int32 vs Julia UInt8/16/32/64; (3) canonical param-string uses 'type: V' colon vs Julia 'type V'; (4) introspection helpers are pure-AST/over-lenient (open B8/B9); (5) full_vector_query/patch_query/@q_str not exported; (6) get_frame default 'name' column not emitted (open API1). The ordering divergence (#1) is the highest-value finding because it produces wrong answers silently. The E11 kernel type-strictness (Float64-default reduction vs Int result -> Julia InexactError) remains genuinely out of scope for R. Julia public-surface count = 47 exported names from queries.jl:11-58 (operators+functions+types); plus get_frame/FrameColumn/FrameColumns/full_vector_query are part of the documented Functions surface in queries.md.

missing_in_r.name: format_get_empty_dense_vector! / format_get_empty_sparse_vector! / format_get_empty_dense_matrix! / format_get_empty_sparse_matrix!
missing_in_r.julia_evidence: formats.jl:435-507 (vectors) and 633-710 (matrices) declare four empty-buffer creation generics; public wrappers in writers.jl:412/445/849/993 (get_empty_dense_vector!, etc.). They return a caller-fillable buffer + CacheGroup, enabling streaming/in-place construction of large dense/sparse properties without first materializing the whole array.
missing_in_r.detail: R format_api.R defines NO format_get_empty_* generic and no public empty_dense_vector/empty_sparse_vector/empty_dense_matrix/empty_sparse_matrix builder. This is already acknowledged internally as divergence 'C3' (test-data-jl-parity.R:209,266; test-chains-jl-parity.R:521-588; test-contracts-access-jl-parity.R:720-732 all skip with 'dafr does not have the empty_*/builder API'). Callers must instead pre-allocate the full array and use set_vector/set_matrix, losing the zero-copy streaming-fill path. This is a whole missing operation family in the formats-interface contract, not just a missing option.

missing_in_r.name: format_filled_empty_dense_vector! / format_filled_empty_sparse_vector! / format_filled_empty_dense_matrix! / format_filled_empty_sparse_matrix!
missing_in_r.julia_evidence: formats.jl:476-483, 520-527, 676-684, 724-732 define the four 'filled' finalization hooks (default no-op) that backends override to flush metadata / patch chunk checksums after the caller fills a buffer returned by format_get_empty_*.
missing_in_r.detail: Absent in R (grep over R/ and NAMESPACE finds none). This is the natural consequence of the missing empty-buffer builders above; with no builder there is no fill-finalize lifecycle. Same C3 root cause.

missing_in_r.name: format_is_packed_vector / format_is_packed_matrix
missing_in_r.julia_evidence: formats.jl:575-593 (vector) and 805-824 (matrix): generics returning whether a property is stored in the packed (chunked+compressed) on-disk encoding; used by relayout/axis-reorder to preserve the source's encoding when rebuilding a property in place.
missing_in_r.detail: R has NO format_is_packed_vector / format_is_packed_matrix generic (grep finds none in R/ or NAMESPACE). FilesDaf has only a private read-side helper .files_is_packed(desc) (files_daf_read.R:253 etc.) that decodes packed v1.1 stores, but there is no generic in the formats-interface and no caller can ask 'is this property packed?'. Because R cannot rebuild a property while preserving packed encoding (no packed-write path exists either - see narrowed item), relayout/reorder in R always rewrites flat.

missing_in_r.name: format_description_footer
missing_in_r.julia_evidence: formats.jl:838-855: format_description_footer(format, indent, lines; cache, deep, tensors) lets a backend emit extra footer lines and (when deep) recurse into nested data sets; documented in formats.md:24-27.
missing_in_r.detail: R defines format_description_header (format_api.R:84-90) but NOT format_description_footer (grep over R/ and NAMESPACE finds none). The 'deep' nested-dataset description recursion and per-backend footer emission have no R hook. Severity is cosmetic in terms of data correctness but it is a genuinely missing generic in the documented description contract.

narrowed.name: format_set_vector! / format_set_matrix! / format_relayout_matrix! (is_packed parameter)
narrowed.what_is_missing: The resolved is_packed::Bool argument. Julia threads packed encoding through the entire write path: format_set_vector! (formats.jl:413-432), format_set_matrix! (610-630), and format_relayout_matrix! (734-754) all take is_packed::Bool; the public set_vector!/set_matrix!/relayout_matrix! expose packed::Maybe{Bool}=nothing (writers.jl:288,386,693,1100) resolved against a per-daf packed_default via resolve_packed (writers.jl:42,372,800,804). R's format_set_vector/format_set_matrix/format_relayout_matrix generics (format_api.R:26,39-54) have NO packed argument; public set_vector/set_matrix/relayout_matrix (writers.R:102,162,242) expose no packed keyword; there is no packed_default or resolve_packed anywhere in R (grep finds none). FilesDaf write path (files_daf_write.R) always writes the flat encoding (no packed/chunk/blosc write branch). Net: R can READ packed v1.1 stores but cannot WRITE packed, and offers no per-write or per-daf knob to request it.

narrowed.name: format_get_vector / format_get_matrix (opaque backing slot)
narrowed.what_is_missing: The third tuple element: an opaque 'backing' object kept alive for the returned array's lifetime to support zero-copy unsafe_wrap aliasing (e.g. HttpDaf). Julia format_get_vector returns Tuple{StorageVector, Any, CacheGroup} (formats.jl:554-572) and format_get_matrix returns Tuple{StorageMatrix, Any, CacheGroup} (787-802); the cache stores the pair as Tuple{NamedArray, Any} so the buffer stays reachable. R's getters return a 2-field list(value=, cache_group=) only (.cache_group_value, cache_group.R:50-52); no backing slot. R's HttpDaf returns fully-materialized R objects (http_format.R), so there is no dangling-on-empty_cache hazard - but the contract shape differs and any future zero-copy backend has no place to anchor the backing buffer.

narrowed.name: format_has_axis (for_change kwarg)
narrowed.what_is_missing: The for_change::Bool keyword (Julia formats.jl:339-345) signalling the check precedes an add/delete. R's format_has_axis generic (format_api.R:15) has no for_change parameter. Behaviorally inert (it is only an assertion/optimization hint in Julia's assert_valid_cache and add/delete guards), so no wrong-answer impact - flagged for signature completeness only.

divergences.name: format_axis_vector renamed to format_axis_array + extra format_axis_dict generic
divergences.julia_behavior: Julia exposes ONE axis-entries backend generic, format_axis_vector (formats.jl:381-391), returning Tuple{AbstractVector{<:AbstractString}, CacheGroup}. The axis->index dictionary is NOT a backend responsibility; it is derived internally by get_axis_dict_through_cache (formats.jl:1070-1083) from the axis vector via a NamedArray, then cached.
divergences.r_behavior: R renames the generic to format_axis_array (format_api.R:19) returning list(value=entries, cache_group=) - same content, different name. R additionally PROMOTES the axis dict to its own backend generic format_axis_dict (format_api.R:21), implemented per-backend (memory_daf.R:138, files_daf_read.R:170, zarr_format.R:433, http_format.R:232, etc.) and dispatched through readers.R:177. This is an architectural divergence: R makes backends own dict construction; Julia derives it centrally. Functionally equivalent results (both return axis->1-based index), but the interface surface differs (extra generic in R, renamed generic).

divergences.name: Lock-protocol generics not ported (end_data_write_lock / begin_data_*_lock / with_*_lock / has_data_*_lock)
divergences.julia_behavior: formats.jl exports end_data_write_lock (line 40) and defines a full read/write lock protocol (begin_data_read_lock 1254, end_data_read_lock 1264, begin/end_data_write_lock 1310-1328, with_*_lock helpers, has_data_read/write_lock 1306/1339) over an ExtendedReadWriteLock, supporting concurrent multi-threaded access with cache consistency.
divergences.r_behavior: R ports none of these (grep finds no end_data_write_lock/begin_data_write_lock in R/). R is single-threaded; the concurrency contract is intentionally dropped. No wrong-answer impact under R's single-threaded model, but any documented thread-safety guarantee of the formats interface is absent. Flagged as architectural divergence.

divergences.name: format_delete_matrix! documented return type
divergences.julia_behavior: formats.jl:757-771 docstring declares format_delete_matrix! ...::StorageMatrix (returns a matrix). This appears to be a doc typo (delete should return Nothing like format_delete_vector!/format_delete_scalar!), but it is what the published contract states.
divergences.r_behavior: R format_delete_matrix returns invisible() (consistent with delete_vector/delete_scalar). If a caller relied on the Julia-documented StorageMatrix return, R would diverge; in practice the Julia source itself almost certainly returns nothing, so this is a documentation discrepancy not a behavioral one. Low confidence it matters.

probes.description: Request packed on-disk encoding on a write. Julia accepts a packed keyword on set_matrix!; R has no such parameter and cannot produce a packed property.

For FilesDaf: files_daf(path,"w"); set_matrix!(...; packed=true) writes chunked+compressed payload. ||| R: d<-memory_daf(); add_axis(d,"r",c("a","b")); add_axis(d,"c",c("x","y")); set_matrix(d,"r","c","m",matrix(c(1,3,2,4),2,2), packed=TRUE)  # ERROR: unused argument (packed = TRUE). And FilesDaf always writes the flat encoding regardless.
probes.expects: Julia: write succeeds; for FilesDaf the on-disk property carries packed/chunked encoding (format_is_packed_matrix==true). R: set_matrix errors on the unknown 'packed' argument; even via the supported signature the FilesDaf payload is always flat (.files_is_packed(desc)==FALSE).

probes.description: Streaming/in-place construction of a large sparse vector via the empty-buffer builder.

probes.description: Deep description footer recursion / per-backend footer lines.

probes.description: Confirm relayout does not preserve packed encoding in R (because is_packed introspection + packed write are both missing).
probes.query_or_snippet: Setup a FilesDaf v1.1 store with a PACKED matrix m[r,c], then relayout_matrix to (c,r). Julia: format_relayout_matrix! receives is_packed resolved from the source via format_is_packed_matrix (writers.jl:1114-1159 — flipped copy mirrors source encoding), so the flipped (c,r) copy is also packed. R: relayout_matrix(d,"r","c","m") reads the packed source but the FilesDaf write path (files_daf_write.R) emits only flat encoding for the flipped copy.
probes.expects: Julia: flipped matrix on disk is packed (matches source). R: flipped matrix on disk is flat even when the source was packed — silent encoding downgrade on relayout/reorder.

confirmed_parity: Scalar generics: format_has_scalar, format_get_scalar, format_set_scalar(!), format_delete_scalar(!), format_scalars_set all present with matching arg order; R get returns list(value, cache_group) mirroring Julia Tuple{StorageScalar, CacheGroup} (memory_daf.R:61-79, format_api.R:8-12).

Axis generics: format_has_axis, format_add_axis(!), format_delete_axis(!), format_axes_set, format_axis_length present and equivalent. format_axis_vector is present under the renamed name format_axis_array (same return content).

Vector generics: format_has_vector, format_get_vector, format_set_vector(!), format_delete_vector(!), format_vectors_set present; R get attaches axis names via .attach_vector_axis_names (memory_daf.R:251-255) honoring the named-vector contract.

Matrix generics: format_has_matrix, format_get_matrix, format_set_matrix(!), format_delete_matrix(!), format_matrices_set, format_relayout_matrix(!) present; R get attaches dimnames via .attach_matrix_axis_dimnames (memory_daf.R:344-348) honoring the dimnames contract. CSC/column-major canonical layout matches Julia.

CacheGroup enum: all three values ported as constants MEMORY_DATA/MAPPED_DATA/QUERY_DATA (cache_group.R:36-44) mapping Julia MemoryData/MappedData/QueryData; every format_get_* returns a cache_group, matching the per-item CacheGroup contract.

empty_cache: present (cache.R:40) with clear/keep keyword semantics mirroring Julia empty_cache! (formats.jl:1421); the 'both clear and keep is an error' invariant is preserved by the underlying tier logic.
format_description_header: present (format_api.R:84-90) with default 'type: <ClassName>' line and per-format overrides, matching Julia formats.jl:826-836.

Names/dimnames preservation: R's read getters reliably attach axis entry names to vectors and row/col dimnames to matrices through .attach_* helpers, satisfying the named-array contract that the FOCUS specifically asked about.
notes: Bottom line: the everyday read/write generic surface (has/get/set/delete/names for scalar/axis/vector/matrix + relayout) is at parity in name set, arg order, and the named-vector/dimnames return contract. The real gaps are all clustered around two Julia subsystems that R never ported: (1) the empty-buffer streaming-construction lifecycle (format_get_empty_*! / format_filled_empty_*!) — already self-acknowledged as divergence 'C3' in dafr's own skipped tests; and (2) the packed (chunked+compressed) on-disk ENCODING-WRITE path — format_set_*!/format_relayout_matrix! lack the is_packed parameter, format_is_packed_vector/matrix generics are absent, and there is no packed_default/resolve_packed. dafr can READ packed v1.1 stores (private .files_is_packed) but cannot WRITE them and silently downgrades packed properties to flat on relayout/reorder (probe FMT-P4 — this is the one with silent-data-shape consequences worth verifying, severity semantic-edge not wrong-answer since values are preserved, only encoding/size differs). Smaller: missing format_description_footer (no deep-nested footer recursion), no opaque 'backing' slot in get_vector/get_matrix (harmless under R's eager-copy backends), and the lock-protocol generics are intentionally dropped (single-threaded R). The format_axis_dict generic is an R-only addition (Julia derives the dict centrally) — extra surface, not a gap. I did not run R or Julia; all evidence is from source reading. The packed-write gap (FMT-P1/FMT-P4) and the empty-buffer gap (FMT-P2) are the highest-value items for the differential harness; FMT-P1 will surface immediately as an R argument error vs Julia acceptance.

subsystem: memory-format (MemoryDaf: construction, storage generics, dtype/sparse/names preservation, overwrite, missing-error)

narrowed.name: set_vector (scalar broadcast)
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia set_vector!(daf, axis, name, vector::Union{StorageScalar,StorageVector}) accepts a SCALAR and fills the whole axis with it. At the memory layer format_set_vector! (memory_format.jl:173-190) materialises this: scalar==0 -> spzeros SparseVector, nonzero scalar -> dense fill. dafr set_vector (writers.R:102-114) routes through .validate_vector_value -> .require_axis_length, which REQUIRES length==axis_length; a length-1 scalar fails on any multi-entry axis. So `set_vector(d,'cell','x', 0)` errors in R but stores a full sparse-zero vector in Julia.
narrowed.evidence: R writers.R:102-114 + utils.R:56-86 (.require_axis_length); Julia writers.jl:320-360 + memory_format.jl:173-190

narrowed.name: set_matrix (scalar broadcast + relayout default)
narrowed.what_is_missing: (a) Julia set_matrix! accepts a StorageScalarBase scalar to broadcast-fill (scalar==0 -> sparse zeros matrix, else dense fill: memory_format.jl:267-293; writers.jl:745-789). R set_matrix (writers.R:162-181) requires a full dense/dgC/lgC matrix; a scalar is rejected by .validate_matrix_value (memory_daf.R:353-401). (b) DEFAULT relayout differs: Julia set_matrix! default relayout=true (writers.jl:753), R set_matrix default relayout=FALSE (writers.R:163, documented). Identical set_matrix(...) call leaves the flipped layout PRESENT in Julia, ABSENT in R.
narrowed.evidence: R writers.R:162-181, memory_daf.R:353-401; Julia writers.jl:745-789, memory_format.jl:267-293

A user wanting to downcast Float64->Float32 or Int64->Int32 at store time cannot.
narrowed.evidence: R writers.R:102,162 (no eltype arg); Julia writers.jl:325,357-359,751,785-787

narrowed.name: format_set_matrix value type acceptance (string / non-CSC sparse matrices)
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia format_set_matrix! accepts any StorageMatrix (AbstractMatrix{T} where T<:StorageScalar, incl. string matrices and any column-major dense). R .validate_matrix_value (memory_daf.R:353-361) only accepts base dense matrix() or dgCMatrix/lgCMatrix; a character matrix() is accepted by is.matrix but a sparse matrix of a different class (e.g. Matrix dgRMatrix / ngCMatrix) is rejected. String DENSE matrices pass is.matrix so are stored, but there is no sparse-string path (Julia also bars sparse strings, so parity there).

divergences.name: Sparse VECTOR representation not preserved on read (densified)
divergences.julia_behavior: A vector stored as a SparseVector is returned by get_vector as a NamedArray wrapping the SparseVector; base_array(get_vector(...)) issparse == true. format_get_vector returns the stored sparse object unchanged (memory_format.jl:248-255), and readers.jl:704-707 only wraps it in a read-only NamedArray.
divergences.r_behavior: format_get_vector -> .attach_vector_axis_names (utils.R:99-117) DENSIFIES any sparseVector via as.numeric (line 112-114) before attaching names, so get_vector ALWAYS returns a plain dense named numeric, even though the value was stored sparse (.validate_vector_value preserves the sparseVector in storage, utils.R:64-66). Confirmed by test-sparse-vector-parity.R:16 which must call as.numeric(get_vector(...)). NOTE: this is asymmetric - MATRICES preserve dgCMatrix/lgCMatrix on read (.attach_matrix_axis_dimnames keeps sparse, utils.R:122-138), only vectors are densified.
divergences.evidence: R utils.R:99-117 (densify) vs memory_daf.R:248-255; Julia memory_format.jl:248-255 + readers.jl:704-707

divergences.name: set_vector with scalar 0 stores SPARSE; R cannot express it
divergences.julia_behavior: format_set_vector!(...,0,...) stores spzeros(...) i.e. a SparseVector of structural zeros (memory_format.jl:183-184); the stored vector is sparse and stays sparse on read.
divergences.r_behavior: No scalar-broadcast path; even if a user constructs a full dense rep(0,n) the stored vector is dense, never sparse. There is no way to produce the sparse-zero in-memory representation Julia produces from set_vector!(...,0).
divergences.evidence: Julia memory_format.jl:183-184; R writers.R:102-114 (no scalar path)

divergences.name: MemoryDaf name is not uniquified
divergences.julia_behavior: MemoryDaf(; name='memory') calls unique_name(name) (memory_format.jl:62) which, via TanayLabUtilities unique_names.jl:78-98, returns the bare name on first use and 'name#2','name#3',... on subsequent uses (separator '#'); names containing '!' are forced unique-as-is. So two MemoryDaf() with the same name get distinct .name values.
divergences.r_behavior: memory_daf(name='memory') stores name verbatim (memory_daf.R:19-34); no unique_name. Two memory_daf() instances both report name 'memory'. Affects brief()/error-message identity and any code that relies on distinct daf names (e.g. chains/views display, debug logs).
divergences.evidence: Julia memory_format.jl:62 + TanayLabUtilities unique_names.jl:78-98; R memory_daf.R:19-34 (verbatim, no uniquifier anywhere in R/)

divergences.name: set_scalar value-type acceptance is broader in R
divergences.julia_behavior: format_set_scalar!/set_scalar! constrain value::StorageScalar = Union{Bool,Int8..64,UInt8..64,Float32/64, AbstractString} (storage_types.jl:48-102). Complex, Rational, Symbol, etc. are rejected at the type boundary.
divergences.r_behavior: .assert_scalar_value (utils.R:39-54) only checks atomic, length 1, non-NA. It therefore ACCEPTS R types Julia would reject - e.g. complex(1), raw, and (since no integer-width check) any double. NaN is accepted by both. So a complex or raw scalar is silently stored in R but cannot exist in a Julia MemoryDaf.
divergences.evidence: R utils.R:39-54; Julia storage_types.jl:48-102 + writers.jl:56,77

confirmed_parity: format_has_scalar / format_get_scalar / format_set_scalar / format_delete_scalar / format_scalars_set: equivalent semantics incl. overwrite check (R memory_daf.R:54-109 vs Julia memory_format.jl:80-112). R adds an explicit .require_no_scalar on !overwrite at the writer layer; Julia enforces it in writers.jl. Sorted key order matches (radix sort).

format_has_axis / format_add_axis / format_delete_axis / format_axes_set / format_axis_length / format_axis_array(vector): equivalent (memory_daf.R:113-198 vs memory_format.jl:114-166). Axis delete cascades to dependent vectors and both matrix row/col buckets in both. R additionally validates entries (no NA/empty/dup) at add - a stricter superset that matches Julia require checks at the writer layer.

format_has_vector / format_delete_vector / format_vectors_set / format_get_vector (length contract + names attach) for DENSE vectors: equivalent. Both attach axis entries as names on read (R .attach_vector_axis_names; Julia as_named_vector). Both error on missing vector.

format_has_matrix / format_set_matrix / format_get_matrix / format_delete_matrix / format_matrices_set: equivalent for dense and dgC/lgC sparse; dimnames validated against axis entries on set and re-attached on get; sparse matrix representation (dgCMatrix/lgCMatrix) is PRESERVED on read (unlike vectors). Missing matrix raises.

format_relayout_matrix: value-equivalent. Julia uses flipped() (rearranged transpose copy) stored at (cols,rows); R uses Matrix::t()/t() (memory_daf.R:432-444). Result element [i,j]->[j,i] matches; R has no row/col-major layout concept so the layout-bookkeeping difference is unobservable from R.

Reorder generics (format_replace_reorder / format_cleanup_reorder / format_reset_reorder + snapshot/restore): functionally equivalent crash-recovery rollback (memory_daf.R:448-573 vs memory_format.jl:488-595); R snapshots into internal$reorder_backup and restores on reset, mirroring MemoryReorderBackup.
is_leaf: equivalent (R .is_leaf_dispatch -> TRUE, memory_daf.R:576; Julia memory_format.jl:72-78).

Missing-error semantics: get on absent scalar/axis/vector/matrix raises in both; delete with must_exist=FALSE/TRUE matches Julia for_set/must_exist (memory_daf.R delete methods vs memory_format.jl delete!).
NaN scalar handling: both accept NaN as a valid value, reject true NA/missing (R utils.R:49-52 explicitly).
Sparse Float/Bool/Int vector VALUES round-trip correctly through memory storage (test-sparse-vector-parity.R) - only the returned representation (dense vs sparse) diverges, not the values.
notes:
Julia public surface for this subsystem = the MemoryDaf constructor (name, packed) plus the ~26 Formats.*/Reorder.* storage generics it implements (the format-API extension points that ARE the storage-generic contract). I counted 28 items. The four empty_*/filled_empty_*/get_empty_* clusters are a KNOWN deliberate deferral (dev/notes/2026-04-22-slice-10-wrapper-parity-analysis.md, section 8) - reported as missing for completeness, not as oversight.

HIGHEST-VALUE findings most likely missed by prior parity passes: (1) sparse VECTOR densification on read (utils.R:112-114 as.numeric) - asymmetric with matrices which DO preserve sparsity; the existing test-sparse-vector-parity.R masks this by always calling as.numeric() and only asserting values. (2) set_vector/set_matrix scalar-broadcast (Julia fills the axis, R errors), including the 0->sparse-zeros special case. (3) eltype= conversion arg absent in R. (4) set_matrix default relayout differs (Julia true, R FALSE) - documented in R but a genuine behavioral divergence for identical calls. (5) unique_name uniquification absent in R (cosmetic). (6) set_scalar over-accepts non-StorageScalar atomic types (complex/raw).

The core storage CRUD, names handling, overwrite, missing-error, and reorder paths are at genuine parity. The memory format is dtype-agnostic at the storage layer (stores whatever atomic/sparse R object it receives), so int-width/unsigned concerns live in the writers/storage-types layer, not here - the only memory-relevant dtype gap is the missing eltype conversion.

missing_in_r.name: root metadata.json consolidated index
missing_in_r.detail: Julia 0.3.0 writes a single root `metadata.json` (files_format.jl:1472 METADATA_JSON, :1594 metadata_json_append!, :1620 metadata_json_rebuild!, :1713 ensure_metadata_json!). It is a one-line JSON object mapping each property's relative path to its descriptor, e.g. `{"axes/cell":{"format":"axis","n_entries":4},"vectors/cell/sv":{"format":"sparse","nzind":{...},"nzval":{...}},...}` (confirmed verbatim in fixture tests/testthat/fixtures/jf11/metadata.json). R NEVER writes this file: it instead writes `metadata.zip` (R/files_metadata_zip.R:25 .metadata_zip_rebuild, :120 .metadata_zip_append) plus `axes/metadata.json` (R/files_metadata_zip.R:11 .write_axes_metadata, a JSON ARRAY of axis names). Both R mechanisms mirror an OBSOLETE Julia design - `grep metadata_zip|write_axes_metadata` over DataAxesFormats.jl/src returns ZERO hits. Consequence: (a) a dafr-written FilesDaf cannot be served to a Julia `HttpDaf` client, which fetches `<url>/metadata.json` and asserts it is a JSON object (http_format.jl:131-133) - it would 404/fail. (b) A Julia-written FilesDaf served over HTTP has `metadata.json` but no `metadata.zip`, so dafr's `http_daf` (R/http_format.R:62 downloads `<url>/metadata.zip`) fails. (c) dafr leaves a stray `axes/metadata.json` Julia never produces (harmless to Julia reads since format_axes_set filters `.txt`, but non-canonical). Local file reads still interoperate because Julia self-heals via ensure_metadata_json! tree-walk on writable opens and dafr reads per-property sidecars directly. This gap is NOT in the existing parity notes (only the unrelated Zarr root zarr.json consolidation is discussed in dev/notes/2026-06-09-zarr-v3-followups-kickoff.md).

missing_in_r.name: sparse string matrix read (.colptr/.rowval/.nztxt with nzval eltype String)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia's write_string_matrix (files_format.jl:932-1011) auto-sparsifies a string matrix when `sparse_size <= dense_size*0.75` (e.g. a matrix of mostly empty strings), emitting `.colptr`/`.rowval`/`.nztxt` + descriptor `{"format":"sparse","colptr":{...},"rowval":{...},"nzval":{"format":"dense","eltype":"String",...}}`. Julia's reader handles it (files_format.jl:1201-1226, eltype String arm reading `.nztxt`). R's `.files_get_matrix_sparse` (R/files_daf_read.R:587-644) has ONLY a Bool arm (line 609) and a numeric-default arm (line 626+); there is NO `eltype == "String"` arm (unlike the sparse VECTOR path which has one at R/files_daf_read.R:369). Parsing reaches the numeric branch, `.files_component_exists(mdir,name,"nzval",...)` is FALSE (Julia wrote `.nztxt`, not `.nzval`), so R errors 'files_daf: sparse matrix <name> missing .nzval for non-Bool' (R/files_daf_read.R:627). R also never WRITES sparse string matrices (R/files_daf_write.R:360-374 routes any String dtype matrix to the dense `.txt` path), so the encoding only appears when Julia is the writer.

narrowed.name: unsigned-integer dense read (UInt32 / UInt64)
narrowed.what_is_missing: R reads on-disk UInt32 as a SIGNED 32-bit int (files_io.R:329-332, `signed = TRUE`) and UInt64 by bit-aliasing into bit64::integer64 which is signed (files_io.R:333-338). A Julia-written UInt32 value >= 2^31 reads back as a negative R integer; a UInt64 value >= 2^63 reads back as a negative integer64. Julia preserves the unsigned value exactly. Scalar fast-path has the same issue: UInt32 scalar value >= 2^31 -> as.integer -> NA (files_io.R:224). R cannot natively represent unsigned ints, so this is a language-level narrowing, but it is a SILENT wrong value, not an error.

narrowed.name: non-Float64 sparse matrix values (Int/Float32 nzval)
narrowed.what_is_missing: R's Matrix package has only dgCMatrix (double) and lgCMatrix (logical) sparse types. `.files_get_matrix_sparse` always builds a dgCMatrix with `x = as.double(vals)` (R/files_daf_read.R:637-643). A Julia-written sparse matrix with eltype Int32/Int64/Float32 is read as Float64 (lossy for Int64 > 2^53). On WRITE, R's `.files_write_matrix_sparse` (R/files_daf_write.R:298-336) hardcodes `dtype <- "Float64"` and `as.double(mat@x)`, so a round-trip Julia(Int32 sparse) -> R -> Julia silently changes the on-disk eltype from Int32 to Float64. Julia's format_set_matrix! preserves eltype(matrix) (files_format.jl:877-930). Partially acknowledged for nzval in dev/notes/2026-06-09-zarr-v3-followups-kickoff.md but not framed as a FilesDaf write-side eltype-loss divergence.

narrowed.name: Float32 / narrow-int dense WRITE
narrowed.what_is_missing: R's `.dtype_for_r_vector` (files_io.R:50-70) maps R double -> Float64, integer -> Int32, integer64 -> Int64 only. There is no path for R to WRITE Float32, Int8, Int16, UInt8/16/32/64 dense properties; Julia can write all of these (StorageReal full set, DTYPE_BY_NAME operations.jl:215-241). READ of all these dtypes works (files_io.R .read_bin_dense covers the full table). So this is a one-directional WRITE narrowing inherent to R's type system, not a read failure.

divergences.name: HTTP serving metadata file name (metadata.zip vs metadata.json)
divergences.julia_behavior: FilesDaf maintains root `metadata.json`; HttpDaf client fetches `<url>/metadata.json` (http_format.jl:131).
divergences.r_behavior: FilesDaf maintains `metadata.zip` (a ZIP of all JSON descriptors) + `axes/metadata.json`; http_daf client fetches `<url>/metadata.zip` (R/http_format.R:62). R server <-> R client are self-consistent but mutually incompatible with Julia in BOTH directions.
divergences.evidence: Julia: files_format.jl:1472,1594,1620,1713; http_format.jl:131. R: R/files_metadata_zip.R:25,120; R/http_format.R:62. Fixture proof: tests/testthat/fixtures/jf11/metadata.json is a JSON object, no metadata.zip present.

divergences.name: w+ truncate does not remove stale root metadata.json
divergences.julia_behavior: Truncate (mode w) does `rm(path; recursive=true)` of the whole directory (files_format.jl:349-352).
divergences.r_behavior: `.files_daf_init(truncate=TRUE)` (R/files_daf.R:209-216) only unlinks the 4 subdirs + daf.json + .reorder.backup, preserving 'unrelated files'. A root `metadata.json` left by a prior Julia open would survive a dafr `w+` truncate and become inconsistent with the rebuilt tree until a Julia writable reopen rebuilds it.
divergences.evidence: R/files_daf.R:209-216 vs files_format.jl:349-352

divergences.name: scalar-broadcast set_vector/set_matrix (value is a scalar incl 0)
divergences.julia_behavior: format_set_vector!/format_set_matrix! accept Union{StorageScalar,StorageVector}; a scalar broadcasts via fill_file, and value `== 0` becomes spzeros on disk (files_format.jl:576-577, 888-889).
divergences.r_behavior: R's public set_vector/set_matrix require a full-length vector/matrix (.validate_vector_value enforces length == axis_length); there is no scalar-broadcast or all-zeros-sparse shortcut path. This is a writers-layer API difference that also affects what FilesDaf writes to disk (Julia can emit a spzeros sparse property where R only ever emits an explicit dense/sparse object the caller materialized).

Per-property sidecar descriptors are byte-identical: dense `{"format":"dense","eltype":"X"}`, scalar `{"type":"X","value":...}`, axis txt one-entry-per-line (files_format.jl:435,1350 + packed_format.jl dense_array_json_bytes vs R/files_io.R:80,168 + R/files_daf_write.R).

v1.1 sparse descriptor shape matches incl per-component n_elements: nzind/nzval for vectors, colptr/rowval/nzval for matrices (packed_format.jl sparse_vector_json_bytes/sparse_matrix_json_bytes/component_descriptor_json vs R/files_io.R:.write_descriptor_sparse). v1.0 legacy top-level eltype/indtype also read by R (.files_parse_sparse_descriptor).

Sparsify heuristic threshold sparse_size <= 0.75*dense_size and indtype_for_size(max(nr,nc,nnz)) for matrices / indtype_for_size(n) for vectors match (files_format.jl:638,956 vs R/files_io.R:.should_sparsify_*,.indtype_for_size).

Reorder crash-safe protocol (.reorder.backup hardlink backup, replace, cleanup, reset-on-reopen, one crash tick per vector and per matrix) mirrors Julia exactly incl suffix lists (files_format.jl:1738-2062 vs R/files_daf_write.R:417-766).
Eager creation of vectors/<axis> and matrices/<axis>/<other> bucket dirs on add_axis, and cascade delete on delete_axis (files_format.jl:494-542 vs R/files_daf_write.R:40-134).
description_header emits `type: FilesDaf` / path / mode for both writer and read-only (files_format.jl:2064-2075 vs R/files_daf.R:185-199).
notes: Highest-confidence and highest-impact finding is the consolidated-metadata divergence: dafr maintains `metadata.zip` + `axes/metadata.json`, both mirroring a Julia design that no longer exists in DataAxesFormats.jl 0.3.0, which uses a single root `metadata.json` (verified by zero grep hits for metadata_zip/write_axes_metadata in the Julia src and by the verbatim fixture tests/testthat/fixtures/jf11/metadata.json). Local file reads still interoperate (Julia self-heals via tree-walk; dafr reads per-property sidecars), so this is invisible in directory round-trip tests and is genuinely missed by the existing parity docs - it only bites HTTP serving across languages. Second finding (sparse string MATRIX read) is a clean crash that the existing string-VECTOR sparse test would not catch because the matrix read path simply lacks the String arm the vector path has. The unsigned/Int-eltype narrowings are real but rooted in R's type system; flagged because they are SILENT. I was READ-ONLY: no R/Julia executed; all evidence is from source + committed fixtures. Probes are written to run through a paired R/Julia harness; the sparse-string-matrix and metadata.json probes are the two that should be wired up first.

missing_in_r.name: ZipDaf (.daf.zip / .dafs.zip ZipFormat backend)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia exports a whole storage format `ZipDaf` (zip_files.jl:93 `export ZipDaf`; constructor zip_files.jl:346) that stores a FilesDaf layout verbatim inside one ZIP archive, with single-daf (`*.daf.zip`) and multi-daf (`*.dafs.zip#/group`) forms, modes r/r+/w+/w, append-only writes, sub-daf sharing of one MmapZipStore, and `metadata.json` sidecar stripping. dafr has NO ZipDaf reader or writer at all: grep across R/ for `zip_daf`/`ZipDaf`/`.daf.zip`/`.dafs.zip` returns only files_packed.R and zarr_sharded.R (which are the *packed-shard* readers, not the ZipFormat container). NAMESPACE exports no `zip_daf`. The MmapZipStore C++ port (src/mmap_zip_store.cpp) exists but is used ONLY for FilesDaf `metadata.zip` and ZarrDaf `.daf.zarr.zip`, never to back a Daf the way Julia's ZipDaf does. Worse, `open_daf` (R/open_daf.R:59-63) routes any `*.daf.zip`/`*.dafs.zip` path to the DEFAULT `files_daf()` branch because it only special-cases `.daf.zarr.zip`/`.daf.zarr`; `files_daf` then tries to open the ZIP file as a directory and fails with a confusing filesystem error rather than an actionable 'ZipDaf unsupported' message. (This top-level gap is noted in dev/notes/2026-06-09-zarr-v3-followups-kickoff.md:188-192 as a known low-priority format gap, but the misrouting/non-graceful error and the full absence of read are worth pinning.)

missing_in_r.name: Packed WRITE (packed=true encoding) for any backend
missing_in_r.detail: Julia writes packed (chunked+compressed dual-format shards) via packed_format.jl `packed_format_write_dense_array!`, `encode_packed_dense_array`, `IncrementalShardWriter`, `make_streaming_shard_writer`, `submit_shard_chunk!`, `finalize_shard!`, and exposes a per-call/per-daf `packed::Bool` knob on FilesDaf/ZipDaf constructors and set_*!/empty_*!/copy_*! (default false; threshold DAF_PACKED_TARGET_CHUNK_KB=8). dafr has NO packed write path: files_packed.R / zarr_sharded.R are read-only; grep shows no IncrementalShardWriter / submit_shard / encode_packed analogue in R/. `files_daf(path, mode, name)` (R/files_daf.R:34) has no `packed` argument, and set_matrix/set_vector accept no `packed=` kwarg. Consequence: dafr can never produce a packed shard; round-trip parity (write-in-R, read-in-Julia) is impossible for packed data, and a Julia consumer expecting dafr to honor a `packed` request gets a flat store instead silently.

missing_in_r.name: DAF_PACKED_* / DAF_HTTP_MAX_COALESCE_GAP_KB / DAF_ZIP_MAX_FILE_SIZE tuning globals
missing_in_r.detail: Julia exports six packed-encoding globals (DAF_PACKED_TARGET_CHUNK_KB=8, DAF_PACKED_COMPRESSION=:blosc_zstd_bitshuffle, DAF_PACKED_COMPRESSION_LEVEL=5, DAF_PACKED_LOCAL_CACHE_KB=65536, DAF_PACKED_HTTP_CACHE_KB=262144, DAF_HTTP_MAX_COALESCE_GAP_KB) plus ZipFormat.DAF_ZIP_MAX_FILE_SIZE=1<<37. None exist in dafr (no equivalents in R/). Mostly moot since R neither writes packed nor coalesces HTTP ranges (it fetches the whole `.zip` shard), but the chunk-size/codec/level knobs have no R surface, so a user cannot control or even introspect packed encoding from dafr.

missing_in_r.name: ZipShardArray / PackedDenseArray / StripedVector / StripedMatrix lazy disk-array readers + HTTP range coalescing
missing_in_r.detail: Julia's packed read path is a lazy DiskArrays.ChunkedArray (packed_format.jl:599) that fetches only the chunks a slice touches, coalesces adjacent HTTP ranges (DAF_HTTP_MAX_COALESCE_GAP_KB), and LRU-caches decoded chunks. dafr always reads the ENTIRE shard file/HTTP object into memory (files_packed.R:78 `.files_packed_read_shard` reads `file.size(zip_path)`; http_format.R fetches the whole `.zip`) and decodes every chunk eagerly. Functionally equivalent results for full reads, but no sub-column / single-chunk slice optimization, no range coalescing — a perf/scaling divergence for large packed properties and for the K-marker query pattern the format was designed for.

narrowed.name: blosc-packed FilesDaf/HttpDaf read (default codec :blosc_zstd_bitshuffle, and :blosc_lz4_bitshuffle)
narrowed.what_is_missing: dafr CAN read packed shards only when the inner codec is gzip (base-R memDecompress) or zstd (configure-gated -DHAVE_ZSTD, present in this build's src/Makevars: `PKG_CPPFLAGS = -DHAVE_ZSTD`, `PKG_LIBS = ... -lzstd`). It CANNOT read blosc-packed shards because this build lacks -DHAVE_BLOSC (src/Makevars has no -DHAVE_BLOSC; configure prints 'c-blosc NOT found -> blosc-packed read errors at runtime'). Since Julia's DEFAULT packed codec is :blosc_zstd_bitshuffle, the *common* packed store is unreadable by this dafr build. files_packed.R:33 maps any `blosc*` compression to inner codec 'blosc', which routes to dafr_blosc_decompress_cpp (shard_codecs.cpp:44), whose #else stub raises 'Reading blosc-packed ZarrDaf requires c-blosc; install it ... and reinstall dafr.' The error IS graceful and actionable (good), but it is a hard read failure on the default-codec store. :zstd_bitshuffle and :gzip_shuffle never reach R because Julia's v3 backend rejects them at write time (packed_format.jl:1637-1648), so they are not a divergence.

narrowed.name: Packed shard index CRC32c validation
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia decodes the start-located shard index through Zarr's index pipeline `BytesCodec + CRC32cV3Codec` (packed_format.jl build_shard_metadata index_pipeline), so a corrupt index CRC32c is an ERROR (the checksum codec validates on decode). dafr only WARNS and continues: zarr_sharded.R:58-62 computes crc32c of the index bytes, and on mismatch emits `warning('zarr_sharded: shard index crc32c mismatch (... != ...); reading anyway')` and proceeds with the offsets. So a corrupted-index shard that Julia rejects, dafr reads (possibly returning garbage). Narrowed: validation exists but is downgraded from error to warning.

narrowed.name: Foreign ZIP-only ('zipped', no leading Zarr index) packed shard read
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia reads BOTH dual-format ('indexed+zipped') shards AND bare ZIP-only ('zipped') shards: ZipShardArray (packed_format.jl:956) reads via the ZIP central directory with O(1) index-arithmetic random access, no leading Zarr index required; the packed_format.md documents a foreign `packed_format=>'zipped'` source as legitimately readable. dafr reads ONLY 'indexed+zipped' shards (via the start-located Zarr index) and explicitly rejects any other packed_format: files_packed.R:46-55 `.files_packed_require_indexed` stops with an actionable message ('dafr can read only indexed+zipped shards (re-save ... or copy to flat components)') if `packed_format != 'indexed+zipped'`. Narrowed read coverage; the rejection is graceful.

narrowed.name: MmapZipStore foreign-archive compressed-entry decode (bzip2 method 12, zstd method 93, deflate64 method 9)
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia's MmapZipStore (mmap_zip_store.jl read_compressed_entry_bytes:567) decodes foreign ZIP entries compressed with DEFLATE(8), DEFLATE64(9) via ZipArchives, BZIP2(12) via CodecBzip2, and ZSTD(93) via CodecZstd, each with CRC+size validation, and errors clearly on any other method. dafr's MmapZipStore (src/mmap_zip_store.cpp read_decompressed:999) handles only STORED(0) and DEFLATE(8) — bzip2(12), deflate64(9), and zstd(93) entries throw 'unsupported compression method N' (mmap_zip_store.cpp:1048-1052). This matters where dafr's MmapZipStore IS used (FilesDaf metadata.zip, ZarrDaf .daf.zarr.zip): a foreign tool that compressed entries with bzip2/zstd/deflate64 inside such an archive is readable in Julia but not in dafr. Error is graceful.

divergences.name: open_daf misroutes .daf.zip / .dafs.zip to files_daf (directory open) instead of a clean ZipDaf-unsupported error
divergences.julia_behavior: ZipDaf('foo.daf.zip') opens the ZIP archive as a Daf; ZipDaf('foo.dafs.zip#/grp') opens a sub-daf; near-miss paths give targeted errors (parse_zip_archive_path: 'missing #/<group>', 'empty group name', 'can't address a sub-daf in a singular path').
divergences.r_behavior: open_daf (R/open_daf.R:59-63) only special-cases `.daf.zarr.zip` and `.daf.zarr`; every other path including `*.daf.zip`/`*.dafs.zip` falls to the default `files_daf(uri, mode, name)`, which tries to treat the ZIP file as a FilesDaf DIRECTORY and fails with a confusing 'not a directory'/'no daf.json' style filesystem error rather than 'ZipDaf format not supported'.
divergences.evidence: R/open_daf.R:36-63 (no .daf.zip branch); zip_files.jl:273-307 parse_zip_archive_path, zip_files.jl:346 ZipDaf constructor

divergences.name: Packed matrix on-disk axis-order convention is FilesFormat-specific in R; a mismatch silently transposes/corrupts
divergences.julia_behavior: FilesFormat writes the chunk_shape in natural Julia [rows, cols] order and the element stream column-major; ZarrDaf stores the reversed [cols, rows] zarr.json shape. Julia reads each via its own metadata so both are correct.
divergences.r_behavior: dafr hard-codes two different matrix reassembly cores: `.files_packed_decode_matrix` (files_packed.R:101) assumes FilesFormat [rows,cols] + column-major grid order (col-chunks outer, row-chunks inner), while `.shard_decode_matrix` (zarr_sharded.R:176) assumes the reversed ZarrDaf convention (C-order grid). These are NOT interchangeable. If a FilesDaf packed matrix were ever written with the ZarrDaf reversed convention (or vice versa), dafr would silently return a transposed/garbled matrix with no error. This is a correctness-critical assumption pinned only against current DAF 0.3.0 fixtures; the code comment (files_packed.R:14-22) acknowledges the convention is 'verified against real DAF 0.3.0 fixtures' but there is no runtime guard.
divergences.evidence: files_packed.R:101-134 vs zarr_sharded.R:176-202; the two opposite grid-iteration orders
