confirmed_parity: zstd-packed and gzip-packed FilesDaf/HttpDaf shard READS: dafr decodes zstd (shard_codecs.cpp:76 dafr_zstd_decompress_cpp, -DHAVE_ZSTD present in src/Makevars) and gzip (zarr_sharded.R:97 base-R memDecompress; the start-located Zarr index points at [gzip-header][DEFLATE][trailer] = a full gzip stream, which memDecompress(type='gzip') consumes correctly). 1-D dense vectors and sparse components (nzind/nzval/colptr/rowval, each independently packable) read through the same shard-decode core.

Packed sparse component layout parity: dafr handles v1.1 per-component descriptors (nzind/nzval/colptr/rowval) being independently flat-or-packed, the Bool all-true nzval-omission optimization (synthesizing TRUE values when nzval is absent), and v1.0/v1.1 descriptor shapes (files_daf_read.R + http_format.R mirror parse_sparse_descriptor logic).

int64/uint64 (Julia Int64/UInt64) packed values read via bit64::integer64 (zarr_v3.R:25-41, .zarr_zero_vector handles integer64), matching Julia's element width; empty-chunk (0xFFFF..FF sentinel) fill-with-zero handling matches (zarr_sharded.R:72-75, files_packed.R:121).

MmapZipStore core read/write/append/recovery is a faithful byte-level port: ZIP64-always archives, 8-byte data alignment via DAF padding extra field (0xDAF1), two-step commit protocol, crash recovery (recover_interrupted_appends / entry_is_valid / roll_back_to_entry), reserve+patch-CRC two-phase append, and remove_entries_from_central_directory all mirror mmap_zip_store.jl (src/mmap_zip_store.cpp). STORED(0) zero-copy + DEFLATE(8) decode with CRC validation match.

Codecs Julia itself cannot write to a v3 sharded backend (:gzip_shuffle, :zstd_bitshuffle) are rejected at WRITE time in Julia (packed_format.jl:1637-1648), so they never appear in a FilesDaf/HttpDaf shard; dafr's inability to decode them is not a real divergence (no producible input).
notes: Audit scope: PackedFormat + ZipFormat + MmapZipStores. Method: read all three .jl files and their .md contracts in full, then mapped each public item to R across R/ + NAMESPACE + src/. Headline: dafr's packed support is READ-ONLY and confined to FilesDaf/HttpDaf packed-shard decoding; it has NO ZipFormat container backend (the whole `.daf.zip`/`.dafs.zip` Daf-in-zip format), NO packed WRITE path, and in THIS build cannot read the DEFAULT blosc codec. The ZipDaf-absence and blosc/zstd-gating are already noted in dev/notes (2026-06-09-zarr-v3-followups-kickoff.md:188-192) as known gaps and were re-confirmed here rather than newly discovered; the NOVEL, higher-value findings are: (1) open_daf SILENTLY MISROUTES `.daf.zip` to files_daf -> confusing error instead of a clean unsupported message (R/open_daf.R:59-63); (2) the shard-index CRC32c check is downgraded from Julia's hard error to a WARNING (zarr_sharded.R:58-62) -> dafr reads corrupt-index shards Julia rejects; (3) the FilesFormat-vs-ZarrDaf matrix axis-order convention is hard-coded with two opposite reassembly cores and no runtime guard -> a convention mismatch silently transposes data; (4) MmapZipStore (used for metadata.zip / .daf.zarr.zip) only decodes STORED+DEFLATE entries, missing bzip2/zstd/deflate64 that Julia's store reads. Errors for the no-blosc / zipped-only / unsupported-method cases ARE graceful and actionable (a plus). I did NOT run R or Julia (read-only audit); probes are specified for the downstream differential harness. The blosc build state is build-specific — a dafr built with -DHAVE_BLOSC (system c-blosc present) would read blosc-packed shards, so PZM-01's blosc branch is contingent on this environment's src/Makevars (which has -DHAVE_ZSTD only).

missing_in_r.name: H5df storage backend (whole native HDF5 single-file DAF format)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia exports `H5df` (h5df_format.jl:167, struct at :268) as a first-class DafWriter backend that stores a complete DAF dataset inside one HDF5 file using the DAF-native internal layout (root `daf` version dataset = [MAJOR_VERSION=1, MINOR_VERSION=0]; sub-groups `scalars`/`axes`/`vectors`/`matrices`). This is explicitly NOT h5ad/AnnData (h5df_format.md:1-9, jl:5-9). dafr has ZERO implementation: R/open_daf.R:37-38 hard-rejects any `.h5df` or `.h5dfs#` URI with stop("H5df backend not supported yet"). There is no h5df_format.R, no `h5df_daf()` constructor, no `H5df`/`H5dfDaf` class, nothing in NAMESPACE. dafr's HDF5 surface is only h5ad conversion (h5ad_as_daf / daf_as_h5ad, AnnData - a distinct format). Confirmed deferred-by-design across many dev notes (slice-6-exit.md:67, slice-8-kickoff.md:87, slice-10-kickoff.md:30) and tracked as reorder-parity divergence R3.

missing_in_r.name: H5df constructor modes r/r+/w+/w with create/truncate semantics
missing_in_r.detail: Julia H5df(root, mode="r"; name, packed) supports the 4 standard modes with a documented truth table (h5df_format.jl:238-248): r->DafReadOnly, r+/w+/w->H5df writer; w+ creates-if-missing without truncate, w truncates. Special: w mode on a `file.h5dfs#/group` path truncates ONLY the group, not the whole file (jl:247-248, 319-323). None of this is reachable in dafr since the backend does not exist.

missing_in_r.name: .h5dfs#/group multi-DAF-per-file path scheme

missing_in_r.name: packed (chunked+compressed) HDF5 encoding option
missing_in_r.detail: Julia H5df constructor `packed::Bool=false` kwarg (jl:294) plus per-call packed kwargs on set_*!/empty_*!/copy_*! select chunked+compressed dataset encoding above DAF_PACKED_TARGET_CHUNK_KB, using Blosc/bitshuffle/Zstd/Deflate filters (jl:64-97, write_packed_dense_dataset! at :2248, hdf5_filters_for at :2271). Reader wraps packed datasets in H5dfDiskArray/LazySparse with an LRU chunk cache (jl:81-89). dafr has packed support only for its OWN FilesDaf format (R/files_packed.R), not for any HDF5/h5df store - moot since h5df backend is absent.

missing_in_r.name: H5df sparse-string (nztxt) and Bool all-true skip-storage encodings

missing_in_r.name: obsp / varp square-matrix mapping (read AND write)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia copy_supported_square_matrices (anndata_format.jl:426-443) reads adata.obsp/adata.varp into Daf as (axis,axis) square matrices, applying flip() so the column-major Daf matrix is the transpose of the row-major AnnData square matrix (documented warning at anndata_format.md:41-65). daf_as_anndata writes them back via copy_square_matrices (anndata_format.jl:647-652). dafr has ZERO obsp/varp support: h5ad_as_daf never reads /obsp or /varp (its docstring at anndata_format.R:133 explicitly says 'obsp / varp ... are still escalated through unsupported_handler and skipped' - but in fact there is no code that even looks at /obsp or /varp, so they are silently ignored, not even warned), and daf_as_h5ad never writes square matrices on (obs_axis,obs_axis) or (var_axis,var_axis). Cell-cell graphs (e.g. connectivities, distances from scanpy neighbors) are dropped entirely.

missing_in_r.name: obs_is / var_is / X_is axis-and-matrix renaming round-trip
missing_in_r.detail: Julia's central design (anndata_format.md:19-22) is: when viewing Daf as AnnData it renames two chosen axes to obs/var and one matrix to X, storing the ORIGINAL names in uns scalars obs_is/var_is/X_is (store_rename_scalar, anndata_format.jl:588-590,633-645), and when reading AnnData back it restores them (by_annotation, anndata_format.jl:168-191). This lets a 'cell'/'gene'/'UMIs' Daf round-trip back to 'cell'/'gene'/'UMIs'. dafr does NOT implement this at all: daf_as_h5ad writes no obs_is/var_is/X_is markers, and h5ad_as_daf hardcodes the axes to 'obs'/'var' (anndata_format.R:182,193) and the X matrix name to 'UMIs' (anndata_format.R:207,218). The package's own test acknowledges this gap (test-anndata-format.R:70-77, test-anndata-jl-parity.R:70-73): a cell/gene Daf round-trips to obs/var, losing the original axis names. Net: axis-name and X-name identity is silently lost on every round-trip.

missing_in_r.name: In-memory anndata_as_daf / daf_as_anndata (AnnData object bridge)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia exports two functions operating on a first-class in-memory AnnData (Muon.AnnData) OR a path string: anndata_as_daf(adata; ...) and daf_as_anndata(daf; h5ad=...) returning an AnnData (anndata_format.jl:73-74,129,564). dafr has no in-memory AnnData type; it only offers file-based h5ad_as_daf(path)/daf_as_h5ad(daf,path) plus a read-only DafAnnData R6 facade. This is a deliberate documented architectural divergence (test-anndata-jl-parity.R:1-45 'CA9'), not a bug, but it means: (a) the zero-copy / memory-mapping view semantics (md:5-8, 'conversion is zero-copy') are absent - dafr always materializes into a memory_daf; (b) daf_as_anndata's return value (an AnnData usable without touching disk) has no equivalent; (c) the DafAnnData facade is read-only and exposes only X/obs/var/layers/uns/names/shape - it does NOT expose obsp/varp/obsm/varm at all.

missing_in_r.name: filter callback parameter on anndata_as_daf
missing_in_r.detail: Julia anndata_as_daf accepts an optional leading filter::Function(member,key)->Bool to selectively skip X/obs/var/obsp/varp/layer members (anndata_format.jl:124-127,140-150, threaded through every copy_supported_* and verify_* function). dafr h5ad_as_daf has no filter argument at all (anndata_format.R:155-156); a caller cannot skip specific layers/columns on load.

missing_in_r.name: X_eltype dtype-coercion parameter on daf_as_anndata
missing_in_r.detail: Julia daf_as_anndata has X_eltype::Maybe{Type} that coerces the X matrix element type on export (anndata_format.jl:569,581-583). dafr daf_as_h5ad has no x_eltype/X_dtype argument; X is written with whatever R storage type get_matrix returns. Minor, but it is a missing knob for controlling on-disk dtype (e.g. forcing Float32).

missing_in_r.name: unsupported_handler coverage for obsm/varm/uns-mapping on read
missing_in_r.detail: Julia's verify_unsupported (anndata_format.jl:196-218) escalates obsm/varm (verify_are_empty: treated as ALWAYS unsupported -> WarnHandler by default) and non-scalar uns and non-row/col-major matrices through the AbnormalHandler BEFORE copying. dafr instead SUPPORTS obsm/varm by inventing synthetic dim axes (anndata_format.R:331-360) - a divergence in itself (see divergences) - and silently drops non-scalar uns leaves with no handler call (.flatten_uns at anndata_format.R:116-123 skips silently; comment admits 'skipped silently here'). So uns mappings/arrays that Julia would WARN about, dafr drops with no warning even under WARN_HANDLER.

narrowed.name: Categorical (factor) handling
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia converts categorical VECTORS to plain strings on import (md:32-33, copy_supported_vectors at anndata_format.jl:403-418 materializes a Vector{element_type}, dropping the categorical wrapper so the Daf vector is a string/numeric vector). dafr instead PRESERVES the factor as an R factor (anndata_format.R:71-85 .read_h5ad_categorical returns a factor, and daf_as_h5ad re-emits factors as categorical groups at 461-465). This is arguably nicer in R, but it is a semantic divergence: a Daf obtained from the same h5ad has an R factor in dafr vs a character vector in Julia, which changes downstream dtype checks and round-trip shape (Julia round-trips categorical->string->dense dataset; dafr round-trips factor->categorical group).

narrowed.name: Sparse X / layer storage on read
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia reads Muon SparseDataset and, for CSR, flips axes so the Daf matrix is stored with columns_axis,rows_axis swapped (anndata_format.jl:475-489) keeping it as a SparseMatrixCSC. dafr reads CSR into a dgRMatrix then coerces to dgCMatrix keeping (obs,var) orientation via the explicit shape attr (anndata_format.R:26-35). Both end with a column-major sparse Daf matrix, BUT dafr's X is always stored only on (obs,var) under name 'UMIs'; Julia stores under X_is and (because of the flip semantics for square only) keeps non-square in row-major-from-AnnData. For non-square X the end orientation matches; flagged only as low-risk.

narrowed.name: uns scalar copy on export
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia copy_scalars copies ALL Daf scalars into adata.uns flat (anndata_format.jl:626-631) and copy_supported_scalars imports only StorageScalar uns entries (skipping mappings) on load. dafr writes all scalars flat to /uns (anndata_format.R:525-529) and on read flattens nested uns groups into '_'-joined keys (anndata_format.R:108-125). The nested-flattening behavior has NO Julia equivalent (Julia stores nested uns as JSON blobs per md:26-27 TODO, or skips); dafr's '_' flattening silently merges namespaces and is irreversible, so a round-trip of nested uns yields different scalar keys than the original (documented at anndata_format.R:373-375).

divergences.name: Dense /X (and dense layer) on-disk orientation not AnnData-canonical
divergences.julia_behavior: daf_as_anndata writes X as flip(get_matrix(daf,var_is,obs_is,X_is).array) producing a genuine row-major (obs x var) Julia AnnData X that writeh5ad stores in the canonical h5ad layout; readh5ad/Muon reads it back correctly, and Python anndata reads it correctly (anndata_format.jl:580-584,605).
divergences.r_behavior: daf_as_h5ad writes the dense X by handing the R column-major matrix straight to hdf5r: h5$create_dataset('X', robj = X) (anndata_format.R:448) with NO transpose and NO shape attr. hdf5r stores an R (n_obs x n_var) column-major matrix to an HDF5 dataset whose logical shape becomes (n_var x n_obs) from a row-major (Python/anndata) reader's perspective. h5ad_as_daf reads it back with the SAME hdf5r convention (x_obj$read() at anndata_format.R:214) so dafr<->dafr round-trips correctly, but a file written by daf_as_h5ad is NOT guaranteed to be read with correct obs/var orientation by Python anndata / Muon / Julia, and conversely a dense-X h5ad written by Python (true obs-major) read by dafr could come back transposed. The dafr dense fixtures are all R-generated (dev/scripts/generate-*-h5ad.R) so this cross-tool path is completely untested. Sparse X is safe because it carries an explicit shape attr (anndata_format.R:24,46,60).
divergences.evidence: anndata_format.R:443-449 vs anndata_format.jl:580-584; fixtures dev/scripts/generate-small-test-h5ad.R, generate-sparse-test-h5ad.R are R-only

divergences.name: obsm / varm representation (synthetic axes vs unsupported)
divergences.julia_behavior: obsm/varm are explicitly treated as UNSUPPORTED on import: verify_are_empty escalates every obsm/varm key through the AbnormalHandler (WarnHandler by default), and copy_supported never copies them (anndata_format.jl:215-216,295-308). They are simply not representable in Julia Daf (md:34-37). daf_as_anndata never produces obsm/varm.
divergences.r_behavior: dafr INVENTS support: h5ad_as_daf reads each /obsm[name] (n_obs x k) into a Daf matrix on a synthetic axis 'obsm_<name>_dim' with entries '1'..'k' (anndata_format.R:331-360), and daf_as_h5ad reverses it by pattern-matching axis names '^obsm_(.+)_dim$' (anndata_format.R:495-522). This is strictly MORE featureful than Julia, but it is a behavioral divergence: the same h5ad loaded in Julia (with WARN) drops obsm/varm and has no such axes, while dafr gains extra axes/matrices. Code written to the Julia contract (expecting obsm to be absent / warned) will see unexpected axes in dafr. It also has no handler escalation - obsm/varm are loaded silently, never WARNed, unlike Julia.
divergences.evidence: anndata_format.R:327-360,492-522 vs anndata_format.jl:215-216,295-308

divergences.name: Vector densify-on-export vs raw write
divergences.julia_behavior: daf_as_anndata copy_vectors calls densify(get_vector(...).array) before storing into the obs/var DataFrame (anndata_format.jl:657), guaranteeing dense obs/var columns in the AnnData (sparse vectors are densified).
divergences.r_behavior: daf_as_h5ad writes format_get_vector(...)$value straight to a dataset (anndata_format.R:460-465,471-477) with no densify step. dafr's Daf vectors are typically dense R atomic vectors so this rarely matters, but a Daf holding a sparse vector (dgCMatrix-backed) would be written without the explicit densify Julia guarantees, risking an hdf5r write error or a non-canonical encoding for that column.
divergences.evidence: anndata_format.R:459-477 vs anndata_format.jl:654-659

divergences.name: Boolean / nullable / NaN-Inf handling on import
divergences.julia_behavior: Julia has explicit machinery for missing/nothing element types and Bool columns: it scans for the first non-missing value to infer element_type, fills missing/undef entries with element_type(0) (or '' for strings), and force-materializes Bool/categorical/non-StorageVector columns into a proper dense vector (anndata_format.jl:381-420). Nullable integer matrices use the zero-is-special convention (md:28-31).
divergences.r_behavior: dafr does none of this. h5ad columns are read with child$read() (anndata_format.R:243,274) and set verbatim; there is no missing->0 fill, no Bool special-casing, no first-non-missing element-type inference. NA handling exists ONLY for categorical codes==-1 (anndata_format.R:79-80). A boolean obs column, a nullable-integer column, or NaN/Inf entries are passed through R's native semantics with no normalization, diverging from Julia's zero-fill convention.
divergences.evidence: anndata_format.jl:381-420 vs anndata_format.R:243-250,274-281 (no equivalent)

confirmed_parity: Default axis naming obs/var and X matrix selection: both default 'obs'/'var' axis names and an X matrix (Julia X_is default 'X'; dafr x_name default 'UMIs' - note the X default-NAME itself differs, but the role mapping is equivalent).

CSR/CSC sparse X and sparse layer read into a column-major sparse matrix (dgCMatrix in dafr; SparseMatrixCSC in Julia) - dafr handles both encodings with explicit shape attr (anndata_format.R:18-48) matching Julia's SparseDataset handling.
Scalar uns import/export for StorageScalar values: both copy flat scalar uns entries in and out (anndata_format.jl:348-359,626-631 vs anndata_format.R:285-291,525-529).
obs/var vector (DataFrame column) import keyed by axis with _index as the axis name vector (anndata_format.jl:331-335,361-424 vs anndata_format.R:181-282).
Extra (obs,var) matrices map to /layers in both directions (anndata_format.jl:340,598,661-674 vs anndata_format.R:293-325,480-490).
Integer vs double dtype round-trip for dense matrices and vectors is preserved by dafr (test-anndata-format.R:106-125) consistent with Julia preserving StorageScalar element types.
notes: dafr's anndata bridge is a deliberate ARCHITECTURAL reimplementation, not a line-port: Julia uses Muon.jl's in-memory AnnData with zero-copy views and the obs_is/var_is/X_is uns-marker convention; dafr is a hand-rolled file-based HDF5 reader/writer (h5ad_as_daf/daf_as_h5ad) plus a read-only DafAnnData R6 facade. This is documented and accepted as CA9 in test-anndata-jl-parity.R, so the in-memory bridge + filter + zero-copy gaps are 'known'. The findings the existing parity docs most likely MISSED, in priority order: (1) the obs_is/var_is/X_is identity round-trip is completely unimplemented - axis and X-matrix names are silently lost on every round-trip (this is the CENTRAL design point of the Julia module per the .md, and dafr drops it); (2) obsp/varp graphs are silently dropped with not even a warning despite the docstring claiming they are 'escalated through unsupported_handler'; (3) the dense /X write uses hdf5r's native (column-major) convention with no transpose/shape attr, so it self-round-trips but is NOT verified to be canonical h5ad readable by Python anndata/Julia - and all dense fixtures are R-generated, so cross-tool orientation is untested (potential silent-wrong-answer). (4) dafr ADDS obsm/varm support (synthetic dim axes) that Julia explicitly rejects - a divergence in the other direction. All cross-tool probes ideally need Python anndata or real Julia to confirm orientation/encoding; I could not run either (read-only). The obsp/var_is/filter/X_eltype/in-memory gaps are confirmable from source alone.

subsystem: http-format (HttpDaf read-only remote FilesDaf over HTTP, plus the HTTP-served Zarr v3 store HttpStore)

missing_in_r.name: Range-GET lazy streaming of large flat dense properties (StripedVector/StripedMatrix over HTTP)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia http_format.jl:484-498 (read_flat_dense_numeric_vector) and :521-536 (read_flat_dense_numeric_matrix) call chunks_for(true, shape, T); when the property exceeds the chunk-byte threshold they return a lazy StripedVector/StripedMatrix backed by url_byte_fetcher (Range GETs of stripe_n_elements at a time, adjacent ranges coalesced, see packed_format.jl:309-329, 359-361, DAF_HTTP_MAX_COALESCE_GAP_KB). dafr R has NO Range-GET support at all: .dafr_http_get (http_client.R:15-38) issues a single plain GET with no Range header; format_get_vector / format_get_matrix (http_format.R:351-438, 463-581) always fetch the ENTIRE .data/.nzval/.rowval file via one GET and materialize it. There is no StripedVector/StripedMatrix analogue, no http_range_get, no coalescing, no DAF_HTTP_MAX_COALESCE_GAP_KB / DAF_PACKED_HTTP_CACHE_KB options. Functionally R still returns the correct values (full download then decode), so this is a perf/scaling gap, not a wrong-answer gap, for FLAT dense data. Note: the threshold also matters because below it Julia ALSO does a single GET, so small properties already match.

missing_in_r.name: Packed (chunked+compressed ZIP-shard) dense properties served over HTTP via suffix-Range + per-chunk Range GETs
missing_in_r.detail: Julia http_format.jl:504-516 (read_packed_dense_vector) and :540-554 (read_packed_dense_matrix) build a ZipShardArray over url_byte_fetcher + url_suffix_byte_fetcher: the ZIP central directory is fetched once via a suffix-Range GET (bytes=-N, http_range_get_suffix, packed_format.jl:334-354) and each needed chunk via a Range GET, decoded through the codec pipeline. dafr R routes packed via .files_packed_decode_vector/.files_packed_decode_matrix (http_format.R:362-366, 388-396, 476-483, 520-521) but ALWAYS downloads the WHOLE .zip / .nzval.zip / .colptr.zip shard with one plain GET (.dafr_http_get(paste0(base, '.zip'))) then decodes locally. So R speaks a DIFFERENT and simpler wire pattern (full-shard GET vs CD-suffix-range + per-chunk-range). For correctness of the materialized values this still works IF the server serves the whole shard; but it cannot do the partial-read bandwidth optimization, and it assumes the server returns a complete object on a plain GET (Julia's path issues Range requests instead). Result values match; the request protocol diverges.

missing_in_r.name: packed kwarg on the HttpDaf constructor
missing_in_r.detail: Julia HttpDaf(url; name=nothing, packed::Bool=false) accepts a packed kwarg 'for API uniformity with the writable formats' (http_format.jl:100-104, doc :78-79; it is a no-op since HttpDaf is read-only). R http_daf(url, name=NULL) (http_format.R:55) has no packed argument. Calling code that passes packed= (mirroring Julia) would error in R with 'unused argument'. Harmless in practice but an API-surface mismatch.

narrowed.name: format_axes_set / format_has_axis enumeration source
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia HttpDaf derives the axes set purely from the in-memory consolidated metadata dict via names_under(http, 'axes') (http_format.jl:168-181, 213-216) which scans keys of form 'axes/<name>' that the metadata.json index carries as {format:'axis',n_entries:N} (files_format.jl:1629). R HttpDaf instead reads a SEPARATE bundled file 'axes/metadata.json' (http_format.R:209-220) that lists axis names as a JSON array - a file Julia FilesDaf neither writes to its root metadata.json index nor relies on for axis enumeration. If a tree built/served by Julia lacks axes/metadata.json inside the (nonexistent in Julia) metadata.zip, R's format_axes_set silently returns character(0) (http_format.R:213-214 early-return on missing axes/metadata.json), i.e. it reports the daf as having NO axes rather than reading them from the index. This is downstream of the wire-protocol divergence but is an independent enumeration-source mismatch.

narrowed.name: URL-derived default name
narrowed.what_is_missing: When no name kwarg and no scalars/name property, Julia sets name = url (the full URL string) then unique_name(url) (http_format.jl:127-135). R sets name = basename(url) (http_format.R:92-93, falling back to 'http' if empty). So Julia names the daf by its full URL; R names it by the last path segment. The R docstring (http_format.R:30-34) explicitly flags this divergence and the collision risk for two hosts sharing a basename. Different daf .name -> different description() output and different default names in chains/views.

narrowed.name: v1.0 sparse default indtype
narrowed.what_is_missing: R .files_parse_sparse_descriptor (files_daf_read.R:327-346, used by the HTTP sparse path) defaults indtype to 'UInt32' when a v1.0 top-level descriptor has eltype but no indtype (line 331). Julia parse_sparse_descriptor (packed_format.jl:1786-1801) reads String(json['indtype']) unconditionally in the v1.0 branch and would throw KeyError if indtype is absent. A malformed/edge v1.0 sparse descriptor missing indtype is silently accepted by R (assuming UInt32) but errors in Julia. Narrow edge; real Julia-written v1.0 always emits indtype.

divergences.name: Open-time wire protocol: metadata.json (Julia) vs metadata.zip (R)
divergences.julia_behavior: HttpDaf(url) GETs {url}/daf.json then {url}/metadata.json (http_format.jl:110, 123). metadata.json is a single-line JSON object mapping each property's relative path to its descriptor (files_format.jl:36, 45-58, 1620-1673; written verbatim into the served FilesDaf tree by metadata_json_rebuild!). The server is assumed to expose the FilesDaf directory tree VERBATIM with GET {url}/{relative_path} (http_format.md / http_format.jl:1-17). No zip is involved anywhere.
divergences.r_behavior: http_daf(url) GETs a single {url}/metadata.zip bundle (http_format.R:62), writes it to a tempfile, and serves all JSON metadata (daf.json, scalars/*.json, vectors/*/*.json, matrices/*/*/*.json, axes/metadata.json) by unzipping entries from it (http_format.R:62-130). The dafr FilesDaf writer produces this metadata.zip (files_metadata_zip.R:25-109) and does NOT write a root metadata.json index. So a dafr-served FilesDaf has metadata.zip but no metadata.json; a Julia-served FilesDaf has metadata.json but no metadata.zip. Cross-reading is impossible: Julia HttpDaf against a dafr server 404s on /metadata.json; R http_daf against a Julia server 404s on /metadata.zip (and would error 'not a daf data set' / the .dafr_http_get non-200 error). They do NOT speak the same wire protocol.
divergences.evidence: Julia: http_format.jl:110-125, files_format.jl:36,45-58,1472,1620-1673. R: http_format.R:62-130, files_metadata_zip.R:25-207 (.metadata_zip_rebuild builds metadata.zip; pack_files_daf_metadata is the R-only public helper to produce it). R docstring http_format.R:8-12 states the server must include metadata.zip; Julia md states the server exposes metadata.json.

divergences.name: Version-incompatibility error message text
divergences.julia_behavior: Errors with multi-line: 'incompatible format version: <maj>.<min>\nthe code supports version: 1.1\nin daf HTTP data set: <url>' (http_format.jl:115-121). Accepts version iff Int(version[1])==1 and Int(version[2])<=1.
divergences.r_behavior: Errors with 'incompatible format version: %d.%d\nfor the daf HTTP data set: %s\nthe code supports version: 1.1' (http_format.R:74-80). Same accept predicate (v[[1]]==1 && v[[2]]<=1) but different line order/wording ('for the daf HTTP data set' vs 'in daf HTTP data set', and the supported-version line comes last in Julia, second in R).
divergences.evidence: Julia http_format.jl:115-121; R http_format.R:74-80. Acceptance logic is equivalent (MAJOR=1/MINOR=1, files_format.jl:286,296); only message text differs.

divergences.name: Transport error / non-200 message shape
divergences.julia_behavior: http_get errors 'HTTP GET error: <exc>\nfor URL: <url>' on transport failure and 'HTTP GET non-200 status: <code>\nfor URL: <url>' on non-200 (packed_format.jl:287-303). Uses retry=false. Range variants add 'HTTP Range GET ...' / 'HTTP suffix Range GET ...' messages.
divergences.r_behavior: .dafr_http_get errors 'HTTP GET failed for: <url>\nunderlying error: <msg>' on transport failure and 'HTTP GET returned status N for: <url>' on non-200 (http_client.R:22-34). Also retry-free (req_retry(max_tries=1)). Adds an allow_404 option (returns NULL on 404) that Julia has no equivalent of - see next item. No Range-GET error messages exist because there is no Range path.
divergences.evidence: Julia packed_format.jl:287-354; R http_client.R:15-52. Message wording differs ('GET failed for' vs 'GET error', 'returned status N for' vs 'non-200 status'). The header comment in http_client.R claims these match upstream message shapes, but the exact strings differ.

divergences.name: All-true sparse Bool detection: descriptor-driven (Julia) vs 404-probe (R)
divergences.julia_behavior: Decides whether a sparse Bool property stored its .nzval by inspecting the descriptor: nzval_present = (nzval_descriptor !== nothing) || haskey(json, 'eltype') (http_format.jl:289, 450). If absent it synthesizes an all-true nzval (all_true_nzval_source / all-true source) with NO HTTP request for .nzval. So Julia never issues a GET for a nonexistent .nzval file.
divergences.r_behavior: For Bool vectors/matrices, R issues an actual GET for {base}.nzval with allow_404=TRUE (http_format.R:417-418, 523-524) and treats a 404 as the all-true signal. This means R makes an extra HTTP round-trip per all-true Bool property AND depends on the server returning 404 (not 403, not a fallback index.html, not a 200 with an error page) for the missing file. A misconfigured static server that returns 200 with a non-.nzval body, or a non-404 status, would diverge: Julia decides from JSON and never asks; R asks and can be fooled. For v1.1 trees where the all-true case omits both the file and the nzval descriptor, the VALUES agree, but the request behavior and failure modes differ.
divergences.evidence: Julia http_format.jl:289-291, 336-343, 450-452. R http_format.R:410-428 (vector Bool), 519-540 (matrix Bool); http_client.R:30 (allow_404 returns NULL on 404).

divergences.name: Sparse Bool vector with a stored (not-all-true) .nzval in v1.0 layout
divergences.julia_behavior: In Julia, nzval_present is true if json has top-level 'eltype' (v1.0) OR a nzval descriptor (v1.1). For a v1.0 sparse Bool vector that stores its .nzval, json has eltype -> nzval_present true -> reads .nzval (http_format.jl:289-299).
divergences.r_behavior: R's vector Bool branch ALWAYS probes {base}.nzval with allow_404 (http_format.R:417). For a v1.0 Bool vector that DOES store .nzval, the GET returns 200 and R reads it - correct. But the all-true detection is purely 'did the GET 404', independent of whether the descriptor advertised eltype. So in v1.0, where eltype is always present, Julia would NEVER treat it as all-true (it reads .nzval and would error on a real 404), whereas R would silently treat a missing .nzval as all-true even in v1.0. If a v1.0 Bool vector legitimately has no .nzval (all-true, writer-skipped), Julia v1.0 path expects .nzval present (eltype set) and would error on the missing file, while R returns all-true. Practically, dafr's own v1.0 writer is not the common path (it emits v1.1), so exposure is low, but the behaviors genuinely differ on a v1.0 all-true Bool.
divergences.evidence: Julia http_format.jl:288-299 (nzval_present includes haskey(json,'eltype')); R http_format.R:410-428 (404-probe regardless of version).

probes.description: Serve a dafr-written FilesDaf over a static HTTP server and try to open it with Julia HttpDaf, and vice-versa (Julia-written FilesDaf opened with R http_daf). Confirms the metadata.json vs metadata.zip wire incompatibility.
probes.query_or_snippet: R side (build + serve): p<-tempfile('d'); d<-files_daf(p,'w+'); add_axis(d,'cell',c('c1','c2')); set_vector(d,'cell','score',c(1.5,2.5)); # ls(p) shows metadata.zip but NO metadata.json. Start `python -m http.server` in p's parent. Julia side: using DataAxesFormats; HttpDaf("http://127.0.0.1:8000/d.daf")  # EXPECT: error 'HTTP GET non-200 status: 404 ... /metadata.json'. Reverse: Julia writes FilesDaf foo.daf (has metadata.json, no metadata.zip), serve it, then R: http_daf('http://127.0.0.1:8000/foo.daf')  # EXPECT: error from .dafr_http_get fetching /metadata.zip (404).
probes.expects: Both directions error at open: Julia cannot find metadata.json in an R-served tree; R cannot find metadata.zip in a Julia-served tree. Proves the two clients do not interoperate with each other's servers.
probes.targets_finding: Open-time wire protocol: metadata.json (Julia) vs metadata.zip (R)

probes.description: Serve a FilesDaf (same backend per side) with a dense Float32 vector large enough to exceed the chunk-byte threshold, and capture the server access log. Julia issues Range GETs (multiple 206 responses) for stripes; R issues one plain 200 GET of the whole .data file.
probes.query_or_snippet: Create axis 'cell' with N entries where N*4 bytes > the striped threshold (e.g. N=20_000_000 Float32 ~ 80MB). Store vectors/cell/big (Float32, flat dense .data). Serve over a logging static server. Julia: get_vector(HttpDaf(url),'cell','big')  # server log: multiple 'Range: bytes=...' 206 requests against /vectors/cell/big.data. R (against an R-served tree to isolate the client behavior): get_vector(http_daf(url),'cell','big')  # server log: ONE GET 200 of the full big.data, no Range header.
probes.expects: Julia server log shows Range/206 partial requests; R server log shows a single full-file 200 GET. Same final numeric vector, but different request protocol -> R lacks lazy/striped HTTP fetch.
probes.targets_finding: Range-GET lazy streaming of large flat dense properties (StripedVector/StripedMatrix over HTTP)

probes.description: Serve a packed (chunked+compressed) dense property and capture server access log. Julia fetches the ZIP central directory via a suffix-Range GET then per-chunk Range GETs; R downloads the whole .zip shard with one plain GET.
probes.query_or_snippet: Write a FilesDaf with packed=true so a vector/matrix is stored as <name>.zip (indexed+zipped). Serve over a logging static server. Julia: get_vector(HttpDaf(url),axis,name)  # server log: GET with 'Range: bytes=-<cd_size>' (suffix) then GET(s) with 'Range: bytes=start-end' per chunk. R: get_vector(http_daf(url),axis,name)  # server log: ONE plain GET 200 of the full <name>.zip.
probes.expects: Julia log: suffix-Range + per-chunk Range (206) requests. R log: single full-shard 200 GET. Values match; request protocol diverges. Confirms R has no partial-read packed-over-HTTP path.
probes.targets_finding: Packed (chunked+compressed ZIP-shard) dense properties served over HTTP via suffix-Range + per-chunk Range GETs

probes.description: Sparse Bool property where every nonzero is true (writer omits .nzval and its descriptor). Trace HTTP requests: Julia never requests .nzval (decides from JSON); R issues a GET that 404s.
probes.query_or_snippet: Build a sparse Bool vector on axis 'cell' that is all-true at its nonzeros (so .nzval is omitted), serve over a logging static server. Julia: get_vector(HttpDaf(url),'cell','flag')  # server log: NO request for /vectors/cell/flag.nzval. R: get_vector(http_daf(url),'cell','flag')  # server log: a GET /vectors/cell/flag.nzval returning 404 (allow_404 swallows it). Both return the same logical vector.
probes.expects: Identical returned values (all-true reconstructed). Server log differs: Julia issues zero .nzval requests; R issues one .nzval request that 404s. Exposes R's reliance on a genuine 404 (vs descriptor inspection) for all-true detection.
probes.targets_finding: All-true sparse Bool detection: descriptor-driven (Julia) vs 404-probe (R)

probes.description: Confirm R derives axes from a bundled axes/metadata.json while Julia derives them from the consolidated index keys, by serving a tree whose index has axis entries but whose axes/metadata.json is absent/empty.
probes.query_or_snippet: Construct a metadata index that contains axes/<name> entries (as Julia's metadata.json does) but where the served bundle lacks an axes/metadata.json entry. R: axes_set(http_daf(url))  # EXPECT character(0) (http_format.R:213-214 early-return). Julia equivalent (metadata.json with axes/<name> keys): axes_set(HttpDaf(url))  # EXPECT the axis names (names_under 'axes'). Concretely, since the formats diverge, the cleanest probe is: against a Julia-style metadata.json with axes, R cannot enumerate axes at all because it reads axes/metadata.json from a zip that does not exist.
probes.expects: R returns no axes when the enumeration relies on axes/metadata.json being bundled; Julia returns axes from the index keys. Demonstrates the differing enumeration source independent of the zip-vs-json wire issue.

probes.description: Open the same URL with no name kwarg and no scalars/name property; compare daf .name.
probes.query_or_snippet: Given URL 'http://host:8000/sub/data.daf' with no 'name' scalar. Julia: name(HttpDaf(url))  # EXPECT a unique_name based on the full URL 'http://host:8000/sub/data.daf' (possibly with a #N suffix). R: name(http_daf(url))  # EXPECT basename = 'data.daf'.
probes.expects: Julia name = full URL (uniquified); R name = 'data.daf'. Diverges. Also probe collision: two http_daf() from different hosts sharing basename get the same R name.

confirmed_parity: Read-only contract: both expose only read generics; both hard-error on writes. R adds an explicit format_relayout_matrix hard-error (http_format.R:583-589) which is acceptable (relayout-on-read is a write-side concern that never fires for a read-only daf through normal query paths); Julia relies on the generic read-only path. No behavioral divergence.

Scalar reads: format_has_scalar / format_get_scalar / format_scalars_set match. Both serve scalar descriptors from the consolidated metadata (Julia dict, R zip entry) and decode type+value identically per dtype (Julia descriptor_to_scalar via DTYPE_BY_NAME http_format.jl:142-153; R .http_scalar_from_json http_format.R:146-168 including bit64 for Int64/UInt64, Float32->double).

Dense numeric vector/matrix VALUES (below the striped threshold, where Julia also does a single GET): both fetch the full .data via one GET and decode little-endian per dtype; integer widths, UInt32-as-signed-int, Int64/UInt64 via bit64, Float32/Float64 as double all align (Julia bytes_to_vector + DTYPE_BY_NAME; R .http_bytes_to_dense http_format.R:252-277). Column-major reshape for matrices matches (R dim<- c(nr,nc); Julia reshape).

String dense vectors/matrices: both fetch .txt, split on \n dropping the final empty line (Julia fetch_lines http_format.jl:155-163; R .http_split_text_lines http_format.R:134-141), assert length == n (vector) or nr*nc (matrix), and reshape column-major for matrices.

Sparse string vector/matrix scatter: both reconstruct a dense character vector/matrix filled with '' and scatter .nztxt lines at nzind/colptr+rowval positions in the same column-major order (Julia http_format.jl:279-284, 431-446; R http_format.R:398-409, 542-564).

Sparse numeric matrix returns CSC; R uses dgCMatrix/lgCMatrix with 0-based i/p (http_format.R:530-577) which is the established dafr representation of Julia's SparseMatrixCSC. Sparse numeric VALUES, colptr length == ncols+1 assertion, and nnz = colptr[end]-1 all align.
Version acceptance predicate: both accept version exactly when major==1 and minor<=1 (Julia http_format.jl:115; R http_format.R:74), consistent with MAJOR_VERSION=1/MINOR_VERSION=1.
format_description_header: both emit 'type: HttpDaf' and 'url: <url>' (Julia http_format.jl:556-566; R http_format.R:594-598). is_leaf returns TRUE on both (Julia :183-189; R :601).

URL normalization: both strip trailing slashes (Julia rstrip(url,'/') http_format.jl:108; R sub('/+$','',url) http_format.R:60) and reject non-http(s) URLs with a 'not an HTTP(S) URL' message (Julia :105-107; R :57-59). join_url single-slash policy matches R's paste0(url,'/...').

HTTP timeout/retry posture: both issue requests without retry (Julia retry=false; R req_retry(max_tries=1L)). R additionally exposes a configurable timeout (options(dafr.http_timeout) / DAFR_HTTP_TIMEOUT, default 30s, http_client.R:7-13) - an additive convenience, not a divergence in correctness.
notes:
The dominant finding is an architectural wire-protocol divergence: Julia HttpDaf serves the FilesDaf tree VERBATIM and reads a root metadata.json (single JSON object index); dafr R reads a metadata.zip bundle that the Julia codebase never produces and the Julia client never requests. Consequently the R http_daf client and the Julia HttpDaf client are NOT interoperable with each other's servers (probe http-wire-protocol-cross-read). This is by design in dafr (the R docstrings and pack_files_daf_metadata() openly document the metadata.zip approach), and it is internally consistent within the dafr ecosystem (dafr FilesDaf writer maintains metadata.zip; dafr http_daf reads it). But against the stated audit question 'Does R speak the same wire protocol as a Julia server?' the answer is clearly NO at the open path and at the all-true-Bool / large-property request layer.

Severity calibration: the cross-server incompatibility is real and would crash/error at open, but ONLY in a mixed Julia-server/R-client (or vice-versa) deployment. Within a pure-dafr deployment everything works. I classified it crash-or-error because the prompt explicitly asks whether R speaks the same wire protocol as the Julia server, and it does not.

The Range-GET / striped / packed-suffix-range gaps are perf/scaling (R still returns correct values by downloading whole files), EXCEPT they also change the assumed server capabilities: Julia's design works against a server that supports Range requests and partial reads; R's design assumes the server returns whole objects on plain GET and returns a clean 404 for absent files (used as the all-true-Bool signal). A static server that does not honor Range (Julia) or does not 404 cleanly (R) would break the respective client.

I did NOT find any silent wrong-answer in the dense/sparse numeric/string VALUE reconstruction within a pure-dafr round trip - dtype widths, bit64, Float32, column-major, CSC, all-true Bool (v1.1), and string scatter all match. The narrowed/edge items (v1.0 indtype default, v1.0 all-true Bool via 404, axes enumeration source) are low-exposure because dafr's own writer emits v1.1 and bundles axes/metadata.json; they bite mainly in cross-implementation or hand-crafted-tree scenarios.

HttpStore (zarr-over-HTTP) is a separate dafr backend with NO direct Julia http_format.jl counterpart in scope (Julia's HTTP-mode ZarrDaf path is referenced in packed_format.jl comments as 'future'); I read it for completeness and it is read-only, v3-only, consolidated-metadata-required, and also does only plain GET + HEAD (no Range). It is not part of the Julia http_format.jl public surface, so I did not score it as a parity gap, but it confirms the no-Range-GET observation extends across all of dafr's HTTP code.

missing_in_r.name: ZarrDaf packed=true write encoding (sharded ZEP-0002 dual-format shards)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia ZarrDaf(path, mode; packed::Bool=false) plus per-call packed kwargs on set_*!/empty_*! write properties at/above DAF_PACKED_TARGET_CHUNK_KB as v3 sharded arrays (sharding_indexed codec, blosc/zstd/gzip inner codec, dual ZIP+Zarr framing, daf_packed_format attr). dafr R has NO write-side packing at all: set_scalar/set_vector/set_matrix have no `packed` argument, zarr_daf() has no `packed` argument, and .zarr_write_dense_array always writes a single flat uncompressed `bytes`/`vlen-utf8` chunk (R/zarr_format.R:314-321, R/zarr_v3.R:67-93). R/zarr_sharded.R + R/files_packed.R are READ-ONLY. This is a DELIBERATE, documented design decision (dev/notes/2026-06-09-zarr-v3-followups-kickoff.md: 'read packed stores; NEVER write packed; CRAN-safe'), so it is a narrowing rather than a bug. Cross-format result fidelity is preserved (R always writes the flat form, which Julia reads). Impact: a Julia store written with packed=true round-trips through R as a flat store; on-disk encoding differs but read values match.
missing_in_r.julia_evidence: zarr_format.jl:394-432 (packed kwarg), :880-908 (dense_zcreate -> sharded_zcreate when chunks_for != nothing), :919-941 (write_packed_shard!), :1948-1996 (packed_streaming_dense_matrix)

missing_in_r.name: Multi-daf ZIP sub-group addressing (.dafs.zarr.zip#/group)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia parse_zarr_path supports three forms incl. `foo.dafs.zarr.zip#/group` to address one of several Daf data sets stored in sub-groups of a single ZIP archive, and rejects cardinality near-misses (a `#/group` on a `.daf.zarr.zip`, or a bare `.dafs.zarr.zip` with no group) with explicit errors. dafr R zarr_daf() unconditionally STRIPS any `#...` fragment (R/zarr_format.R:94 `zip_path <- sub('#.*$', '', uri)`) and opens the archive at its ROOT. There is no `.dafs.zarr.zip` plural form and no sub-group selection. If the archive holds sub-dafs with no root `daf` marker, R errors 'not a valid ZarrDaf store'; if a root daf happens to exist, R silently opens that instead of the requested sub-group.

missing_in_r.name: zarr_to_files / files_to_zarr hard-link (zero-copy) conversion preserving packed + sparse-vector encoding
missing_in_r.detail: Julia ZarrConvert hard-links every numeric blob (dense chunks and colptr/rowval/nzind/nzval) and re-serializes only metadata + string properties, so the converted store is byte-identical in numeric payload and PRESERVES packed/sharded encoding and the exact sparse layout (incl. sparse VECTORS as nzind/nzval child arrays). dafr's files_to_zarr/zarr_to_files walk the DafReader/DafWriter API and RE-WRITE everything through set_*/get_* (R/zarr_convert.R:114-141; the docstring states 'correctness-first... re-written through the regular set_* API rather than hard-linked'). Consequences: (1) packed source -> always flat destination (R has no packed write); (2) a sparse-on-disk VECTOR is densified by get_vector (.zarr_get_sparse_vector R/zarr_format.R:611-653 returns a dense atomic vector) and rewritten DENSE in the destination, whereas Julia keeps it sparse; (3) dtype width is collapsed (see divergence 'dtype width not preserved on write'). Sparse MATRICES stay sparse in both. The same-filesystem hard-link probe is kept in R purely as a guard, so the API can later gain the optimization.

missing_in_r.name: Reorder crash-recovery (hardlink backup / replace / reset / lock)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia ZarrDaf implements the full crash-safe reorder protocol: format_lock_reorder! creates a .reorder.backup/ dir, format_backup_reorder! recursive-hardlinks the affected axis/vector/matrix subtrees, format_replace_reorder! ticks a crash counter, format_reset_reorder! restores from the backup on a crashed reorder, format_cleanup_reorder! removes the backup (zarr_format.jl:2308-2628). dafr R does a best-effort in-place reorder with NO on-disk backup: format_reset_reorder always returns FALSE and format_replace_reorder mutates in place (R/zarr_format.R:1147-1223, comment: 'No on-disk crash recovery yet... a crash mid-reorder leaves the store in an undefined state'). A crash mid-reorder is unrecoverable in R; Julia recovers.

narrowed.name: HTTP packed/flat read uses whole-blob GET, not Range-GET per inner chunk / per stripe
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia's HTTP backend reads sharded arrays via per-inner-chunk Range-GETs (http_packed_array -> PackedDenseArray, zarr_format.jl:1380-1396) and flat above-threshold arrays via column-tile striped Range-GETs (try_http_striped_vector/matrix, :1356-1378), so a slice fetches only the bytes it needs. dafr's HttpStore.store_get_bytes fetches the ENTIRE chunk/shard file over one HTTP GET (R/http_store.R:124-131), then decodes in memory via the same flat/sharded code path. Values are identical; only the network access pattern differs (whole-object vs partial). Perf-only narrowing; for large remote matrices the R path transfers far more bytes.

narrowed.name: get_vector on a sparse-on-disk vector returns dense, not a SparseVector
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia format_get_vector on a sparse vector returns a SparseVector (or LazySparseVector for lazy sources), preserving sparsity to the caller (zarr_format.jl:1843-1855). dafr densifies it to a named atomic vector at the read boundary (.zarr_get_sparse_vector, R/zarr_format.R:611-653; also .attach_vector_axis_names densifies sparseVector). This is a deliberate dafr-wide convention (get_vector contract = 'named atomic vector'), shared with FilesDaf, not zarr-specific; values match, representation does not. Drives divergence #3 (convert densifies sparse vectors).

divergences.name: Numeric dtype WIDTH not preserved on R write (Float32/Int8/Int16/UInt*/Int collapse to float64/int32)
divergences.julia_behavior: Julia preserves the exact element type on write: dense_zcreate(eltype(vector)/typeof(value), ...) emits a v3 data_type via Zarr.typestr3(T), so a Float32 vector stays 'float32', Int8 stays 'int8', Int16 'int16', UInt8 'uint8', etc. zarr_format.jl:895-908, :1681. zarr_to_files/files_to_zarr round-trip the exact type via DTYPE_BY_NAME.
divergences.r_behavior: zarr_v3_dtype_for_r (R/zarr_v3.R:14-22) maps ALL R integer vectors -> 'int32' and ALL non-integer numerics -> 'float64' (only integer64 -> int64, logical -> bool, character -> string). R has no Float32/Int8/Int16/UInt type, so any narrow-typed property written through dafr is stored WIDER than Julia would. Reading a Julia-written narrow array widens losslessly to double/integer (R/zarr_v3.R:330-351 supports float32/int8-16/uint8-32/uint64 on READ), but on rewrite the width is lost. Round-trip Julia->R->store: float32 matrix becomes float64; int8/int16/uint8/uint16/uint32 vector becomes int32 (uint32 may even widen to double for values >= 2^31, R/zarr_v3.R:340-345). Data VALUES are identical; the on-disk data_type string and byte width differ, so a strict Julia reader sees a different (wider) type than it wrote. This is silent.
divergences.evidence: R/zarr_v3.R:14-22 (write mapping) vs zarr_format.jl:895-908; read-side widths R/zarr_v3.R:25-48,330-351

divergences.name: int64/uint64 NON-bool sparse nzval narrowed to double on read (lossy > 2^53)
divergences.julia_behavior: Julia reads a sparse vector/matrix nzval array at its true element type; an int64/uint64-valued sparse property keeps full 64-bit integer precision in the returned SparseVector/SparseMatrixCSC (zarr_format.jl:1847-1861, :2219-2228).
divergences.r_behavior: .zarr_get_sparse_vector / .zarr_get_sparse_matrix read non-bool nzval and coerce to double for the dgCMatrix / numeric output (R/zarr_format.R:639-651, :929-950). bit64 integer64 nzval is narrowed to double, so values above 2^53 lose precision. dafr's own writer only ever writes float/int32/int64-bit64/bool nzval, but a Julia-written int64-valued sparse (now reachable via packed read too) reads back lossy. Documented as an open follow-up in dev/notes/2026-06-09-zarr-v3-followups-kickoff.md:165-167. Rare in practice (DAF sparse values are realistically float/bool).
divergences.evidence: R/zarr_format.R:639-651,929-950 vs zarr_format.jl:1847-1861

divergences.name: All-fill (all-zero) dense chunk: Julia may elide the chunk file; R errors on a missing chunk
divergences.julia_behavior: Julia notes that Zarr's pipeline 'elides writes when every cell equals fill_value = zero(T)' (zarr_format.jl:1703-1704,1768,2070), which is why the empty_* paths POKE the last element so the chunk materialises. A regular set_vector!/set_matrix! with an all-zero dense array goes through write_dense_data! -> setindex! WITHOUT a poke; if Zarr.jl elides the all-fill chunk, no c/0 file is written and the reader reconstructs an all-zero array from fill_value. (Needs empirical confirmation of Zarr.jl 0.10 setindex! elision behavior.)
divergences.r_behavior: dafr ALWAYS writes the chunk via store_set_bytes (R/zarr_format.R:314-321), and on READ a missing chunk is a hard error: .zarr_get_vector stop('vector ... missing chunk') (R/zarr_format.R:600-604) and .zarr_get_dense_matrix stop('matrix at ... missing chunk') (:894-897). If a Julia-written store omitted an all-fill dense chunk file, dafr would ERROR rather than return zeros. (R's own stores never trigger this since R always writes the chunk; only the R-reads-Julia direction is exposed, and only if Zarr.jl elides.)
divergences.evidence: R/zarr_format.R:600-604,894-897 vs zarr_format.jl:1703-1704; elision is a Zarr.jl behavior not directly readable from this repo

probes.description: Write a Float32 dense matrix in Julia, read+rewrite via R, then inspect the on-disk data_type. Julia stores 'float32'; after an R set_matrix the data_type is 'float64'. Confirms width collapse.
probes.query_or_snippet: Julia: d=ZarrDaf("f32.daf.zarr","w+"); add_axis!(d,"r",["r1","r2"]); add_axis!(d,"c",["c1","c2"]); set_matrix!(d,"r","c","m",Float32[1 2; 3 4]); then read matrices/r/c/m/zarr.json -> data_type == "float32". R: z<-zarr_daf("f32.daf.zarr","r"); m<-get_matrix(z,"r","c","m"); storage.mode(m) is 'double' (lossless). Now R write: z2<-zarr_daf("f32b.daf.zarr","w"); add_axis(z2,"r",c("r1","r2")); add_axis(z2,"c",c("c1","c2")); set_matrix(z2,"r","c","m",matrix(c(1,2,3,4),2,2)); jsonlite::fromJSON(rawToChar(store_get_bytes(S7::prop(z2,'store'),'matrices/r/c/m/zarr.json')))$data_type == "float64".
probes.expects: Julia on-disk data_type='float32'; R-written data_type='float64'. Values equal; dtype string differs.
probes.targets_finding: dtype WIDTH not preserved on R write

probes.description: Write an Int8 (and UInt8/Int16) dense vector in Julia; verify R reads correct values but cannot reproduce the narrow data_type on rewrite (becomes int32).
probes.query_or_snippet: Julia: set_vector!(d,"cell","u8",UInt8[0,255,7]) -> data_type 'uint8'. R read: get_vector(z,"cell","u8") returns c(0,255,7) as integer (correct). R rewrite of any integer vector -> data_type 'int32'. Edge: a uint32 value >= 2^31 read by R returns a DOUBLE (R/zarr_v3.R:340-345), so get_vector type differs from a Julia Int read.
probes.expects: Values correct on read; on-disk data_type 'uint8'/'int16' unreproducible by R writer; uint32 high values surface as R double not integer.
probes.targets_finding: dtype WIDTH not preserved on R write

probes.description: Open a .dafs.zarr.zip#/group path in R; confirm the fragment is stripped and the sub-group is not addressed.
probes.query_or_snippet: R: zarr_daf("multi.dafs.zarr.zip#/g1", mode="r") — R strips '#/g1' (R/zarr_format.R:94) and opens at archive root; if there is no root daf marker it errors 'not a valid ZarrDaf store', whereas Julia ZarrDaf("multi.dafs.zarr.zip#/g1") opens sub-daf g1. (Also test bare "multi.dafs.zarr.zip": Julia errors 'group required'; R treats it as a single-root zip.)
probes.expects: R cannot open a sub-daf inside a multi-daf zip; Julia can. R either errors (no root daf) or silently opens the wrong daf (root daf present).

probes.description: Round-trip a sparse vector through R's files<->zarr convert; confirm it lands DENSE in the destination, whereas Julia keeps it sparse (nzind/nzval child arrays).
probes.query_or_snippet: Create a daf with a sparse vector (e.g. a SparseVector with 3 nonzeros over a length-1000 axis). Julia files_to_zarr: destination vectors/<axis>/<name>/zarr.json node_type=='group' (nzind/nzval present). R files_to_zarr(src,dst): destination vectors/<axis>/<name>/zarr.json node_type=='array' (dense), no nzind/nzval. Inspect via store_get_bytes(...,'vectors/<axis>/<name>/zarr.json').
probes.expects: Julia destination = sparse group; R destination = dense array. Values equal; on-disk layout differs (sparse->dense).
probes.targets_finding: convert re-writes through set_* and densifies sparse vectors

probes.description: Convert a packed (sharded) Julia ZarrDaf to FilesDaf via R; confirm the destination is FLAT, whereas Julia hard-links the dual-format shard.
probes.query_or_snippet: Julia: write a store with packed=true so a dense matrix is a sharded array (matrices/.../<name>/c/0/0 shard, zarr.json codecs[1].name=='sharding_indexed'). R zarr_to_files(src,dst): destination matrix descriptor is flat (FilesDaf .data, format 'dense', no packed_format). Julia zarr_to_files would hard-link the .zip shard with packed_format 'indexed+zipped'. Inspect dst matrix .json.
probes.expects: R destination flat-encoded (no packed_format); Julia destination retains the packed shard. Values equal; encoding differs.
probes.targets_finding: convert does not preserve packed encoding

probes.description: If a Julia-written all-zero dense vector elides its c/0 chunk file (Zarr fill-value optimization), confirm dafr errors instead of returning zeros.
probes.query_or_snippet: Construct (or simulate) a v3 array node vectors/cell/zeros with a valid zarr.json but NO c/0 chunk file (fill_value=0.0). dafr: get_vector(z,"cell","zeros") -> stop('vector ... missing chunk') (R/zarr_format.R:600-604). Julia: returns fill(0.0, n). First confirm empirically whether Julia set_vector! of an all-zero Float64 vector actually omits c/0 under Zarr.jl 0.10; if it always writes the chunk, this divergence is unreachable in practice.
probes.expects: If Julia omits the all-fill chunk: dafr errors, Julia returns zeros. If Julia always writes it: parity holds (probe is a no-op).
probes.targets_finding: all-fill dense chunk elision vs missing-chunk error

probes.description: Read a sparse property whose nzval is int64 with a value > 2^53; confirm dafr narrows to double (precision loss) while Julia keeps Int64.
probes.query_or_snippet: Julia: build a SparseVector{Int64} with a nonzero value 9007199254740993 (2^53+1), set_vector!. R: get_vector(z,axis,name)[idx] returns a double != 9007199254740993 exactly (rounds). Julia get_vector returns the exact Int64.
probes.expects: R value loses the low bit (precision loss above 2^53); Julia exact.
probes.targets_finding: int64/uint64 non-bool sparse nzval narrowed to double on read

confirmed_parity: Flat (uncompressed) v3 on-disk layout: per-node zarr.json, lowercase v3 dtype names, c/-prefixed chunk keys (c/0, c/0/0), root-group `daf:[1,0]` attribute, four container groups scalars/axes/vectors/matrices (R/zarr_v3.R, R/zarr_format.R:213-220 vs zarr_format.jl:774-798).

Dense matrix shape is stored REVERSED [n_cols, n_rows] with column-major chunk bytes; R reads nr=shape[2], nc=shape[1] and fills dim=c(nr,nc) directly, matching the Julia/Zarr C-order-over-reversed-shape convention (R/zarr_format.R:872-906 vs zarr_format.jl:181-191).

Sparse vector layout: group with nzind (int64, 1-based) + nzval child arrays; all-true Bool sparse omits the nzval child and is inferred from its absence (R/zarr_format.R:734-760 vs zarr_format.jl:1735-1748).

Sparse matrix layout: group with colptr/rowval (int64, 1-based) + nzval; +1/-1 base conversion vs R's 0-based @p/@i; all-true Bool omits nzval (R/zarr_format.R:1031-1064,908-951 vs zarr_format.jl:2021-2038).

vlen-utf8 string encoding (numcodecs wire format: u32 count, then per-string u32 len + UTF-8 bytes); strings via the `string` data_type + vlen-utf8 codec (R/zarr_v3.R:356-403 vs zarr_format.jl:319-345).
Inline consolidated_metadata at root: kind='inline', must_understand=false, metadata = {path: node-zarr.json}, omitted on MmapZip backend (R/zarr_v3.R:200-274 vs zarr_format.jl:86-124,1126-1199).
Zarr v2 store rejection on open with the `python -m zarr v2_to_v3` hint (R/zarr_format.R:179-191 vs zarr_format.jl:755-762).
Format version verify: reject major mismatch or minor > supported (R/zarr_format.R:195-209 vs zarr_format.jl:800-819).

Packed/sharded READ: sharding_indexed codec detection, start-located shard index (N*16 bytes + crc32c, warn-not-fail), inner gzip/blosc/zstd decode, 1-D and 2-D reassembly, vlen-utf8 sharded strings, per-component sparse sharding (R/zarr_sharded.R vs zarr_format.jl read paths + packed_format).

HTTP read backend: requires inline consolidated_metadata, read-only, rejects v2, serves node metadata from the consolidated index and chunks lazily; rejects mode != 'r' (R/http_store.R, R/zarr_format.R:80-86 vs zarr_format.jl:573-638).
MmapZip backend is append-only: deletion/overwrite of properties errors; consolidated metadata omitted (R/zarr_store.R:300-307, R/zarr_v3.R:228-229 vs zarr_format.jl:2240-2243, :1027-1048).
mmap zero-copy fast path for flat single-chunk float64/int32 dense arrays on the directory store (R/zarr_format.R:558-568 vs zarr_format.jl:1251-1299,1511-1525).
In-memory backend (DictStore / Julia DictStore) and directory backend selection by path suffix; :memory: maps to DictStore (R/zarr_format.R:73-134 vs zarr_format.jl:640-684).
notes:
Audit scope: Julia zarr_format.jl (2638 lines) + zarr_convert.jl + their .md docs vs dafr R zarr_format.R, zarr_store.R, zarr_v3.R, zarr_sharded.R, zarr_convert.R, http_store.R.

Headline: the flat v3 read+write core is at strong parity (interop is live-tested in tests/testthat/test-zarr-julia-interop.R). The real gaps cluster in (a) write-side encoding richness and (b) conversion fidelity.

Most consequential SILENT divergence: numeric dtype WIDTH is not preserved on R write (Float32/Int8/Int16/UInt*->float64/int32), because R has no narrow numeric types. Values are correct; the on-disk data_type string and byte width change after any R write or R-mediated convert. This is the one a differential harness should hammer (probes zarr-dtype-float32-roundtrip, zarr-dtype-int8-roundtrip). It is NOT mentioned in the zarr-v3-followups kickoff doc (which only tracks the int64-sparse-nzval narrowing) — likely missed by prior parity work.

Deliberate, documented narrowings (NOT bugs): no packed write, packed read only (dev/notes/2026-06-09-zarr-v3-followups-kickoff.md); convert re-writes through set_* instead of hard-linking (R/zarr_convert.R docstring); no reorder crash recovery (R/zarr_format.R:1147-1153 comment). I flagged these as missing-feature/semantic-edge so the harness can confirm the resulting encoding differences, but they do not corrupt values in the R->R or R-writes/Julia-reads directions.

Two findings need empirical confirmation I could not do read-only: (1) whether Zarr.jl 0.10 setindex! actually elides an all-fill dense chunk on a regular set_vector! (probe zarr-all-zero-dense-missing-chunk) — if it never elides, that crash-or-error divergence is unreachable; (2) exact Julia on-disk data_type for each narrow type via Zarr.typestr3 (assumed lowercase 'float32'/'int8'/etc., consistent with R's read-side acceptance list).

Pre-existing tracked note reconfirmed: int64/uint64 non-bool sparse nzval narrows to double on read (now reachable via packed read too).

narrowed.name: complete_chain relative-path construction
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia uses relpath(base_path, dirname(new_path)) which produces a correct relative path for any layout including sibling/parent traversal (e.g. '../base'). dafr's manual construction (complete.R:44-54) only handles base==new-parent ('.') and base-under-new-parent (strip prefix); for any other layout it falls back to storing the ABSOLUTE base path, defeating the move/rename portability goal of relative storage. Resolves correctly when reopened but the stored value differs from Julia and is non-portable. (This is the CompleteDaf subsystem, only adjacent to chains.)

narrowed.name: chain shallow description() output
narrowed.what_is_missing: No format_description_header/footer method exists for ReadOnlyChainDaf/WriteChainDaf, so a chain falls through to the default DafReader header. Even at the shallow (non-deep) level this diverges: dafr renders 'type: ReadOnlyChainDaf'/'type: WriteChainDaf' and OMITS the 'chain:' member-listing section entirely, whereas Julia renders 'type: ReadOnly Chain'/'type: Write Chain' AND a 'chain:' section listing each member's brief() even when deep=false (chains.jl:807-831). The team's divergence note (C2) claims the shallow/!deep output 'happens to match' Julia - that is inaccurate; the type label and the chain listing differ at every depth.

divergences.name: relayout_matrix on a chain mutates the writer with a copy of base data
divergences.julia_behavior: format_relayout_matrix!(chain,...) finds the matrix in the first (reverse) daf that has it. If that daf is read-only (the common base case), it computes the flipped matrix and stores it ONLY in the per-daf cache (get_slow_through_cache), returning a transposed NamedArray view. No daf is mutated; the writer is untouched (chains.jl:685-715).
divergences.r_behavior: format_relayout_matrix(WriteChainDaf,...) when the writer lacks the matrix finds it in an earlier daf, then COPIES it into the writer via format_set_matrix(writer, rows, cols, name, m, TRUE) and relayouts there, also auto-adding the axes to the writer. After the call the writer physically contains BOTH orientations of the base matrix (chain_daf.R:620-652). Observable: matrices_set(writer_alone, rows, cols) gains the matrix; the base copy now lives durably in the writer and survives even if the base later changes. Uncovered by both the Julia and dafr chain test suites.
divergences.evidence: chains.jl:695-714 (read-only branch returns flipped cache, no write) vs chain_daf.R:640-651 (format_set_matrix into writer)

divergences.name: read_only(daf) result name lacks the .read_only suffix
divergences.julia_behavior: read_only(daf::DafReader; name=nothing) sets name = daf.name * '.read_only' then unique_name(...) (read_only.jl:42-46); read_only(read-only daf) with a name rewraps. Propagates to chain_reader singleton (chains.jl:84).
divergences.r_behavior: read_only(daf, name=NULL) uses name = daf.name verbatim (chain_daf.R:124), so daf_name(read_only(d)) == 'inner' instead of Julia's 'inner.read_only'. dafr intentionally tests the bare name (test-class-sugar.R:38), so it is a deliberate-but-real observable divergence; also affects the name of a singleton chain_reader.
divergences.evidence: read_only.jl:42-46 vs chain_daf.R:117-127; test-class-sugar.R:38

divergences.name: chain constructors do not unwrap read_only wrappers into the dafs vector
divergences.julia_behavior: reader_internal_dafs unwraps any DafReadOnlyWrapper to its inner .daf before pushing into the chain's dafs (chains.jl:200-204), so the stored member and its name are the underlying daf (e.g. 'second!').
divergences.r_behavior: chain_reader/chain_writer store the ReadOnlyChainDaf wrapper produced by read_only() directly in dafs with no unwrapping. Because dafr's read_only preserves the inner name by default the common case is invisible, but if a member is read_only(x, name='custom') the chain's deletion error 'because it exists in the earlier: <name>' (and any per-member name use) shows the wrapper name, not the inner daf's name as Julia would. Also adds an extra indirection layer per read.
divergences.evidence: chains.jl:200-204 vs chain_daf.R:62-83,140-180 (no unwrap step)

divergences.name: version-counter sum guards on axis existence
divergences.julia_behavior: format_get_version_counter sums format_get_version_counter over every chained daf unconditionally (chains.jl:858-864), so a daf whose axis was deleted but whose counter is nonzero still contributes.
divergences.r_behavior: vector_version_counter/matrix_version_counter/stamps add a per-source `if format_has_axis(d, axis)` guard before summing (cache.R:144-179,225-270), so a source lacking the axis contributes 0. Differs only in the rare deleted-axis-with-nonzero-counter edge; harmless for cache invalidation in practice.
divergences.evidence: chains.jl:858-864 vs cache.R:225-270

probes.description: Build a write chain [base, writer] where matrix M lives only in the read-only base at (cell,gene). Call relayout_matrix on the chain, then inspect the writer in isolation. Julia leaves the writer empty (relayout is an ephemeral cached transpose); dafr copies M into the writer so writer now physically holds both (cell,gene) and (gene,cell) layouts.
probes.query_or_snippet: R: base<-memory_daf(name='base'); add_axis(base,'cell',c('A','B')); add_axis(base,'gene',c('X','Y','Z')); set_matrix(base,'cell','gene','UMIs',matrix(c(0L,3L,1L,4L,2L,5L),2,3)); w<-memory_daf(name='w'); ch<-chain_writer(list(read_only(base),w),name='ch'); relayout_matrix(ch,'cell','gene','UMIs'); list(writer_cellgene=matrices_set(w,'cell','gene'), writer_genecell=matrices_set(w,'gene','cell')) ## Julia: base<-MemoryDaf(name="base"); add_axis!(base,"cell",["A","B"]); add_axis!(base,"gene",["X","Y","Z"]); set_matrix!(base,"cell","gene","UMIs",[0 1 2;3 4 5]); w=MemoryDaf(name="w"); ch=chain_writer([read_only(base),w];name="ch"); relayout_matrix!(ch,"cell","gene","UMIs"); (matrices_set(w,"cell","gene"), matrices_set(w,"gene","cell"))
probes.expects: Julia: writer w has NO matrices at either (cell,gene) or (gene,cell) -- both sets empty. dafr: writer w now contains 'UMIs' at both (cell,gene) AND (gene,cell). Divergence on whether the writer is mutated.
probes.targets_finding: relayout_matrix on a chain mutates the writer with a copy of base data

probes.description: Compare the name of read_only(d) and of a singleton chain_reader.
probes.query_or_snippet: R: d<-memory_daf(name='inner'); daf_name(read_only(d)) ## Julia: d=MemoryDaf(name="inner"); read_only(d).name
probes.expects: Julia: 'inner.read_only' (possibly with a unique '#N' suffix). dafr: 'inner'.

probes.description: Put a renamed read_only wrapper as an earlier chain member that also holds a scalar, then trigger the delete-blocked error and inspect which member name appears.
probes.query_or_snippet: R: b<-memory_daf(name='base'); set_scalar(b,'v',1); ro<-read_only(b,name='ALIAS'); w<-memory_daf(name='w'); ch<-chain_writer(list(ro,w),name='ch'); tryCatch(delete_scalar(ch,'v'), error=function(e) conditionMessage(e)) ## Julia: b=MemoryDaf(name="base"); set_scalar!(b,"v",1); ro=read_only(b;name="ALIAS"); w=MemoryDaf(name="w"); ch=chain_writer([ro,w];name="ch"); try; delete_scalar!(ch,"v"); catch e; sprint(showerror,e); end

probes.description: Render description() of a write chain and inspect the type line and presence of a 'chain:' member listing at the default (shallow) depth.
probes.query_or_snippet: R: f<-memory_daf(name='first'); s<-memory_daf(name='second'); ch<-chain_writer(list(f,s),name='ch'); cat(description(ch)) ## Julia: f=MemoryDaf(name="first"); s=MemoryDaf(name="second"); ch=chain_writer([f,s];name="ch"); print(description(ch))
