probes.description: Create base and new FilesDaf under a common root that are SIBLINGS, then complete_chain (relative) and read the stored base_daf_repository scalar to compare the stored relative path.
probes.query_or_snippet: R: root<-tempfile(); dir.create(root); bd<-file.path(root,'base'); nd<-file.path(root,'new'); dir.create(bd); dir.create(nd); base<-files_daf(bd,name='base',mode='w+'); new<-files_daf(nd,name='new',mode='w+'); complete_chain(base_daf=base,new_daf=new); get_scalar(new,'base_daf_repository') ## Julia equivalent with FilesDaf + complete_chain! then get_scalar(new,"base_daf_repository")
probes.expects: complete_path(FilesDaf) returns the daf directory, so dirname(new_path) is the common root; both Julia and dafr should store 'base'. If dafr's complete_path returns the parent differently, dafr may instead store the absolute path of base while Julia stores a clean relative path. Confirms whether the relpath fallback diverges for the sibling-under-common-root layout.

notes:
Scope: I audited chains.jl + chains.md against R/chain_daf.R (plus cache.R version-counter chain paths, complete.R for complete_chain, readers.R/writers.R for the public delete/relayout/description wrappers that drive the chain format methods). The public surface (chain_reader, chain_writer, complete_chain!, ReadOnlyChain/WriteChain) is fully present and the core precedence/override/delete-across-layers/which-layer-a-write-lands-in semantics are at strong parity, including identical 'because it exists in the earlier' delete-block error wording.

ALREADY-DOCUMENTED divergences (in dev/notes/2026-05-07-chains-jl-parity-divergences.md and guarded by skip() in test-chains-jl-parity.R) - I did NOT re-list these as new findings: C1 singleton identity (now actually FIXED by commit c582c2a; the note is stale), C2 description(deep) (but see my 'chain shallow description' narrowed item - the note's claim that shallow output matches is wrong), C3 no empty_dense_*/empty_sparse_* two-phase builder API (this is a Formats-internal write protocol, not user-facing public surface, so I did not treat it as a chains gap), C5 complete_path errors on memory-backed chains, T1 error text single-line vs Julia multi-line chomp blocks, T2 Set vs sorted character vector.

GENUINELY MISSED (not in the note): (1) the relayout_matrix-on-chain writer-mutation divergence is the highest-value finding - it is silently wrong (writer gets polluted with a durable copy of base data) and is exercised by NEITHER test suite; (2) read_only naming suffix; (3) no unwrapping of read_only wrappers in chain constructors; (4) shallow description type-label + missing chain: listing; (5) version-counter axis-existence guard edge.

Architectural notes that are NOT gaps: dafr's format API is single-phase (format_set_vector/format_set_matrix) with no format_get_empty_*/format_filled_empty_* and no is_packed concept - this is a deliberate whole-port choice, harmless for chains. dafr's format_has_axis has no for_change kwarg; Julia chains reset for_change=false after the first daf (chains.jl:359) but leaf backends ignore for_change (only affects require_axis message phrasing), so dropping it is cosmetic. dafr has no brief() (TanayLabUtilities concept), so the Julia chain test's brief(chain)=='ReadOnly Chain chain!' assertion has no analog - out of scope. dafr read_only builds a 1-element ReadOnlyChainDaf with its own cache env rather than a DafReadOnlyWrapper sharing the inner internal/cache; cache identity differs but is internal.

missing_in_r.name: Tensor (3D) views (TensorKey 4-tuple keys + tensor rollup)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia views.jl supports TensorKey = (main_axis, rows_axis, columns_axis, name) 4-tuple keys in `data` (reversed_view_tensors, collect_view_tensor, prepare/fetch_matrix_query tensor branch, lines 314-340, 623-647, 762-786, 893-909, 1045-1088). A tensor key like ("batch","cell","gene","is_measured") => "=" exposes the per-main-axis-entry matrices batch1_is_measured, batch2_is_measured, ... and validates the main axis is exposed (error 'hidden tensor main axis'). Julia restricts tensor query to "="/nothing and forbids "*" wildcards in tensor keys (errors 'unsupported tensor wildcard'/'unsupported tensor query'). dafr's view_daf.R has ZERO tensor handling: .parse_view_item only accepts 1/2/3-element keys; a 4-element key falls through .resolve_view_matrices' `length(parsed$key)==3` guard and is silently ignored (no error, no exposure). Already documented as V1 but the doc understates it: it is not only a description()/rollup gap, the 4-tuple key itself is silently dropped.
missing_in_r.julia_evidence: views.jl:141 (TensorKey in ViewDatum), :314-340 (tensor key parse+validation), :623-647 (is_identity_matrix tensor branch), :1045-1088 (collect_view_tensor)

missing_in_r.name: __rows_axis__ / __columns_axis__ placeholders in matrix view queries
missing_in_r.detail: Julia prepare_matrix_query (views.jl:1164-1170) patches the user matrix query, replacing `__rows_axis__` with the rows-axis query and `__columns_axis__` with the columns-axis query (analogous to __axis__ for vectors). dafr's .view_query_for_matrix (view_daf.R:579-601) does NO substitution: it only handles the bare `:: ...` auto-prefix case. A view matrix query like ("obs","var","x") => "@ __rows_axis__ @ gene :: UMIs" is passed verbatim to the R parser, which treats `__rows_axis__` as a literal axis name and errors. The vector `__axis__` placeholder IS handled in R (gsub at view_daf.R:570), but the matrix dual placeholders are entirely absent.

narrowed.name: Partial-wildcard data keys with `=` ( (axis,"*")=>"=", ("*",name)=>"=", and matrix (axis,"*",name)=>"=" etc.)
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia collect_view_vector/collect_view_matrix EXPAND partial wildcards: ("cell","*")=>"=" exposes every vector of cell; ("*","age")=>"=" exposes `age` on every exposed axis; ("cell","*","UMIs")=>"=" / ("*","*","UMIs")=>"=" expose that matrix across all matching axes (views.jl:968-973, 1003-1023). In dafr, when an explicit `data` list is given (strict-include mode, nothing seeded), the (axis,"*") and ("*",name) branches with q=="=" do NOTHING (view_daf.R:371-372 'Identity already the default', :386-387), and the matrix partial-wildcard q=="=" branch also does nothing (view_daf.R:466-470). Result: these explicit partial-wildcard includes expose ZERO data in R, where Julia exposes the expanded set. Only the full ("*","*")/("*","*","*") => "=" forms work in R (they call seed_all()). Not covered by the existing V2/V3 divergence notes, which only address full wildcards and the seed-default policy.

narrowed.name: NamedTuple / multi-field named-list spec form for axes and data
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia ViewAxes/ViewData = Union{AbstractVector, NamedTuple}; a NamedTuple like (cell="=", gene="=") is converted via named_tuple_as_pairs (views.jl:100,152,241-242). The natural R analog is a single multi-entry named list axes=list(cell="=", gene="="). dafr's viewer iterates `for (item in axes)` and .parse_view_item only accepts a 1-element named list or a 2-element unnamed list (view_daf.R:515-524); a multi-entry named list is iterated element-wise, dropping the names, so this convenience form is unsupported. Cosmetic in practice since the list-of-pairs form works.

narrowed.name: Identity fast-path / representation & names preservation (is_pure_axes/is_identity_*)
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia short-circuits identity views: format_get_vector/format_get_matrix/format_axis_vector call the BASE format_* directly and wrap read_only_array (views.jl:432-437, 460-466, 504-510), preserving sparse/packed storage, names, and avoiding the query engine. format_is_packed_vector/matrix also delegate to the base for identity slots (views.jl:468-475, 512-524). dafr has NO identity fast-path: every view access goes through get_query(base, '@ axis : name') + raw[idx] subsetting (view_daf.R format_get_vector/matrix), which materializes/may densify sparse data, can lose the packed flag, and is materially slower. The .md explicitly frames views as cheap lazy wrappers; the R subset-after-full-query model defeats that for large matrices.

narrowed.name: Lazy evaluation contract (queries evaluated only on access)
narrowed.what_is_missing: views.md: 'These queries are evaluated only when data is actually accessed. Therefore, creating a view is a relatively cheap operation.' Julia stores the (reversed) view specs and resolves queries lazily in fetch_*_query. dafr's viewer() EAGERLY evaluates at construction: .resolve_view_axis_renames calls query_axis_name on every axis query, and .resolve_view_axis_indices calls get_query(daf, q) and format_axis_array for every non-identity axis (view_daf.R:213-256). So constructing a view over many/large masked axes runs all axis queries up front, and any axis-query error surfaces at construction time rather than access time (the latter is partly captured as T1, but the perf/laziness aspect is broader).

divergences.name: __axis__ substituted as axis NAME, not the masked axis QUERY (cardinality-dependent ops give wrong answers)
divergences.julia_behavior: prepare_vector_query patches __axis__ with the full axis QUERY sequence (views.jl:1132-1133): for a masked axis cell=>'@ cell [ batch = V ]', __axis__ becomes '@ cell [ batch = V ]', so the vector query is computed over only the masked entries.
divergences.r_behavior: .view_query_for_vector does gsub('__axis__', override$base_axis, ...) replacing __axis__ with the bare base axis NAME 'cell' (view_daf.R:570), runs the query over ALL base entries, then subsets with raw[idx]. For element-wise/per-row ops this coincides, but for any op whose result depends on the axis CARDINALITY computed inside the query (e.g. '% Fraction', a denominator Sum, mean/normalization across the axis), R uses the FULL-axis denominator and then picks a subset, while Julia uses the masked-axis denominator. Silent wrong numeric answer.
divergences.evidence: Julia views.jl:1132-1133 (patch __axis__ with axis_query); R view_daf.R:570 (gsub to base_axis name) + :712-713 (raw[idx] post-subset)

divergences.name: Same __rows_axis__/__columns_axis__/axis-query semantics for masked-axis MATRIX queries
divergences.julia_behavior: prepare_matrix_query prepends the masked rows/cols axis QUERIES (rows_axis_query |> columns_axis_query |> query, views.jl:1171-1172) or substitutes the __rows_axis__/__columns_axis__ placeholders with them, so matrix queries with cardinality-dependent ops (per-column Fraction, Sum normalization) compute over the masked axes.
divergences.r_behavior: .view_query_for_matrix prepends the bare BASE axes '@ base_rows @ base_cols' (unmasked) for the auto-prefix case (view_daf.R:597-598) and has no placeholder substitution; result is computed over full base axes then index-subset with raw[r_idx,c_idx] (view_daf.R:742-744). Same cardinality-mismatch wrong-answer class as the vector __axis__ case, plus outright parse error if __rows_axis__/__columns_axis__ is used.
divergences.evidence: Julia views.jl:1171-1172; R view_daf.R:585-600, 742-744

divergences.name: View shares base cache + version counters instead of a fresh frozen Internal
divergences.julia_behavior: DafView is built with a fresh Internal(; is_frozen = true) (views.jl:354) - its own cache, independent of the base. View query results are cached under QueryData cache group keyed within the view's own cache.
divergences.r_behavior: viewer() passes the BASE daf's cache and axis/vector/matrix version counters into the ViewDaf (view_daf.R:172-175: cache = S7::prop(daf,'cache'), *_version_counter = S7::prop(daf,...)). The view and base share one cache namespace. A view that renames/derives a property to a name that also exists on the base (e.g. view exposes scalar/vector under a name the base also uses) can collide on cache keys (scalar_cache_key/vector_cache_key are name-based), risking a stale/cross-contaminated cached value between base and view. Also view-returned data is tagged MEMORY_DATA (view_daf.R:621,661,713,744) whereas Julia tags it QueryData, changing cache-group invalidation semantics.
divergences.evidence: Julia views.jl:354 fresh Internal; R view_daf.R:172-175 shared cache/counters, :621/:744 MEMORY_DATA group

divergences.name: viewer() all-default optimization returns full ViewDaf instead of plain read-only wrapper
divergences.julia_behavior: viewer(daf) with axes===nothing && data===nothing returns read_only(daf) - a lightweight DafReadOnlyWrapper, NOT a DafView (views.jl:229-231). Documented as an explicit optimization in the docstring.
divergences.r_behavior: viewer(daf) with axes=NULL,data=NULL builds a full ViewDaf that eagerly seeds every axis/scalar/vector/matrix (view_daf.R:164-184, seed_all paths). No short-circuit to a plain read-only wrapper, so the result type and cost differ.
divergences.evidence: Julia views.jl:229-231; R view_daf.R:164-184 (no all-default branch)

probes.description: Masked axis + __axis__ vector query using a cardinality-dependent op (Fraction). Julia substitutes the masked axis query (denominator = 2 masked cells); R substitutes the bare axis name and subsets after a full-axis Fraction (denominator = 3 cells). Numeric divergence.
probes.query_or_snippet: R: d<-memory_daf(); add_axis(d,'cell',c('X','Y','Z')); set_vector(d,'cell','age',c(1,2,3)); set_vector(d,'cell','batch',c('U','V','V')); v<-viewer(d, axes=list(list('cell','@ cell [ batch = V ]')), data=list(list(c('cell','frac'),'@ __axis__ : age % Fraction'))); get_vector(v,'cell','frac')  ||  Julia: d=MemoryDaf(); add_axis!(d,"cell",["X","Y","Z"]); set_vector!(d,"cell","age",[1,2,3]); set_vector!(d,"cell","batch",["U","V","V"]); v=viewer(d; axes=["cell"=>"@ cell [ batch = V ]"], data=[("cell","frac")=>"@ __axis__ : age % Fraction"]); get_vector(v,"cell","frac")
probes.expects: Julia: age over masked {Y=2,Z=3}, Fraction => [2/5, 3/5] = [0.4, 0.6]. R (bug): Fraction over all {1,2,3} sum=6 => [2/6,3/6]=[0.333,0.5] then subset Y,Z. Values differ.
probes.targets_finding: divergence: __axis__ substituted as name not masked query

probes.description: Tensor 4-tuple key in viewer data. Julia exposes the per-main-axis matrices; R silently ignores the 4-element key (no error, no matrices).
probes.query_or_snippet: Setup base with batch axis {b1,b2}, cell, gene, and matrices b1_is_high, b2_is_high (cell x gene). R: viewer(d, data=list(list(c('batch','cell','gene','is_high'),'='))) then matrices_set(v,'cell','gene')  ||  Julia: viewer(d; data=[("batch","cell","gene","is_high")=>"="]) then matrices_set(v,"cell","gene")
probes.expects: Julia: matrices_set includes b1_is_high, b2_is_high. R: 4-tuple key dropped by .resolve_view_matrices (only handles length==3 keys) => those matrices NOT exposed (and no error).

probes.description: Partial-wildcard data include (axis,"*")=>"=" with explicit data list (strict-include mode). Julia expands to all vectors of that axis; R exposes none.
probes.query_or_snippet: R: d<-memory_daf(); add_axis(d,'cell',c('X','Y')); set_vector(d,'cell','age',c(1,2)); set_vector(d,'cell','batch',c(1,2)); v<-viewer(d, axes=list(VIEW_ALL_AXES), data=list(list(c('cell','*'),'='))); vectors_set(v,'cell')  ||  Julia: v=viewer(d; axes=[VIEW_ALL_AXES], data=[("cell","*")=>"="]); vectors_set(v,"cell")
probes.expects: Julia: {age, batch}. R: character(0) (the (axis,'*') q=='=' branch is a no-op and nothing was seeded under strict-include).

notes: The dafr view layer has clearly advanced past the 2026-05-07 divergence note (dev/notes/2026-05-07-views-jl-parity-divergences.md): V2, V3, V5(vectors), V7 are now implemented in the current view_daf.R, so that doc is stale - confirmed parity items above. The remaining real gaps are: (1) tensor views entirely missing AND 4-tuple keys silently dropped (worse than V1's 'description rollup only' framing); (2) __rows_axis__/__columns_axis__ matrix placeholders absent (V5 was only fixed for the vector __axis__ case); (3) NEW gap not in any note - explicit partial-wildcard includes like (axis,'*')=>'=' and ('*',name)=>'=' expose nothing in R (Julia expands them); (4) the highest-risk silent-wrong-answer class: R's index-subset-after-full-query model substitutes __axis__ as a bare axis NAME and prepends UNMASKED base axes, so any cardinality-dependent query op (Fraction/Sum normalization) over a masked axis computes the wrong denominator then subsets - element-wise ops coincide so existing tests (which use Sum/Abs reductions that happen to be subset-invariant) do not catch it. Architecture divergence underlying several findings: R models a view axis as an index vector into the base axis (.resolve_view_axis_indices, eager get_query at construction) rather than Julia's lazy per-access query rewriting with masked axis queries threaded through; this also breaks the documented laziness/cheap-construction contract and the identity fast-path (sparse/packed/names preservation). The shared-cache concern (view reuses base cache + version counters vs Julia's fresh frozen Internal) is a plausible cross-contamination edge worth a targeted probe but I did not fully trace R's cache-key derivation, so it is rated semantic-edge. All probes are runnable on memory_daf fixtures; VIEW-P1 and VIEW-P7 are the sharpest (numeric divergence on standard query ops).

missing_in_r.name: TensorKey expansion of `empty` in concatenate()
missing_in_r.detail: Julia concatenate! (concat.jl:153-154) runs `expand_tensors(; dafs=[destination, sources...], data=empty, ...)` BEFORE using `empty`. This means a 4-tuple TensorKey `(main_axis, rows_axis, columns_axis, matrix_name)` in `empty` is expanded against every daf's main-axis entries into a set of 3-part MatrixKeys `(rows_axis, columns_axis, "<entry>_<matrix_name>")` => value (copies.jl:737-780, EmptyData/TensorKey docs in copies.jl:628-638). R `concatenate()` (concat.R:58-150) does NO tensor expansion at all - it only ever looks up flat `empty` keys as literal "axis|name" (vectors, concat.R:217) or "rows|cols|name" / "cols|rows|name" (matrices, concat.R:279-281). dafr's own `empty_data()` builder (copies.R:601-605) WILL produce a 4-part `"main|rows|cols|name"` key, but concat never matches it. Net effect: a user supplying a tensor-style empty for a per-entry matrix group that is missing from some source gets a silent miss -> dafr raises 'no empty value for the matrix ...' where Julia fills the per-entry matrices with the tensor empty value. Note even copy_all() in R explicitly documents 'Tensors are not auto-expanded here' (copies.R:486-487), so this is a deliberate-but-unported gap, not just a concat oversight.
missing_in_r.julia_evidence: concat.jl:153-154 (expand_tensors call on empty); copies.jl:737-780 (expand_tensors body); copies.jl:628-638 (EmptyData TensorKey doc)

narrowed.name: Per-axis dense vector concatenation never produces a sparse result
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia concatenate_axis_vector (concat.jl:484-550) computes sparse_vectors_storage_fraction (concat.jl:1259-1286) and, when sparse storage saves >= sparse_if_saves_storage_fraction (default 0.25), stores the concatenated per-axis vector SPARSE (concat.jl:520-531). R's .concat_axis_vector (concat.R:208-261) always does `out <- do.call(c, parts)` followed by format_set_vector on a plain atomic vector - it never inspects source sparsity and never produces a sparse vector. The `sparse_threshold` argument is threaded into .concat_axis_vector but is unused there (no reference to it in the function body). Result: for a sparse-input or mostly-zero per-axis vector, Julia stores/returns sparse and R stores/returns dense. Values match; the stored representation and (for files_daf) on-disk format diverge. Lower practical impact than the matrix case because cell/gene vectors are usually dense, but the `sparse_if_saves_storage_fraction` parameter is silently a no-op for this path.

divergences.name: Per-axis matrix sparse-vs-dense decision ignores sparse_if_saves_storage_fraction
divergences.julia_behavior: concatenate_axis_matrix (concat.jl:671-721) computes sparse_matrices_storage_fraction (concat.jl:1288-1322) over ALL sources (sparse sources contribute nnz, dense sources contribute full n_rows*n_cols, missing sources with nonzero empty contribute full size). It stores SPARSE iff savings >= sparse_if_saves_storage_fraction (default 0.25), otherwise DENSE - and when it goes sparse it sparsifies any dense source matrices (sparsify_concatenated_matrices, concat.jl:1355-1382); when it goes dense it densifies sparse sources. So the result representation is a pure function of the storage-savings threshold, independent of how each individual source happens to be stored.
divergences.r_behavior: .concat_axis_matrix (concat.R:263-306) decides purely on source storage class: `if (all(parts are dgCMatrix)) cbind -> SPARSE else densify-all -> DENSE` (concat.R:295-300). It never computes a savings fraction and never consults `sparse_threshold` (the arg is passed in but unused in the body). Two concrete divergence directions: (1) all sources sparse-typed but DENSE-valued (e.g. 100% nonzero dgCMatrix on each source): R keeps it sparse (dgCMatrix), Julia computes negative savings and stores DENSE. (2) mixed: one dense source + one sparse mostly-zero source: R densifies the whole thing (not all dgCMatrix), Julia computes positive savings and stores SPARSE. The dafr concat parity test `concat / sparse / matrix / dense` (test-concat-jl-parity.R:333-350) uses exactly case (1) - two fully-dense dgCMatrices - and the test comment at lines 369-370 explicitly acknowledges 'dafr's concat takes the sparse fast path ... so the result IS sparse here', i.e. the divergence is known-and-papered-over: the test only asserts `as.matrix()` values, never the storage class on this case.
divergences.evidence: Julia: concat.jl:687-718, 1288-1322, 1355-1382. R: concat.R:295-300. Test that papers over it: tests/testthat/test-concat-jl-parity.R:333-374 (esp. comment 369-370)

divergences.name: Scalar MERGE_COLLECT_AXIS with a source missing the scalar: silent NA (R) vs error/crash (Julia)
divergences.julia_behavior: concatenate_merge_scalar CollectAxis (concat.jl:929-943): `scalars = [get_scalar(source, name; default=nothing) for source in sources]` then `eltype = reduce(merge_dtypes, scalars; init=typeof(empty_value))` then `scalars = [eltype(scalar) for scalar in scalars]`. A source missing the scalar yields `nothing`; calling the merged-dtype constructor on it (e.g. `Float64(nothing)`, or `Nothing(value)` when no empty is given and dtype collapses to Nothing) raises a conversion/MethodError. So Julia effectively REQUIRES every source to hold the scalar (and ignores `empty` as a fill - it only seeds the dtype from typeof(empty_value)).
divergences.r_behavior: .concat_merge_scalar CollectAxis (concat.R:421-432): `vals <- lapply(sources, function(s) if (format_has_scalar(s,name)) ...$value else NA)` then `format_set_vector(destination, dataset_axis, name, do.call(c, vals))`. A source missing the scalar silently contributes an `NA` entry in the collected dataset-axis vector. R never errors and never consults `empty`. Net: same inputs (one source lacks the scalar) -> Julia errors, R writes a vector with NA. When every source has the scalar, both produce the same collected vector (parity holds).
divergences.evidence: Julia: concat.jl:938-940. R: concat.R:428-431

probes.description: Two sources, each with a fully-DENSE (100% nonzero) sparse-typed matrix on the concat axis. Julia's storage-savings fraction is negative so it stores the concatenated matrix DENSE; dafr's cbind-of-dgCMatrix fast path stores it SPARSE. Probe the storage class of the result, not the values.
probes.query_or_snippet:
# R (dafr)
a <- memory_daf(name="A"); add_axis(a,"cell",c("A1","A2")); add_axis(a,"gene",c("X","Y"))
b <- memory_daf(name="B"); add_axis(b,"cell",c("B1","B2","B3")); add_axis(b,"gene",c("X","Y"))
set_matrix(a,"cell","gene","UMIs", methods::as(matrix(c(1,3,2,4),2,2),"dgCMatrix"))
set_matrix(b,"cell","gene","UMIs", methods::as(matrix(c(5,7,9,6,8,10),3,2),"dgCMatrix"))
d <- memory_daf(name="D"); concatenate(d,"cell",list(a,b))
inherits(get_matrix(d,"cell","gene","UMIs"), "dgCMatrix")   # dafr -> TRUE (sparse)
# Julia (DataAxesFormats)
a = MemoryDaf(name="A"); add_axis!(a,"cell",["A1","A2"]); add_axis!(a,"gene",["X","Y"])
b = MemoryDaf(name="B"); add_axis!(b,"cell",["B1","B2","B3"]); add_axis!(b,"gene",["X","Y"])
set_matrix!(a,"cell","gene","UMIs", sparse([1.0 2; 3 4]))
set_matrix!(b,"cell","gene","UMIs", sparse([5.0 6; 7 8; 9 10]))
d = MemoryDaf(name="D"); concatenate!(d,"cell",[a,b])
using SparseArrays; issparse(get_matrix(d,"cell","gene","UMIs").array)  # Julia -> false (dense; savings negative)
probes.expects: Storage class differs: dafr returns dgCMatrix (issparse=TRUE), Julia returns a dense Matrix (issparse=false). Element values are identical either way.
probes.targets_finding: Per-axis matrix sparse-vs-dense decision ignores sparse_if_saves_storage_fraction

probes.description: Mixed inputs: source A stores the matrix DENSE, source B stores it as a mostly-zero sparse matrix. Julia computes positive storage savings and stores SPARSE; dafr sees 'not all parts dgCMatrix' and densifies the whole result.
probes.query_or_snippet:
# R (dafr): A dense, B sparse mostly-zero, big enough that sparse wins in Julia
a <- memory_daf(name="A"); add_axis(a,"cell",paste0("A",1:50)); add_axis(a,"gene",c("X","Y"))
set_matrix(a,"cell","gene","UMIs", matrix(0, 50, 2))   # dense storage, all zeros
b <- memory_daf(name="B"); add_axis(b,"cell",paste0("B",1:50)); add_axis(b,"gene",c("X","Y"))
set_matrix(b,"cell","gene","UMIs", methods::as(matrix(c(rep(0,99),7),50,2),"dgCMatrix"))
d <- memory_daf(name="D"); concatenate(d,"cell",list(a,b), empty=list("cell|gene|UMIs"=0))
inherits(get_matrix(d,"cell","gene","UMIs"),"dgCMatrix")   # dafr -> FALSE (densified)
# Julia: same data; concatenate! computes savings>=0.25 -> SPARSE
# issparse(get_matrix(d,"cell","gene","UMIs").array) -> true
probes.expects: dafr returns dense, Julia returns sparse. Values identical. Confirms the inverse-direction divergence (R densifies any mixed-storage group; Julia keeps it sparse when it saves space).
probes.targets_finding: Per-axis matrix sparse-vs-dense decision ignores sparse_if_saves_storage_fraction

probes.description: MERGE_COLLECT_AXIS for a scalar that is present in one source but MISSING in another. dafr silently writes NA for the missing source; Julia errors trying to construct the merged element type from `nothing`.

probes.description: Supply `empty` as a 4-part tensor-style key for a per-entry matrix group missing from a source. Julia expand_tensors fans it out to per-entry matrix empties and fills; dafr never matches a 4-part key against the 3-part matrix lookup and raises 'no empty value'.
probes.query_or_snippet:
# R (dafr) - source B is missing the per-batch matrix 'B1_score'
a <- memory_daf(name="A"); add_axis(a,"cell",c("A1","A2")); add_axis(a,"gene",c("X","Y")); add_axis(a,"batch","B1")

concatenate(d,"cell",list(a,b), empty=list("batch|gene|cell|score"=0))

# Julia: empty=[("batch","gene","cell","score")=>0]; expand_tensors -> ("gene","cell","B1_score")=>0 -> fills, no error
probes.expects: dafr errors with 'no empty value'; Julia expands the tensor key and fills the missing per-entry matrix. Confirms the tensor-key empty expansion is not ported into concat.

Multi-axis concatenation, per-axis prefix vector, and the 'no matrix with both axes in the concat set' guard are present (concat.R:80-100 vs concat.jl:189-204).

notes:
Scope: concat.jl/concat.md vs R/concat.R for the concatenate() subsystem. The prior parity work (dev/notes/2026-05-06-concat-jl-parity-* and the P1 backlog exit 2026-06-10) was genuinely thorough: B1/B2 fixed and M1/M2/M4/M5 all closed and verified in test-concat-jl-parity.R (now 104 pass / 0 skip). I did NOT re-report those.

New findings this audit (all confirmed against source, none speculative):

1. HIGH-VALUE: Per-axis MATRIX sparse-vs-dense decision diverges (DIVERGENT). dafr decides on source storage class (all-dgCMatrix -> sparse; any-dense -> densify-all), Julia decides on the sparse_if_saves_storage_fraction storage-savings threshold and re-sparsifies/densifies as needed. The prior M2 fix only covered the vector COLLECT_AXIS *merge* path; the per-axis matrix path (the common UMI-matrix case) and the per-axis dense vector path were never aligned. The existing test `concat / sparse / matrix / dense` (test-concat-jl-parity.R:333-374) literally documents this divergence in a comment and dodges it by only checking values, not storage class. Observable as issparse()/inherits(.,\"dgCMatrix\") differences and (for files_daf) on-disk format/size. For pure in-memory value comparison the numbers match, so I rated it semantic-edge rather than silent-wrong-answer, but it is a real, reproducible, currently-live behavioral difference.

2. Per-axis dense VECTOR path never produces sparse (NARROWED/perf) - same root cause; sparse_threshold arg is dead in .concat_axis_vector. Lower impact (vectors usually dense).

3. Scalar MERGE_COLLECT_AXIS with a missing source: dafr silently writes NA, Julia errors (silent-wrong-answer). Fires only when a source lacks the scalar; full-coverage case matches.

4. TensorKey `empty` expansion not ported into concatenate() (missing-feature). Julia runs expand_tensors over `empty`; R only matches flat 2-/3-part keys. dafr's own empty_data(tensors=...) can build a 4-part key that concat will never match. Niche but a real divergence and consistent with copies.R also not auto-expanding tensors.

Probes are R+Julia snippet pairs (concat is not query-based, so no get_query() probes). They are written against memory_daf for determinism; the matrix-storage probes are also meaningful on files_daf where the divergence additionally changes the on-disk format. Severity of #1/#2 is representation/perf when only values are compared; if the differential harness compares get_matrix() return classes or files_daf storage layout, #1 will fire as a hard mismatch.

missing_in_r.name: copy_all! tensor handling (TensorKey expansion + ensure_tensors)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia copy_all! expands any TensorKey in empty/types into per-entry MatrixKeys (expand_tensors, copies.jl:737-780) and then ensure_tensors (copies.jl:961-996) CREATES an empty-filled matrix for every main-axis entry that exists in the destination but not the source. R copy_all (copies.R:515-565) has zero tensor logic. Worse, empty_data(tensors=...) builds a 4-part key 'main|rows|cols|name' (copies.R:601-604) but copy_all only ever looks up 3-part matrix keys 'rows|cols|name' (copies.R:552-553) and bare scalar keys, so a tensor empty/types spec is SILENTLY IGNORED and dest-only main-axis entries never get their empty matrices created.
missing_in_r.julia_evidence: copies.jl:695-732 (tensor_keys, expand_tensors, ensure_tensors wired into copy_all!)

missing_in_r.name: packed kwarg (write-side packed/chunked layout)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia copy_all!/copy_vector!/copy_matrix!/copy_tensor! all take packed::Maybe{Bool} routed into the writer (copies.jl:147,180,229,303,345,566). The .md staging idiom centers on copy_all!(...; packed=false) to stage a packed remote into an unpacked local daf. R has no packed parameter anywhere in copies.R or writers.R; dafr cannot WRITE packed at all (read-only packed support). So the documented staging workflow (copy_all from packed source choosing the destination layout) cannot specify packed in R.

missing_in_r.name: bestify / min_sparse_saving_fraction
missing_in_r.detail: Julia copy_vector!/copy_matrix!/copy_tensor! take bestify::Bool and min_sparse_saving_fraction to re-encode Real data sparse-vs-dense before writing (copies.jl:223-225,387-389). R has none of these. Explicitly declared out of scope in dev/plans/2026-04-21-slice-6. Real gap: a Julia user copying with bestify=true gets a compacted (possibly sparsified or densified) result; R always preserves the source's storage class only when already sparse and never promotes/demotes.

missing_in_r.name: explicit Julia-Type eltype (Float32 / Int8/16/32 / unsigned widths)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia type/eltype accepts any Type{<:StorageScalarBase}: Float32, Int8, Int16, UInt32, etc., and target_types validates isbitstype (copies.jl:1057-1064). R type accepts only the strings 'logical'|'integer'|'double'|'numeric'|'character' (.cast_scalar copies.R:11-24, .cast_vector_type copies.R:120-130, .cast_matrix_type copies.R:338-355). So copying with type=Float32 (to halve storage) or type=Int8/UInt16 is impossible in R; everything collapses to R double/integer. This is a real dtype-preservation/conversion gap even if R's storage model is the underlying cause.

narrowed.name: copy_vector sparse preservation
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia copy_vector! preserves sparse vectors in both the :same path (empty_sparse_vector! copies.jl:230-244) and the source_is_subset pad path (sparse_vector(dense), copies.jl:265-271). R copy_vector has NO sparse branch at all (copies.R:194-220): it operates on format_get_vector(source)$value which dafr densifies on readback (utils.R:112-114), and writes a dense atomic vector. A sparse source vector becomes a dense dest vector. Note dafr's own get_vector also densifies, so this is partly inherent to dafr's vector model rather than a copy-specific bug.

narrowed.name: copy_matrix default = full StorageMatrix
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia default may be a StorageMatrix used verbatim by get_matrix (copies.jl:296,335,382). R copy_matrix treats a matrix default via matrix(default, nrow=nr, ncol=nc) (copies.R:317) which flattens then refills column-major and drops dimnames; effectively only a scalar default is faithfully supported.

divergences.name: copy_matrix on flipped-only source layout: R errors, Julia succeeds
divergences.julia_behavior: copy_matrix! fetches via get_matrix(source, rows_axis, columns_axis, name; default, relayout=true) (copies.jl:382). With relayout default TRUE, get_matrix transposes-on-read when the matrix is physically stored only at the flipped (columns_axis, rows_axis). So copy_matrix!(dest, src, rows_axis=cell, columns_axis=gene, name=UMIs) succeeds even when src stores UMIs only at (gene, cell).
divergences.r_behavior: copy_matrix checks format_has_matrix(source, rows_axis, columns_axis, name) (copies.R:308) which is ORIENTATION-STRICT (memory_daf.R:314-323, files_daf_read.R:475). When src stores UMIs only at (gene,cell), this is FALSE, falls to the default branch, and with default=.DAFR_UNDEF calls .require_matrix(... relayout=FALSE) which RAISES 'no such matrix'. R never transpose-reads the flipped source.
divergences.evidence: copies.R:308-311 vs copies.jl:382; format_has_matrix orientation-strict at memory_daf.R:314-323

divergences.name: copy_all double-copies / errors when source has both physical matrix layouts
divergences.julia_behavior: copy_matrices guards with 'if !relayout || columns_axis >= rows_axis' (copies.jl:936) and skips slash-prefixed relayout-internal names 'if name[1] != /' (copies.jl:938), so each logical matrix is copied exactly once and relayout writes the flip.
divergences.r_behavior: copy_all matrix loop iterates every (ra, ca) ordered pair with no >= guard and no slash filter (copies.R:546-563). format_matrices_set is orientation-strict, so for a source that physically stores a matrix in BOTH layouts (e.g. a files_daf written with relayout=TRUE, or any relaid-out store), the name is returned at both (cell,gene) and (gene,cell). First copy (relayout=TRUE) writes both dest layouts; second copy then hits an existing dest matrix with overwrite=FALSE,insist=TRUE and RAISES (or, with overwrite=TRUE, redundantly double-writes). For a memory source that stores only one layout this does not trigger.
divergences.evidence: copies.R:546-563 (no guard) vs copies.jl:936-938; files_daf_read.R:475-486 returns names per physical orientation

divergences.name: copy_tensor with no empty + missing per-entry source matrix: R errors, Julia skips
divergences.julia_behavior: copy_tensor! passes default = empty to copy_matrix! (copies.jl:614,616). When empty is nothing, default=nothing, so get_matrix returns nothing for a missing per-entry matrix and copy_matrix! silently returns (copies.jl:382-385). Missing tensor slices are skipped.
divergences.r_behavior: copy_tensor sets default <- if (is.null(empty)) .DAFR_UNDEF else empty (copies.R:469). With empty=NULL the default is UNDEF, so a missing per-entry source matrix triggers .require_matrix and RAISES instead of skipping.
divergences.evidence: copies.R:469 vs copies.jl:614 (default = empty)

divergences.name: type-cast string<->number semantics differ (silent NA/coerce vs error)
divergences.julia_behavior: copy_scalar! type-conversion: number->String via string(value); String->number via parse(concrete_type, value), which ERRORS on a non-parseable / non-integer string; Bool(2) throws InexactError (copies.jl:71-81).
divergences.r_behavior: .cast_scalar/.cast_vector_type use as.integer/as.numeric/as.logical (copies.R:16-23,122-128). as.integer('12.5')->12 (warn, truncate), as.numeric('abc')->NA (warn, no error), as.logical(2L)->TRUE (no error). So lossy/invalid conversions that ERROR in Julia silently produce truncated values, NA, or coerced booleans in R.

divergences.name: copy_scalar pre-existing-dest vs missing-source error ordering
divergences.julia_behavior: copy_scalar! with overwrite=FALSE,insist=TRUE fetches source first (get_scalar(source,name; default=undef), copies.jl:69); if the scalar is absent from source it raises a 'missing source scalar' error BEFORE the dest set_scalar! would raise the 'already exists' error.
divergences.r_behavior: copy_scalar checks the destination first: if format_has_scalar(destination,...) && !overwrite && insist it immediately calls .require_no_scalar and raises 'already exists in destination' (copies.R:59-64), never inspecting the source. So for the corner case (dest has X, source lacks X, overwrite=FALSE, insist=TRUE) the two raise different errors.
divergences.evidence: copies.jl:65-69 vs copies.R:59-64

notes: Scope: copies.jl (1066 lines) + copies.md vs copies.R (611 lines). R is read-only; no R/Julia executed. dafr exposes copy_scalar/copy_axis/copy_vector/copy_matrix/copy_tensor/copy_all + empty_data helper (NAMESPACE:127-142). Julia exports 6 copy_*! + EmptyData (DataTypes documented in .md but not exported). The 6 core copy functions are structurally faithful ports; sparse-matrix empty==0 pad preservation and explicit-zero survival are handled and tested. The substantive gaps cluster in copy_all!'s tensor machinery (entirely absent in R; empty_data tensor keys are dead) and two correctness-class divergences that produce R errors where Julia succeeds: (1) copy_matrix against a flipped-only source orientation - R format_get_matrix/format_has_matrix are orientation-strict and never transpose-read, whereas Julia's get_matrix(...; relayout=true) does; (2) copy_all over a source that physically stores both matrix layouts double-copies because R lacks Julia's 'columns_axis >= rows_axis' relayout guard. copy_tensor without empty raises on a missing slice where Julia skips. Secondary: write-side packed and bestify are wholly absent (packed is read-only in dafr; bestify explicitly out of scope per dev/plans slice-6); explicit narrow/Float32 eltypes are inexpressible in R's string-type API; string<->number type casts diverge (R silent NA/truncate/coerce vs Julia parse/Inexact errors). Highest-priority for the differential harness: copy-flipped-matrix, copy-all-both-layouts, copy-tensor-missing-slice-no-empty, copy-all-tensor-empty-ignored. The flipped-matrix and both-layouts probes specifically need a source with non-default layout storage (relayout=TRUE writes or a files_daf) to fire - they will NOT reproduce on a trivial single-layout memory source.

missing_in_r.name: Per-direction structured documentation (contract_documentation)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia contract_documentation (contracts.jl:153-332) emits a structured markdown doc split by direction into `## Inputs` / `## Outputs`, each subdivided into `### Scalars`, `### Axes`, `### Vectors`, `### Matrices`, `### Tensors`, with type-annotated lines like `**cell @ donor**::String (required)` and short-form expectation tags (required/created/guaranteed/optional via short()). It also emits relaxed-mode notes (`Additional inputs may be used depending on the parameter(s).`). R has two doc functions (contract_docs in contract_ux.R:197 = pipe tables, contract_description in computations.R:108 = indented lines) and NEITHER splits by input/output direction, neither emits the relaxed-mode note. So the same property appears once regardless of whether it is an input or output, losing the Julia doc's input/output grouping.

missing_in_r.name: Tensor rendering in contract_description
missing_in_r.detail: R's contract_description (computations.R:120-147) filters data into scalar/vector/matrix only and renders no tensor section, so tensor contract entries are silently omitted from contract_description output. (contract_docs in contract_ux.R:170 does render tensors.) Julia's tensors_documentation (contracts.jl:295-320) always renders tensors.

narrowed.name: Contract data type vocabulary (Int/float width)
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia contract types are full Julia types (DataSpecification = Tuple{ContractExpectation, Type, AbstractString}), so a contract can demand Int32 vs Int64 vs UInt8, or Float32 vs Float64, and verify_* enforces it via `eltype(value) <: type` (contracts.jl:774, 842) / `value isa type` (contracts.jl:719). R stores `type` as a class-name string and .type_ok/.vector_type_ok/.matrix_type_ok (contracts.R:735-767) only distinguish integer/numeric/double/character/logical. There is no way to express or enforce a specific integer width or Float32/Float64 in an R contract. A Julia contract with Int32 on an Int64 vector REJECTS; the nearest R contract ("integer") accepts any integer vector. integer64/bit64 is also not in the R type switch (falls to inherits()), so an integer64 vector against an "integer" contract is rejected by R (is.integer is FALSE) where a Julia Int64 contract would accept.

divergences.name: Pre-existing OptionalOutput rejected by R, accepted by Julia (verify_input, !overwrite)
divergences.julia_behavior: is_forbidden (contracts.jl:1605-1607) = `!is_for_output && expectation == CreatedOutput && !overwrite`. ONLY CreatedOutput is forbidden when it already exists at verify_input time. A pre-existing OptionalOutput scalar/axis/vector/matrix passes verify_input silently even with overwrite=false. The Julia reference test confirms this: test/contracts.jl gates the pre-existing error on `is_output(expectation) && expectation != OptionalOutput` (lines 163,176,333,346,505,519,725,740), i.e. OptionalOutput is explicitly NOT forbidden.
divergences.r_behavior: .is_forbidden (contracts.R:727-731) = `!is_for_output && expectation %in% c(CreatedOutput, GuaranteedOutput, OptionalOutput) && !overwrite`. R RAISES `pre-existing OptionalOutput <kind>: <name>` from verify_input/verify_contract when an OptionalOutput property already exists and overwrite=FALSE. The R parity test was rewritten to match R's own behavior (test-contracts-scalar-jl-parity.R:18-20 admits 'CS1 lifted 2026-05-08: .is_forbidden widened to include OptionalOutput'), so it does NOT catch this divergence from the Julia reference.
divergences.evidence: Julia: contracts.jl:1605-1607 + test/contracts.jl:163. R: contracts.R:727-731 + .verify_scalar_data/.verify_axis_data/.verify_vector_data/.verify_matrix_data calls to .is_forbidden.

divergences.name: GuaranteedOutput enforced by R, inert in Julia
divergences.julia_behavior: is_mandatory (contracts.jl:1601-1603) checks only CreatedOutput on output; is_forbidden (contracts.jl:1605-1607) checks only CreatedOutput on input. The literal GuaranteedOutput enum is therefore NEITHER required-to-exist at verify_output NOR forbidden-when-pre-existing at verify_input. (Per its docstring it means 'created unless it already exists', i.e. a pre-existing GuaranteedOutput is fine.)
divergences.r_behavior: .is_mandatory (contracts.R:722-725) includes GuaranteedOutput in the output-mandatory set, and .is_forbidden (contracts.R:727-731) includes GuaranteedOutput in the input-forbidden set. So an R contract using the literal GuaranteedOutput enum will (a) error `missing output ...` at verify_output if the property was not created, and (b) error `pre-existing GuaranteedOutput ...` at verify_input if it already exists without overwrite. This is the opposite of Julia for the same enum value. The R parity tests never exercise R's literal GuaranteedOutput against Julia (they remap Julia-guaranteed -> R CreatedOutput, see test-contracts-scalar-jl-parity.R:10-17), so the divergence on the GuaranteedOutput symbol is unguarded.
divergences.evidence: Julia: contracts.jl:1601-1607. R: contracts.R:722-731. R test remap note: tests/testthat/test-contracts-scalar-jl-parity.R:10-17.

divergences.name: integer matrix type check is value-based in R, type-based in Julia
divergences.julia_behavior: verify_matrix_data uses `eltype(value) <: type` (contracts.jl:842). A contract `Int64` on a Float64 matrix whose values happen to be whole numbers REJECTS (Float64 <: Int64 is false). Type identity, not value, decides.
divergences.r_behavior: .matrix_type_ok(m, 'integer') calls .is_integer_valued(m) (contracts.R:758-778), which returns TRUE for a double/dgCMatrix whose stored values are all integer-valued and below .Machine$integer.max. So an R `integer` matrix contract ACCEPTS a double matrix of integer-valued numbers. Symmetric quirk for logical: .matrix_type_ok(m,'logical') accepts a numeric/dgCMatrix whose values are all 0/1 (.is_logical_valued_sparse). This is a silent acceptance where the strict Julia analog would reject on element type.
divergences.evidence: Julia: contracts.jl:842. R: contracts.R:758-783 (.matrix_type_ok, .is_integer_valued, .is_logical_valued_sparse).

divergences.name: ContractDaf wrapper name format
divergences.julia_behavior: contractor builds the wrapper name as `unique_name("<base>.for.<last-dot-segment-of-computation>")` (contracts.jl:405-410), e.g. base `memory!` + computation `pkg.normalize` -> `memory!.for.normalize#<n>` with a uniquifying counter.
divergences.r_behavior: contractor sets name = `paste0(<base>, '.', <computation>)` (contracts.R:280-282), e.g. `memory!.pkg.normalize` - no `.for.` infix, no last-segment split of the computation, no unique_name uniquifier. Affects the wrapper's name and any brief()/description() that prints it.
divergences.evidence: Julia: contracts.jl:405-410. R: contracts.R:280-282.

missing_in_r.detail: Julia computations.jl defines `macro @computation(first_contract, second_contract, definition)` and `(first, second, third, definition)` (lines 202-287) plus computation_wrapper(::Contract, ::Contract, ...) and (::Contract,::Contract,::Contract,...) (lines 78-129). These wrap functions taking 2 or 3 daf data sets, where the non-first dafs are passed as KEYWORD args matched by `Contract.name` (args_daf/patch_args, lines 42-62). R `computation(name, contract, fn)` (computations.R:41) takes exactly ONE Contract and forces the daf to be the first POSITIONAL arg (wrapped <- function(daf, ...), line 50). narrowed.name: function_contract index argument

narrowed.name: contractor name uniquification (unique_name suffix)
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia contractor builds the wrapper daf name via `unique_name("$(name).for.$(split(computation,'.')[end])")` (contracts.jl:410), producing a globally unique name like 'memory!.for.single#7'. R contractor sets name <- paste0(daf.name, '.', computation) (contracts.R:281) with NO uniquification and NO '.for.' infix. The ContractDaf name format differs; if any error message or downstream code surfaces the wrapper name, the strings will not match. Cosmetic for behavior but a real string divergence.

divergences.name: overwrite not threaded through the single-contract computation wrapper
divergences.julia_behavior: computation_wrapper (single-contract, computations.jl:64-76) calls kwargs_overwrite(kwargs) (lines 32-40) on EVERY arity and passes overwrite into contractor(name, contract, daf; name=..., overwrite=kwargs_overwrite(kwargs)) (line 68). So a single-contract computation invoked with overwrite=true permits re-writing a pre-existing CreatedOutput / GuaranteedOutput / pre-existing OptionalOutput axis/scalar/vector/matrix without the contract complaining (is_forbidden honors overwrite, contracts.jl:1605-1607). This makes an idempotent re-run of a computation work.
divergences.r_behavior: computation()'s wrapper (computations.R:50-64) calls contractor(computation=name, contract=contract, daf=daf) with NO overwrite argument, so contractor defaults overwrite=FALSE (contracts.R:273) and never inspects the caller's `...` for an `overwrite` value. The R ContractDaf and verify path FULLY support overwrite (.is_forbidden honors it, contracts.R:727-731; verify_*_data pass S7::prop(cd,'overwrite')), but the wrapper hardcodes FALSE. Therefore re-running a single-contract computation whose CreatedOutput already exists raises 'pre-existing CreatedOutput ...' even when the caller passes overwrite=TRUE. This is NOT the CC3 (multi-contract) gap - it is a distinct, undocumented single-contract divergence. The package's overwrite tests only exercise the multi-contract `cross` path (which dafr skips entirely as CC3), so this single-contract gap is untested on the R side.
divergences.evidence: Julia computations.jl:68 (overwrite = kwargs_overwrite(kwargs)) vs R computations.R:57-59 (contractor call omits overwrite); R contractor default contracts.R:273; Julia kwargs_overwrite computations.jl:32-40.

divergences.name: wrapper enforces daf as first POSITIONAL arg; rejects daf passed by name
divergences.julia_behavior: For a single unnamed contract, args_daf returns args[1] as the daf (computations.jl:43-44) and patch_args replaces args[1] (lines 56-57); for a named contract the daf is located among kwargs by matching Contract.name. There is no hard 'must be DafReader' type-guard that errors before dispatch beyond Julia's own method signature on the inner function.
divergences.r_behavior: R wrapped() begins with `if (!S7::S7_inherits(daf, DafReader)) stop('first argument to computation %s must be a DafReader')` (computations.R:50-56). Because the daf is bound to the first formal `daf`, calling the wrapped fn with the daf supplied by name (e.g. fn(quality=0, daf=d)) still binds correctly in R, but if a user wrote a fn whose first useful arg is not the daf, R cannot express it. Practically aligned for the single-contract case, but the explicit positional/type guard is an R-only behavior with a different (R-specific) error string than any Julia equivalent.
divergences.evidence: computations.R:50-56 vs computations.jl:42-62.

probes.description: Single-contract computation re-run with overwrite=TRUE on a CreatedOutput that already exists. Exposes that R's computation() wrapper does not plumb overwrite, while Julia's does (for single contracts).

narrowed.name: group_names (member dedup/sort semantics)
narrowed.what_is_missing: R's .stable_hash applies sort(unique(strings)) before hashing (groups.R:29), so it dedups repeated members and orders members LEXICALLY by name string. Julia (groups.jl:42-44) hashes each member entry name exactly once per occurrence, in the ORDER of the supplied index list (it does NOT dedup and does NOT re-sort by name; it assumes the index list is already sorted by index). For groups whose index order does not match lexical name order (e.g. axis entries named 'b','a' at indices 1,2 -> group list c(1,2)), Julia hashes name-of-1 then name-of-2 ('b' then 'a'); R hashes sort(unique(c('b','a'))) = 'a' then 'b'. Even with a matching hash function the byte stream fed to the digest differs. This is on top of the hash-function difference. R is also member-order invariant by construction (sort), whereas Julia is index-order dependent and only invariant because callers pass sorted indices.

divergences.name: group_names output name FORMAT
divergences.julia_behavior: Returns prefix + group_index + '.' + 2-digit zero-padded decimal suffix, where suffix = sum(SHA2_256 digest bytes) % 100. Example: prefix 'M', group #123 -> 'M123.89'. The group index is embedded in the name (groups.jl:46: "$(prefix)$(group_index).$(lpad(suffix, 2, "0"))"). This GUARANTEES globally unique names (the index differentiates groups) and yields a low-entropy 2-digit collision suffix (1% collision on recompute, by design per the .md doc).
divergences.r_behavior: Returns prefix + 8-hex-char FNV-32 hash of the member names, with NO group index and NO '.' separator. Example: 'grp_e7dbdb80' (groups.R:155: paste0(prefix, .stable_hash(names)); .stable_hash returns sprintf('%08x', ...)). Names are NOT guaranteed unique across groups: two groups with identical membership get IDENTICAL names (no index to disambiguate). The hash is a different algorithm (FNV-32 vs SHA2-256) over a differently-constructed byte stream (sort+unique+SOH-joined vs concatenated-in-index-order), so for the SAME input the suffix value is unrelated to Julia's.
divergences.evidence: Julia groups.jl:39-48 vs R groups.R:25-31,146-156. dafr's own test-groups-jl-parity.R:21-38 explicitly documents this as accepted divergence 'CR2' and asserts only SHAPE (2 names, prefix-tagged, deterministic), not value parity. A daf whose 'group' axis was created by Julia (names like 'M123.89') cannot have its group entries reproduced/matched by dafr's group_names, and vice-versa; any cross-implementation workflow that relies on group names being reproducible silently breaks.

divergences.name: group_names API signature
divergences.julia_behavior: group_names(names_of_entries::AbstractVector{<:AbstractString}, entries_of_groups; prefix) - takes a PLAIN VECTOR of entry names directly; has no knowledge of a daf or axis. Pure function over names + group membership (groups.jl:34-38).
divergences.r_behavior: group_names(daf, axis, entries_of_groups, prefix) - takes a DafReader and an axis name, then resolves the entry names internally via format_axis_array(daf, axis)$value (groups.R:137,144). Cannot be called with a bare name vector; requires a live daf. This is a deliberate ergonomic wrapper, but it means a caller cannot name groups for an axis-name set that is not materialized in a daf, and the out-of-range member-index check (groups.R:148-152) is an R-only addition Julia lacks (Julia would throw a BoundsError on names_of_entries[entry_index] instead).
divergences.evidence: Julia groups.jl:34-38 vs R groups.R:137-144. Functionally the R form can reproduce Julia's result for any daf-backed axis, but the surface is not 1:1 and the inputs accepted differ.

probes.expects: Both succeed (no error). Julia: 'E1.NN' (SHA of empty input). R: 'E<8hex of empty FNV>' = 'E811c9dc5' (FNV-32 offset basis hex). Different but both non-erroring; documents empty-group edge behavior parity at the no-crash level.

confirmed_parity: compact_groups: renumbers non-zero group indices densely to 1..N in first-seen order, preserves 0 as 'no group'. R groups.R:49-75 matches Julia groups.jl:59-74. Return-shape differs cosmetically (R returns list(n_groups, group_indices) since R cannot mutate in place; Julia mutates the vector and returns N) but the substantive content is identical. R adds an input guard rejecting negative indices (groups.R:51-55) and tolerates NA (treated like 0); Julia has no such guard but the documented contract is non-negative indices, so no behavioral conflict on valid input.

collect_group_members: inverts a compact group-index assignment into per-group sorted entry-position lists, omitting 0-index entries, length = max group index, empty inner vectors for absent indices. R groups.R:91-115 matches Julia groups.jl:85-96. Entry positions are appended in ascending scan order so each inner vector is naturally sorted, matching Julia. R returns integer(0) for empty groups vs Julia's empty Vector{T}; equivalent. R handles length-0 input by returning list() (groups.R:93-95); Julia returns empty Vector{Vector{T}}; equivalent.

Subsystem scope: the Julia groups.jl module contains NO query-DSL aggregate operations, NO group-by reductions, and NO grouped-accumulation API beyond these 3 helpers. grep confirms group_names/compact_groups!/collect_group_members are not consumed by any other Julia source file - they are a standalone public utility surface. The R port exports exactly the same 3 functions (NAMESPACE:114-115,161). No whole operation is missing.
notes: The 'groups' subsystem is tiny: 3 standalone public helpers, no DSL/aggregate/reduction operations (those live elsewhere in the query engine, not in groups.jl). compact_groups and collect_group_members are at genuine parity (only a cosmetic, documented return-shape difference for compact_groups since R cannot mutate in place). The single real gap is group_names, and dafr's maintainers already KNOW about it and consciously accepted it as divergence 'CR2' (test-groups-jl-parity.R:21-38, dev/notes/slice-10c-exit.md:96-104, dev/notes/2026-04-23-slice-10c-design.md:142-144): R uses a hand-rolled FNV-32 hex hash to avoid a SHA dependency, vs Julia's SHA2-256 sum%100. I flag it adversarially because the divergence is BROADER than 'just the hash function': (1) the entire name FORMAT differs - Julia embeds the group index and a '.'+2-digit decimal suffix ('M123.89'), R emits prefix+8-hex with no index ('grp_e7dbdb80'); (2) Julia's index embedding GUARANTEES uniqueness across groups, R's does not (identical-membership groups collide to the same name in R, a potential silent duplicate-axis-entry hazard - probe groups-P2); (3) the hashed byte stream is built differently (R sort+unique+SOH-join of names vs Julia concatenation of names in index order with no separator and no dedup - probe groups-P3). cache_group.R is unrelated to the Julia groups module (it is dafr's R-side mirror of Formats::CacheGroup); it contains no Julia-groups parity surface. Per the user's standing preference (Julia is the parity reference), if exact cross-implementation group-name reproducibility were ever required, R would need to switch to SHA2-256 and adopt Julia's 'prefix+index+.NN' format and index-order hashing - but this is a known, accepted, dependency-driven trade-off, not an overlooked bug. Severity of the format divergence is silent-wrong-answer ONLY for cross-implementation name-reproduction workflows; within a single implementation both are deterministic and self-consistent.

missing_in_r.name: overwrite_implicit_values (in-place rewrite of the implicit property)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia reconstruct_axis! rewrites the implicit property vector back onto existing_axis when it is NOT a string, OR when empty_implicit is a non-empty value (reconstruction.jl:100-104, 125-126, 162-164). The rewritten vector is ALWAYS String: numeric values become their string form ('1','2',...) and empty/empty_implicit entries become ''. The Julia integer test asserts the post-call type is `batch: 4 x Str (Dense)` (test/reconstruction.jl:60). dafr's reconstruct_axis (R/reconstruction.R:73-156) computes impl_str locally but NEVER calls format_set_vector for the implicit property; it leaves existing_axis/implicit_axis exactly as the caller stored it. Consequences: (a) numeric implicit axis - Julia leaves cell/batch as Str ['1','1','2',''], R leaves it as the original Int [1,1,2,0]; type AND the empty-entry value (0 vs '') differ. (b) string implicit with non-empty empty_implicit (e.g. empty_implicit='NA') - Julia overwrites cell/type to ['T','','B',''], R leaves the original ['T','NA','B','NA']. The dafr R test test-reconstruction.R:21-35 exercises empty_implicit='NA' but never inspects cell/type afterward, so this divergence is uncaught.

missing_in_r.name: PropertiesDefaults type validation + multiple input forms
missing_in_r.detail: Julia accepts properties_defaults as AbstractDict, vector-of-pairs, OR NamedTuple (PropertiesDefaults union, reconstruction.jl:22; pairs_as_dict at :78) and @asserts each key isa AbstractString and each default isa StorageScalar (:92-97). dafr only accepts a named list and performs no validation of names/types (R/reconstruction.R:142-143 just indexes properties_defaults[[prop]]). A malformed default (e.g. a list, NULL, or wrong type) silently flows into the migrated vector via vapply instead of erroring. Low impact but a missing guard.

narrowed.name: reconstruct_axis pre-existing-axis (manual-entry) merge
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia treats an already-existing rename_axis as the 'manual entries' case: it accepts the existing axis, verifies every used implicit value is present in it (error 'missing used entry: Y ...' reconstruction.jl:110-123), reuses the axis order, and for each reconstructed property requires a properties_defaults entry for axis entries NOT seen via the implicit property (error 'no default value specified for the unused entry: Z ...' :216-232). dafr supports this ONLY when properties_defaults is supplied (R/reconstruction.R:60-65, 80-93, 142-148); with a pre-existing axis and properties_defaults=NULL it HARD-ERRORS 'axis ... already exists; reconstruct_axis does not support merging into a pre-existing axis' rather than performing the merge/validation. Also dafr's missing-entry error wording differs ('implicit values not in existing axis' vs Julia 'missing used entry'). This is already noted as CR4 in test-reconstruction-jl-parity.R:50-64 but remains a genuine behavioral narrowing.

divergences.name: Returned dict key set: migrated property with no empty entries
divergences.julia_behavior: value_of_empties_of_properties[property] = value_of_empty_of_property ALWAYS sets the key (reconstruction.jl:152, 208). When a migrated property has no empty-implicit entries the value is `nothing` but the KEY IS PRESENT, so keys(results) includes that property.
divergences.r_behavior: empty_values[[prop]] <- empty_v with empty_v == NULL is a no-op under R's [[<- semantics (R/reconstruction.R:153). The property is OMITTED from the returned named list entirely. test-reconstruction.R:18 `expect_identical(empties$donor_age, NULL)` passes only because $ on a missing list element returns NULL - it is asserting the wrong thing and masks the divergence. Result: names(reconstruct_axis(...)) differs from keys(reconstruct_axis!(...)) whenever a migrated property has no empty-implicit entries.
divergences.evidence: reconstruction.jl:127,152,208 vs R/reconstruction.R:109,153; masked by test-reconstruction.R:18

divergences.name: unique-value sort collation
divergences.julia_behavior: sort!(unique_values) uses Julia's default lexicographic ordering (reconstruction.jl:106).
divergences.r_behavior: sort(unique(non_empty), method='radix') (R/reconstruction.R:91). For pure-ASCII strings radix matches Julia. For non-ASCII / mixed-case-with-locale, radix (C/byte order) and Julia's default ordering can differ from a locale-collated sort, changing the new axis entry ORDER and thus the order of every migrated property vector. Low likelihood in practice but a possible silent reordering on non-ASCII implicit values.
divergences.evidence: reconstruction.jl:106 vs R/reconstruction.R:91

divergences.name: NA implicit value handling
divergences.julia_behavior: Julia string vectors do not carry missing/NA; implicit_values are genuine strings, and only literal '' (or empty_implicit) count as empty.
divergences.r_behavior: impl_str <- as.character(impl_vec); nzchar(NA_character_) returns TRUE (default keepNA=FALSE), so an actual NA implicit entry is treated as a NON-empty key whose name is NA_character_ and indexed into mapping via mapping[[NA]] - undefined/error-prone list indexing. No explicit handling (R/reconstruction.R:74,79,112-114). This is an R-only edge with no Julia analogue but could crash or misgroup if a vector backend ever yields NA implicit values.
divergences.evidence: R/reconstruction.R:74,79,112,122

confirmed_parity: reconstruct_axis core: new axis built from sorted unique non-empty implicit values; for ASCII strings the radix sort matches Julia's ordering (reconstruction.jl:105-106 vs R/reconstruction.R:91)

Consistent-property auto-migration: scanning all vectors of existing_axis (minus the implicit property), migrating those uniquely determined by the implicit value, deleting the migrated property from existing_axis (reconstruction.jl:129-170 vs R/reconstruction.R:95-153)

implicit_properties as an explicit set restricts which properties are considered AND forces consistency (error on inconsistency); implicit_axis is excluded (reconstruction.jl:84-85,133-149 vs R/reconstruction.R:100-101,128-134)
skipped_properties excludes named properties from migration even when consistent (reconstruction.jl:130-132 vs R/reconstruction.R:97-99)

empty_implicit equates a given value with the empty string for grouping; empty entries are excluded from the new axis and their per-property value is captured separately (reconstruction.jl:99-126 vs R/reconstruction.R:75-79,114-119) - grouping semantics match (only the in-place rewrite differs)

Return value: named mapping property -> value-of-empty-implicit-entries; populated for properties that DO have empty entries (e.g. results['age']==3 / empties$color=='gray') (reconstruction.jl:64,172 vs R/reconstruction.R:153-155)
rename_axis selects the new axis name; defaults to implicit_axis (reconstruction.jl:72,80-82,158-159 vs R/reconstruction.R:49,57)

properties_defaults fills unused entries of a pre-existing axis with the per-property default (reconstruction.jl:135-148,216-232 vs R/reconstruction.R:142-148), matching the Julia 'manual/default' test
set_vector! of migrated properties uses overwrite=false in both (reconstruction.jl:168 vs R/reconstruction.R:151)
notes: Julia public surface for this subsystem = 2 items: the exported function reconstruct_axis! and the documented type alias PropertiesDefaults (collect_property_data and value_of_implicit_property are internal helpers, not exported). Core grouping/migration semantics are at parity. The two highest-value, previously-undocumented gaps are both SILENT: (1) dafr never performs Julia's overwrite_implicit_values in-place rewrite of the implicit property, so after reconstructing a numeric implicit axis (or a string one with a non-empty empty_implicit) the existing_axis property differs in both dtype and the empty-entry value from Julia - and the existing R test for empty_implicit never inspects the rewritten vector, so it is uncaught; (2) the returned mapping omits keys for migrated properties that have no empty-implicit entries (R [[<-NULL no-op), whereas Julia always includes the key with value nothing - and test-reconstruction.R:18's `expect_identical(empties$donor_age, NULL)` passes for the wrong reason, masking it. The pre-existing-axis merge narrowing (CR4) is already documented in test-reconstruction-jl-parity.R. Recommended fix direction per the project's Julia-parity default: add the overwrite_implicit_values write-back and always-set the empties key (value NULL/NA for none) to match keys(results)."}

missing_in_r.name: build_reorder_plan / FormatReorderPlan / PlannedAxis / PlannedVector / PlannedMatrix public API
missing_in_r.detail: Julia `module Reorder` exports build_reorder_plan and the four Planned* / FormatReorderPlan struct types as part of its public format-extension surface (reorder.jl:23-29). dafr keeps the equivalents strictly internal: .build_reorder_plan and .reorder_planned_axis in R/reorder_plan.R, plain named-lists instead of typed structs, none exported in NAMESPACE (only reorder_axes and reset_reorder_axes are exported, NAMESPACE:200-201). End-user reorder parity is unaffected; only third-party format-author extensibility is narrowed.

narrowed.name: files_daf reorder: sparse vector storage encoding not preserved
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia replace_reorder_vector reads source as a real SparseVector and rewrites it sparse, preserving the SparseVector encoding and its index type I=eltype(nonzeroinds(source)) (files_format.jl:1858-1872). dafr's files sparse-vector reader densifies on read (.files_get_vector_sparse returns a plain dense R vector, files_daf_read.R:348-392), so the methods::is(src_vec,'sparseVector') branch in .reorder_replace_vector (files_daf_write.R:578) is effectively dead for files_daf. The reordered vector is rewritten via .files_write_vector_dense which re-runs the sparsify heuristic and a recomputed indtype, so a vector stored sparse on disk may come back dense (or sparse with a different index width) after reorder, whereas Julia keeps the exact sparse encoding.

narrowed.name: zarr reorder: no crash recovery
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia's reorder contract (reorder.md) guarantees crash-safety: a backup + lock marker is written before any data changes so a partial reorder can be rolled back. dafr's ZarrDaf reorder is best-effort with NO backup/lock: format_reset_reorder(ZarrDaf) unconditionally returns FALSE and there is no .reorder.backup equivalent (zarr_format.R:1148-1223). A crash mid-reorder leaves the zarr store in an undefined, unrecoverable state. (ZarrDaf is an R-only format with no Julia counterpart, but it violates the general documented reorder contract that files_daf honors.)

divergences.name: files_daf reorder silently widens narrow dense dtypes (Float32->Float64, Int8/Int16/UInt8/UInt16->Int32)
divergences.julia_behavior: replace_reorder_vector/replace_reorder_matrix set T=eltype(source_vector)/eltype(source_matrix) and allocate the destination with that exact type, preserving the on-disk eltype across the reorder (files_format.jl:1859,1874,1938,1990). A Float32 vector stays Float32; an Int16 matrix stays Int16.
divergences.r_behavior: dafr reads narrow dtypes by upcasting in memory (Float32->double, Int8/16/UInt8/16->integer; files_io.R:300-339) so the source dtype tag is lost before reorder. .reorder_replace_vector/.reorder_replace_matrix then recompute the dtype from the permuted R values via .dtype_for_r_vector, which only ever yields Bool/Int32/Int64/Float64/String (files_io.R:50-70). A property stored as Float32 is rewritten as Float64 (2x size) and Int8/Int16/UInt8/UInt16 become Int32, silently changing the descriptor and on-disk bytes. Values stay numerically equal so it is silent.
divergences.evidence: R: files_daf_write.R:584 (eltype<-.dtype_for_r_vector(new_nzv)), :613 (dtype<-.dtype_for_r_vector(as.vector(permuted))); files_io.R:339,300-307. Julia: files_format.jl:1859,1874,1990

divergences.name: files_daf reorder changes sparse index width vs Julia (UInt16 -> UInt32)
divergences.julia_behavior: For sparse vectors/matrices the destination index type is I=eltype(nonzeroinds(source))/eltype(source_matrix.colptr), i.e. the source's stored indtype is preserved exactly (files_format.jl:1860,1939). A UInt16-indexed sparse matrix stays UInt16 after reorder.
divergences.r_behavior: .reorder_replace_vector/.reorder_replace_matrix recompute indtype via .indtype_for_size(n) / .indtype_for_size(max(nr,nc,nnz)), and dafr's .indtype_for_size only ever returns UInt32 or UInt64 - it never emits UInt16 (files_io.R:345-349), unlike Julia's indtype_for_size which uses UInt16 for size<=65535 (TanayLabUtilities matrix_formats.jl:1217-1225). So a Julia-written small sparse property reordered by dafr has its index width silently widened from UInt16 to UInt32.
divergences.evidence: R: files_daf_write.R:586,304; files_io.R:345-349. Julia: files_format.jl:1860,1939; matrix_formats.jl:1217-1225

divergences.name: files_daf reorder forces sparse matrix nzval to Float64
divergences.julia_behavior: Sparse matrix reorder preserves T=eltype(source_matrix) for the nzval buffer (files_format.jl:1938,1941-1949); an Int32 or Float32 sparse matrix keeps its element type.
divergences.r_behavior: .files_write_matrix_sparse writes nzval as as.double(mat@x) with eltype 'Float64' for any non-logical sparse matrix (files_daf_write.R:300,327-331), because R's Matrix package only has dgCMatrix(double)/lgCMatrix(logical). After reorder an Int/Float32 sparse matrix is stored Float64. This is a general files_daf storage ceiling (R cannot hold a typed-int sparse matrix), but reorder is a rewrite so it manifests here.
divergences.evidence: R: files_daf_write.R:298-333 (.files_write_matrix_sparse called from .reorder_replace_matrix:610). Julia: files_format.jl:1937-1949

divergences.name: memory_daf and zarr reorder tick the crash counter on the axis pass; Julia (and files) do not
divergences.julia_behavior: Reorder.format_replace_reorder! for MemoryDaf calls tick_crash_counter! once per planned vector and once per planned matrix only, never on the axis pass (memory_format.jl:543,560). So _simulate_crash=N fires after the N-th vector/matrix replacement.
divergences.r_behavior: dafr's MemoryDaf path calls tick_crash_counter inside the axis loop too (memory_daf.R:456), in addition to per-vector (:470) and per-matrix (:478); ZarrDaf does the same (zarr_format.R:1160,1169,1182). With the same crash_counter=N the crash therefore fires one (or n_axes) ticks earlier than Julia, so the crash index semantics differ. files_daf matches Julia (no per-axis tick, files_daf_write.R:640-656). Test-only internal (_simulate_crash/crash_counter), so impact is limited to crash-recovery test reproducibility, not user behavior.
divergences.evidence: R: memory_daf.R:455-456; zarr_format.R:1159-1160. Julia: memory_format.jl:528-543 (axis loop has no tick)

non-leaf writer is rejected with an error before any data is touched (R reorder.R:46-51 / :70-75 is_leaf check; Julia reorder.jl:270-278)

build_reorder_plan walking logic matches: enumerates vectors on each permuted axis, matrices on (perm_axis, other) for all other axes, plus (other, perm_axis) only when other is not itself permuted (avoids double-listing) - R reorder_plan.R:65-115 vs Julia reorder.jl:137-167

files_daf crash-safe reorder via .reorder.backup hardlink directory with lock/backup/replace/cleanup/reset and auto-rollback on r+/w+ open - files_daf_write.R:446-748 and files_daf.R:70-75 mirror Julia files_format.jl:1738-2060 REORDER_BACKUP_DIR protocol and the reorder.md contract

reorder_axes values for dense and sparse matrices (row/column/both permutation) are numerically correct, including canonical row-index ordering within sparse columns (R uses Matrix '[' subscripting and order(); Julia uses permute_sparse_* kernels with sortperm) - both produce sorted rowval/nzind

reset_reorder_axes returns Bool (TRUE iff a pending reorder was rolled back), no-op on memory with no pending reorder returning FALSE - reorder.R:148-151 and memory_daf.R:506-516 match Julia reorder.jl:409-451 / memory_format.jl:578-595
notes: The reorder ORCHESTRATION layer (reorder.R / reorder_plan.R, the named subsystem files) is at strong parity with Julia: plan-building, multi-writer coordination, permutation direction/validation, leaf checks, empty-input handling, and the files_daf crash-recovery protocol all match. The real divergences live one layer down in the format-specific replace kernels (files_daf_write.R, zarr_format.R) and are rooted in dafr's storage-fidelity model, not in reorder logic per se: (1) dafr loses narrow on-disk dtypes (Float32, Int8/16, UInt8/16, UInt16 indices) on read because R has no native narrow types, so any reorder rewrite silently widens them, whereas Julia preserves eltype/indtype exactly through the reorder; (2) dafr's .indtype_for_size never emits UInt16 (caps low end at UInt32) so it diverges from Julia's indtype_for_size even for supported widths; (3) dafr sparse VECTORS densify on read so sparse-vector encoding isn't preserved through reorder; (4) ZarrDaf (an R-only format) reorder has no crash recovery, violating the documented crash-safe contract; (5) a test-only crash-counter tick-on-axis-pass discrepancy in memory/zarr backends. Findings 1-3 are the highest-value ones the existing value-only parity tests (test-reorder-jl-parity.R) would not catch, since they compare numeric values via as.matrix() and never assert on-disk descriptor eltype/indtype. All probes that compare against Julia require a Julia-written fixture with narrow dtypes (Float32 / UInt16-indexed sparse) since dafr cannot itself create those types in memory; the differential harness should generate those fixtures from Julia, reorder them with dafr, and diff the descriptor JSON.
