divergences.name: base_daf_view JSON serialization format is cross-language incompatible
divergences.julia_behavior: complete_chain! (chains.jl:185-191) writes `JSON.json(Dict(:axes=>axes,:data=>data))` where axes/data are vectors of Pairs/Tuples. Each pair serializes as a single-key JSON object and a tuple matrix/vector key stringifies WITH PARENS, e.g. base_daf_view = `{"axes":[{"cell":"="},{"gene":"="}],"data":[{"(cell, gene, umi)":"="}]}`. On read, parse_view_parameters (complete.jl:135-154) iterates each entry as a single-key object and converts paren-strings back to tuples by replacing `(`->`[`,`)`->`]` then JSON-parsing.
divergences.r_behavior: complete_chain (complete.R:61-63) writes `jsonlite::toJSON(list(axes=axes,data=data), auto_unbox=TRUE)` where axes/data are viewer-format lists-of-lists. This produces POSITIONAL ARRAYS, e.g. base_daf_view = `{"axes":[["cell","="],["gene","="]],"data":[[["cell","gene","umi"],"="]]}`. complete_daf (complete.R:162-170) reads it back with fromJSON(simplifyVector=FALSE) + .normalise_json_spec, which expects this array shape. R cannot parse Julia's single-key-object form (it would treat `{"cell":"="}` as a named list, not list(key,value)), and Julia's parse_view_parameters cannot parse R's array form (it iterates `for (pattern,value) in pair` expecting an object). A chain persisted by one language is unreadable by the other whenever a base_daf_view is present.
divergences.evidence: chains.jl:185-191 + complete.jl:135-154 (Julia) vs complete.R:57-66,162-170,178-193 (R)

divergences.name: complete_daf r+ with a base_daf_view returns a read-only ViewDaf (loses writability)
divergences.julia_behavior: Under mode="r+", complete_daf builds chain_writer(dafs) where dafs is `[leaf, viewer(base_chain)]` reversed (complete.jl:75-79, 109-122). The view wraps only the BASE; the writable leaf sits on top, so the returned object is a DafWriter and the leaf remains writable; the view affects only how base data is seen.
divergences.r_behavior: complete.R:155-170 builds the chain first (chain_writer when mode=='r+'), then if the leaf has base_daf_view it wraps the ENTIRE chain in `viewer(chain, ...)` (complete.R:167). ViewDaf extends DafReadOnly (view_daf.R:134-137), so the returned object is read-only and any set_*/add_* on it errors - the user cannot write the leaf. R's r+ test (test-complete.R:59-72) only covers the no-view case, so this is untested.
divergences.evidence: complete.jl:75-79,109-122 vs complete.R:155-170 + view_daf.R:134-137

divergences.name: base_daf_view applies to whole chain (R) vs base only (Julia)
divergences.julia_behavior: viewer wraps ONLY the base chain; the leaf daf is chained ON TOP of the viewed base (complete.jl:119-122 builds `chain` of base_dafs, wraps in viewer, then the calling daf chains over it). Leaf-local data is NOT subject to the view's renames/filters and can override base data through the view.
divergences.r_behavior: viewer wraps the ENTIRE chain including the leaf (complete.R:167 `viewer(chain, ...)` where chain already contains base+leaf). The view's axis renames / data filters apply to leaf-local data too, and the leaf can no longer override through the outer view. For a renamed-axis view, leaf vectors/matrices on the renamed axis are reachable only if they were on the base axis name; leaf data added under the renamed name would not resolve the same way as in Julia.
divergences.evidence: complete.jl:109-123 (view wraps base, leaf on top) vs complete.R:155-170 (view wraps full chain)

divergences.name: complete_daf chain/view naming
divergences.julia_behavior: Chain name is `name * ".complete"` (complete.jl:77-78); nested chains/views get `.chain_<index>` / `.view_<index>` suffixes (complete.jl:119-120). Default name when not given is the leaf path (complete.jl:64-66).
divergences.r_behavior: Chain name is `basename(leaf)` with no `.complete` suffix (complete.R:154-160); the re-applied view reuses chain_name (complete.R:167) with no `.view` suffix. Default name is `basename(leaf)` rather than the full leaf path. Cosmetic, but observable via the daf's name property and in log messages.

divergences.name: open_daf memory:// extension not in Julia
divergences.julia_behavior: Julia open_daf has no memory backend. A path "memory://" (or empty) falls to the default FilesDaf branch (complete.jl:195-196) and tries to open a directory literally named 'memory:' (or '').
divergences.r_behavior: R open_daf (open_daf.R:30-32) treats NULL / "" / "memory://" as an in-memory memory_daf. This is an R-only convenience extension; it diverges only for the (unusual) case of a real on-disk directory literally named with those tokens, and means complete chains referencing 'memory://' behave differently across languages. Low impact since memory dafs have no on-disk path to persist into base_daf_repository anyway.
divergences.evidence: open_daf.R:30-32 vs complete.jl:178-198 (no memory branch)

notes:
SCOPE NOTE: The task FOCUS describes 'fill missing'/IfMissing storage-layer completion, but complete.jl is actually about completing repository CHAINS (tracing base_daf_repository / base_daf_view across a tree of dafs). There is no missing-vector/matrix defaulting logic in this file; IfMissing/default semantics live in queries/readers, not here. I audited the actual chain-completion subsystem.

HIGHEST-IMPACT FINDINGS (verify first): (1) base_daf_view JSON format is structurally incompatible across languages - Julia writes single-key objects with paren-stringified tuple keys and parse_view_parameters (complete.jl:135-154) round-trips that exact shape, while R writes/reads positional nested arrays (complete.R:61-66,162-193). Any cross-language complete chain with a view breaks. Within each language the round-trip is self-consistent and tested (R test-complete-view-roundtrip.R). (2) R complete_daf returns a read-only ViewDaf under r+ when a base_daf_view exists, losing leaf writability; Julia keeps the leaf writable because it views only the base and chains the writer on top. (3) R applies base_daf_view to the WHOLE chain vs Julia to the BASE only, and R ignores base_daf_view on intermediate (non-leaf) repositories entirely.

TESTING GAP: Julia complete_chain! is marked '# UNTESTED' (chains.jl:166) and there are zero Julia tests for complete_daf/base_daf_view round-trip, so the Julia reference behavior for views was derived by reading code (collect_dafs recursion + parse_view_parameters), not from a passing test. R has self-consistent round-trip tests but none covering r+ with a view, intermediate views, or cross-language JSON.

R EXTENSIONS beyond Julia open_daf: memory:// in-memory shortcut (open_daf.R:30-32). MISSING backends in R open_daf: ZipDaf (.daf.zip/.dafs.zip#) and H5df (.h5df/.h5dfs#, explicit error). The packed kwarg is absent from both R complete_daf and R open_daf.

divergences.name: adapter copy-back uses insist=FALSE (silent skip) vs Julia insist=true (error) on pre-existing destination properties
divergences.julia_behavior: adapters.jl:114 calls copy_all!(; source=output, destination=daf, empty, relayout, overwrite) WITHOUT passing insist, so it uses copy_all!'s default insist=true (copies.jl:688). With the adapter defaults overwrite=false, when the output view re-exposes a property (scalar/vector/matrix) that already exists in the base daf, copy_vector!/copy_matrix!/copy_scalar! do NOT take their early-skip guard (guard requires !insist, e.g. copies.jl:186, 354, 65) and fall through to set_vector!/set_matrix!/set_scalar! with overwrite=false, which call require_no_vector/require_no_matrix and RAISE an 'already exists' error (writers.jl:362-364, 795). So copying back a colliding property aborts the whole adapter with an error.
divergences.r_behavior: adapters.R:96 explicitly passes insist = FALSE to copy_all. In copies.R the per-property helpers (copy_scalar copies.R:59-63, copy_vector copies.R:186-188, copy_matrix copies.R:354-356) take the early return when insist=FALSE && !overwrite && property exists, SILENTLY SKIPPING the copy. So a colliding copy-back is dropped without error, and the base daf keeps its old value. dev/plans/2026-04-21-slice-6-... documents this as intentional ('skipping conflicts silently is the established behaviour'), but the rationale conflates 'property only in daf, not in output view' (never iterated, insist-irrelevant) with 'property in BOTH output view and daf' (the case insist actually governs).

divergences.name: name parameter: Julia uses it only as a flame_timed profiling label; R injects it into internal daf object names
divergences.julia_behavior: adapters.jl:97 uses name ONLY as the flame_timed(name) span label. The internal dafs are named from base_name alone: viewer name = base_name*'.input' (line 106), capture = base_name*'.capture' (107), chain = base_name*'.adapted' (108), output = base_name*'.output' (113). Default name='.adapter' (line 87) therefore never appears in any daf object name; with base daf named 'memory!' the input view is 'memory!.input'.
divergences.r_behavior: adapters.R has no profiling infrastructure; instead it interpolates name INTO every internal daf name: paste0(base_name, name, '.input') (line 78), '.capture' (81), '.adapted' (84), '.output' (90). With default name='.adapter' and base 'memory!' the input view is 'memory!.adapter.input' (extra '.adapter' segment vs Julia's 'memory!.input'). These names surface in error messages (e.g. 'no-op'/missing-property errors and chain/view diagnostics), so identical failing inputs produce differently-worded errors.

divergences.name: No flame_timed profiling spans in R adapter
divergences.julia_behavior: adapters.jl wraps the whole body in flame_timed(name) and the input/output phases in flame_timed('input')/flame_timed('output') (lines 97, 100, 112), emitting nested profiling spans consumable by TanayLabUtilities flame timing.
divergences.r_behavior: adapters.R has no flame_timed equivalent (grep for flame_timed across R/ returns nothing); the adapter runs with no profiling instrumentation. Purely an observability/perf-tooling gap, no effect on data results.

probes.description: Adapter whose output view copies back a scalar that already exists in the base daf with overwrite=false. This is the minimal trigger for the insist default divergence: Julia should error on the copy-back collision, R should silently skip and keep the old value.
probes.query_or_snippet:

d <- memory_daf(name='base'); set_scalar(d,'kept', 1L)
adapter(d, function(adapted){ set_scalar(adapted,'kept', 999L); 'ok' },
  input_data=list(list('x','. kept')),
  output_data=list(list('kept','. x')))
# R: returns 'ok'; get_scalar(d,'kept') stays 1L (copy-back of pre-existing 'kept' silently skipped)

adapter(daf; input_data=['x' => '. kept'], output_data=['kept' => '. x']) do adapted
  set_scalar!(adapted,'kept',999); 'ok'
end

confirmed_parity: Single exported public item 'adapter' present and exported on both sides (Julia adapters.jl:6 export adapter; R NAMESPACE:100 export(adapter)).

Core pipeline structure matches: build input view -> create capture writable -> chain_writer([input, capture]) as 'adapted' -> run computation(adapted) -> build output view -> copy output back into base daf -> return the computation's value (adapters.jl:106-116 vs adapters.R:77-98).
no-op guard parity: both error when all of input_axes/input_data/output_axes/output_data are NULL/nothing (adapters.jl:102-105 @assert 'no-op adapter' vs adapters.R:70-74 stop('no-op adapter ...')).

capture default parity: Julia default capture=MemoryDaf called as capture(; name=...) vs R default capture=memory_daf called as capture(name=...) - same effect, a fresh in-memory writable (adapters.jl:90,107 vs adapters.R:63,81).
relayout default TRUE and overwrite default FALSE match on both sides and are threaded straight into copy_all!/copy_all (adapters.jl:94-95,114 vs adapters.R:64,93-97).

Return-value passthrough parity: result = computation(adapted) / fn(adapted) is returned verbatim, including non-scalar returns (adapters.jl:111,116 vs adapters.R:87,98; R test 'returns fn value untouched').

empty subset-pad feature is wired through to the copy-back on both sides (Julia empty tuple-keys, R flat 'axis|name' / 'rows|cols|name' keys); R test 'sparse pad-mode copy-back preserves sparsity' exercises it.
DafWriter type-check on the daf argument exists on both (Julia dispatch on ::DafWriter vs R explicit S7_inherits(daf, DafWriter) stop, adapters.R:66-68).
Behavioral fixture parity confirmed for the non-colliding output (per-cell total_umis): R test-adapter-julia-compat.R reproduces the committed Julia fixture.json values bit-identically (856 totals).
notes: Subsystem is tiny: exactly one public function (adapter). The port is structurally faithful. The one substantive concern is the insist=FALSE default in R's copy-back vs Julia's insist=true (the default of copy_all!). Static analysis is unambiguous about the R side (silent skip) and about Julia's per-property helpers (set_vector!/set_matrix!/set_scalar! with overwrite=false call require_no_* which raises). HOWEVER there is a genuine tension I could not resolve read-only: the committed fixture (tests/testthat/fixtures/julia-adapter/fixture.json, real Julia HEAD 49fbba14, result 'ok') was produced by regen-julia-adapter-fixture.jl which copies back ALL_MATRICES+ALL_VECTORS over example_cells_daf that already contains UMIs and the original vectors. If Julia's copy_all! with insist=true truly errored on those collisions, that script would have thrown and never written the fixture - yet it returned 'ok'. I found NO skip-if-identical or same-backing short-circuit anywhere in copies.jl/writers.jl that would explain this. So either (a) Julia's output view (ALL_VECTORS/ALL_MATRICES over the input+capture chain) does NOT in fact re-expose the already-in-base properties back to daf in a colliding way, or (b) there is some path I missed. Probe adapter-insist-collision-scalar is the clean minimal test (a scalar deliberately overwritten in the computation and copied back under its original name) and adapter-insist-collision-allmatrices reruns the exact fixture scenario; together they will tell the harness definitively whether this is a crash-or-error divergence (most likely) or a semantic-edge that the typical adapter idiom never hits. I deliberately did NOT downgrade it because the R code path provably differs and would mask a real Julia error if one occurs. The other two divergences (name->daf-name injection, missing flame_timed) are cosmetic/perf only and never affect data results.

missing_in_r.name: empty_dense_vector! / empty_sparse_vector! / empty_dense_matrix! / empty_sparse_matrix!
missing_in_r.detail: Julia writers.jl exports the entire empty-builder family: empty_dense_vector! (writers.jl:402), empty_sparse_vector! (518), empty_dense_matrix! (838), empty_sparse_matrix! (973). These allocate an uninitialized buffer (dense vector/matrix, or sparse nzind/nzval/colptr/rowval), hand it to a `fill` callback, then finalize - the core idiom for writing large arrays directly into memory-mapped disk storage without an extra copy. NONE of these exist in dafr. NAMESPACE has no `empty_*` builder export (only empty_cache/empty_data). The R FilesDaf write path (files_daf_write.R) has internal sparse-assembly helpers but no public empty-builder API. Julia evidence: writers.jl:402-1091; R evidence: `grep empty_dense|empty_sparse R/ NAMESPACE` returns nothing.

missing_in_r.name: get_empty_dense_vector! / get_empty_sparse_vector! / get_empty_dense_matrix! / get_empty_sparse_matrix! + filled_empty_* (8 functions)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia exports the lock-explicit get_empty_*! / filled_empty_*! pairs (writers.jl:22-25 exports get_empty_dense_matrix!, get_empty_dense_vector!, get_empty_sparse_matrix!, get_empty_sparse_vector!, and lines 18-21 filled_empty_*). The .md (writers.md:38-47) documents these as the no-callback driver path for language wrappers (e.g. a Python/R wrapper that cannot pass a Julia closure). Entirely absent in dafr. This is the exact mechanism a foreign-language binding would need; its absence means dafr cannot stream-fill on-disk arrays.

missing_in_r.name: set_vector eltype / packed arguments
missing_in_r.detail: Julia set_vector! (writers.jl:320-328) has keyword args `eltype::Maybe{Type{<:StorageReal}} = nothing` (convert data to a target element type before storing) and `packed::Maybe{Bool} = nothing` (per-write override of the daf packed default). dafr set_vector (writers.R:102) has only (daf, axis, name, vec, overwrite). No way to request element-type coercion at the writer API, and no per-write packed override.

missing_in_r.name: set_matrix eltype / packed arguments
missing_in_r.detail: Julia set_matrix! (writers.jl:745-755) has `eltype::Maybe{Type{<:StorageScalarBase}} = nothing` and `packed::Maybe{Bool} = nothing`. dafr set_matrix (writers.R:162) has only (daf, rows_axis, columns_axis, name, mat, overwrite, relayout). No eltype coercion, no per-write packed override.

missing_in_r.name: add_axis overwrite argument
missing_in_r.detail: Julia add_axis! (writers.jl:174-179) has `overwrite::Bool = false`: when true it first delete_axis! the existing axis (and all its data) then adds. dafr add_axis (writers.R:14) has only (daf, axis, entries); calling it on an existing axis always errors. A user must manually delete_axis first, and there is no atomic replace.

missing_in_r.name: relayout_matrix packed argument
missing_in_r.detail: Julia relayout_matrix! (writers.jl:1126-1132) has `packed::Maybe{Bool} = nothing`; when nothing it mirrors the source's packed encoding, otherwise forces the flipped copy's encoding. dafr relayout_matrix (writers.R:242) has only (daf, rows_axis, columns_axis, name, overwrite). No packed control.

missing_in_r.name: matrices_set relayout / tensors arguments
missing_in_r.detail: Julia matrices_set (readers.jl:807-813) has `tensors::Bool = true` and `relayout::Bool = true`. relayout=true unions in matrix names available only in the flipped layout; tensors=true condenses tensor matrices `<entry>_name` into `/<tensor_axis>/_matrix`. dafr matrices_set (readers.R:363) has only (daf, rows_axis, columns_axis) - it returns only the names stored at the exact (rows_axis,columns_axis) pair with no relayout union and no tensor condensation.

missing_in_r.name: description deep / cache / tensors arguments + rich rendering
missing_in_r.detail: Julia description (readers.jl:1257) has `cache::Bool=false, deep::Bool=false, tensors::Bool=true` and renders dtype/size/layout/sparsity for every vector and matrix (e.g. `donor: 856 x Str (Dense)`, `UMIs: 856 x 683 x UInt8 in Columns (Dense)`, `is_lateral: 683 x Bool (Dense; 438 (64%) true)`), plus a tensors section, optional cache section, and deep nested-daf description. dafr description (readers.R:473) takes only (daf), emits bare property names with NO dtype/size/sparsity/layout, no tensors/cache/deep. Output is structurally different and far less informative.

narrowed.name: has_vector / get_vector reserved `name` and `index` properties
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia has_vector (readers.jl:545) returns true for name=="name" || name=="index" unconditionally; get_vector (readers.jl:664-674) returns the axis entry names for "name" and the 1..N integer indices for "index" as a NamedVector. dafr has_vector (readers.R:234) and get_vector (readers.R:276) do NOT special-case these: has_vector(daf, axis, "name") returns FALSE and get_vector(daf, axis, "name") / get_vector(daf, axis, "index") raise `missing vector: name/index`. (The query layer query_eval.R:658 handles virtual `name`, but the direct reader API does not, so the two APIs disagree.)

narrowed.name: get_vector default=0 sparse construction
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia get_vector (readers.jl:696-697): when the vector is missing and default==0, it returns spzeros (a SparseVector) of the axis length, not a dense fill. dafr get_vector (readers.R:285-296) always builds a dense `rep(default, n)` regardless of default value, so a 0 default yields a dense vector. Result values match but the storage/representation (sparse vs dense) diverges, which matters for downstream sparsity-preserving ops and memory.

narrowed.name: get_matrix default=0 sparse construction
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia get_matrix (readers.jl:1005-1010): missing matrix with default==0 returns spzeros (SparseMatrixCSC). dafr get_matrix (readers.R:407) always builds a dense `matrix(default,...)`. Same representational divergence as the vector case.

narrowed.name: get_vector named-vector default validation
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia get_vector (readers.jl:657-662): a StorageVector default must match the axis length, and a NamedVector default must have names exactly equal to the axis entries (require_axis_names). dafr get_vector (readers.R:285-296) only checks length==1 or length==n; it ignores the names of a named default entirely (does not validate or reorder them), so a length-n named default with names in the wrong order is silently used as-is in the wrong positions.

narrowed.name: axis_dict return type
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia axis_dict (readers.jl:365) returns an OrderedDict{AbstractString,Int64} preserving axis order with 1-based indices. dafr axis_dict (readers.R:174) returns an R environment (format_axis_dict). Environments are unordered and have no defined iteration order, so code relying on ordered iteration of the dict (Julia: insertion/axis order) cannot be reproduced; lookups still work.

divergences.name: set_matrix relayout default (FALSE in R vs true in Julia)
divergences.julia_behavior: set_matrix! default relayout=true (writers.jl:753): storing a matrix automatically also stores the flipped (row-major) layout, so get_matrix(columns_axis, rows_axis, name; relayout=false) immediately succeeds.
divergences.r_behavior: set_matrix default relayout=FALSE (writers.R:163, and the doc at writers.R:146 explicitly notes 'Default FALSE; set to TRUE to match Julia'). By default dafr stores only one layout, so the flipped layout is materialized lazily/transposed-on-the-fly by get_matrix instead of being persisted. Different on-disk/stored state and different has_matrix(...; relayout=FALSE) results after a plain set_matrix.
divergences.evidence: writers.jl:753 (relayout::Bool = true) vs writers.R:163 (relayout = FALSE) + writers.R:146 doc comment

divergences.name: set_vector named-vector: subset+reorder vs exact-match
divergences.julia_behavior: set_vector! with a NamedVector requires names equal to the FULL axis entries (require_axis_names, writers.jl:341-342) - a mismatch (including a subset or wrong order) is an error.
divergences.r_behavior: .validate_vector_value (utils.R:68-84) accepts a named vector whose names are any SUBSET of axis entries, errors only if a name is NOT in the axis, then reorders to axis order. A partial-coverage named vector that Julia would reject (length mismatch) is also caught by the length check, but a full-length named vector in a different order is silently reordered in R whereas Julia errors on any name!=expected ordering mismatch. Net: R is more permissive and reorders silently; Julia errors.
divergences.evidence: writers.jl:341 require_axis_names(...names(vector,1)) vs R/utils.R:56-86 .validate_vector_value subset+reorder

divergences.name: add_axis empty-string entry handling
divergences.julia_behavior: add_axis! (writers.jl:195) only checks allunique(entries); an empty-string entry name is accepted.
divergences.r_behavior: format_add_axis for MemoryDaf (memory_daf.R:154-156) rejects any empty-string entry with `axis X entries contain empty strings`. dafr is stricter; an axis Julia would create, dafr refuses.
divergences.evidence: writers.jl:195 (only allunique) vs memory_daf.R:154

divergences.name: version-counter increment policy (documented as intentional, but observable)
divergences.julia_behavior: Julia bumps the vector version on set_vector! AND on empty_dense_vector!/empty_sparse_vector! (update_before_set_vector at writers.jl:623 via format_increment_version_counter); matrix version bumps on set_matrix!/empty_*matrix!; axis version bumps on delete_axis!.
divergences.r_behavior: dafr (cache.R:93-102) bumps vector counter only on set_vector, matrix only on set_matrix, axis only on delete_axis. Because dafr has no empty_* builders the empty-path bump is moot, but the public *_version_counter values can still differ from Julia after equivalent operation sequences (e.g. Julia's add_axis! does not bump axis counter either, so those match; the divergence surfaces if/when empty_* builders are added). Low severity / mostly internal.
divergences.evidence: writers.jl:623 update_before_set_vector increments version; cache.R:93-121 R bump policy

missing_in_r.name: TensorKey (3D-tensor key form: <axis>,<axis>,<axis>,<name>)
missing_in_r.detail: Julia keys.jl:51 defines TensorKey = Tuple of 4 AbstractStrings, documented (keys.jl:43-52) as a way to refer to a whole set of `<main-axis-entry>_<property>` matrices for copy/view/contract/concat. dafr has no TensorKey concept. grep across R/ finds no 4-tuple data key, no `tensor` handling in copies.R / view_daf.R / contracts.R / concat.R. So a copy/view/contract spec that in Julia names a tensor (expanding to the per-entry matrices) has no dafr equivalent. Julia evidence: keys.jl:51-57 (TensorKey, DataKey = Union{PropertyKey, TensorKey}). R evidence: no match for tensor key in R/ (grep tensor R/ -> only unrelated).

missing_in_r.name: named_tuple_as_pairs / pairs_as_dict
missing_in_r.detail: keys.jl:59-91 exports pairs_as_dict and named_tuple_as_pairs (convert dict / vector-of-pairs / NamedTuple, nothing-tolerant). These are Julia-idiom helpers for keyword-style API inputs; R passes named lists natively so there is no direct equivalent and none is needed. Listed only for completeness; not a behavioral gap.

narrowed.name: Storage eltype write/round-trip: Float32 and narrow/unsigned ints
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia StorageScalar admits 11 stored eltypes: Bool, Int8/16/32/64, UInt8/16/32/64, Float32, Float64, String (storage_types.jl:53-93). dafr READS all 11 (files_daf_read.R:383-389 maps Int8/16/UInt8/16/32 -> R integer, Int64/UInt64 -> bit64, others -> double), but on WRITE can only emit Bool, Int32, Int64, Float64, String: .dtype_for_r_vector (files_io.R:50-70) maps R logical->Bool, integer->Int32, integer64->Int64, double->Float64, character->String. There is NO path to write Float32, Int8, Int16, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64. Consequence: reading a UInt8 (or Float32) store and writing it back silently changes the on-disk eltype (UInt8 16-bit etc. -> Int32, 4x bytes; Float32 -> Float64) and the values for Float32 are re-stored at Float64 width. Julia preserves the exact eltype on round-trip.

narrowed.name: Float32 value semantics in `% Convert type Float32` / Float32-typed results
narrowed.what_is_missing: .cast_to_type (operations.R:546-580) maps Float32 -> R storage.mode 'double' with NO Float32 rounding (line 553 numeric/double/Float32/Float64 -> 'double'; line 577 as.vector(value, mode='double')). Julia Float32(x) actually rounds to 32-bit precision. So `% Convert type Float32` of 0.1 yields R 0.1 (Float64) vs Julia 0.10000000149011612 (Float32 widened back to Float64 on display). Any query producing a Float32 result diverges in the low-order bits. The InexactError range checks are correct; only the precision narrowing is absent.

narrowed.name: Property/axis NAME grammar is far stricter in dafr than Julia
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia imposes NO character restrictions on axis names, axis entries, scalar/vector/matrix property names: keys.jl declares them as bare AbstractString; set_scalar! (writers.jl:77), add_axis! (writers.jl:174-205), set_vector!/set_matrix! do only existence/uniqueness checks, never a char/empty/whitespace check. Names with ':' ',' '/' '\' tab/newline are storable and queryable (escaped via Tokens.escape_value, tokens.jl). dafr .assert_name (utils.R:8-27) REJECTS empty names, leading/trailing whitespace, and any of '/ \ : , \n \r \t \0' (utils.R:3 .FORBIDDEN_NAME_CHARS). .assert_name is wired into every writer entry point (writers.R:15-245, copies.R, contracts.R, contract_ux.R, concat.R:72). Root cause: dafr builds cache keys by ':'-joining (cache.R:15-19 cache_key_vector='vector:axis:name', cache_key_matrix='matrix:rows:cols:name'), so ':' would collide; Julia uses structured tuple CacheKeys (formats.jl:104,183-194) and has no such constraint. Result: a vector named 'a:b' or an axis named 'a,b' that Julia stores/reads fine is rejected at write time by dafr.

narrowed.name: Sum/Abs/Round integer eltype-widening rules (sum_type_for / unsigned_type_for / int_type_for)
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia defines result-eltype rules: Sum of Bool->UInt32, Int8/16->Int32, UInt8/16->UInt32 (operations.jl:121-133 SUM_DTYPE_FOR); Abs of Int8->UInt8 ... (operations.jl:156-168 UNSIGNED_DTYPE_FOR); Round of Float32->Int32, Float64->Int64 (operations.jl:90-101 INT_DTYPE_FOR). dafr .op_sum/.op_abs/.op_round just call sum()/abs()/round() on R Int32/Int64/double with no width mapping. Numerically the answers coincide for almost all values because R has only Int32/Int64/double, BUT: (a) the default `% Round` eltype on a Float32-origin column is Int32 in Julia vs Int64 in dafr (since dafr stored it as Float64); (b) Sum-of-Bool eltype is UInt32 vs R integer; (c) for Int8 inputs near typemin, Abs result eltype UInt8 vs R int. Mostly eltype-only divergence, observable on write-back or on a downstream overflow.

divergences.name: register_query_operation idempotency vs unconditional conflict error
divergences.julia_behavior: registry.jl:163-196 register_query_operation is documented idempotent ('safe to invoke multiple times'). Re-registering the SAME type from the SAME source_file/source_line is a silent no-op; it errors ONLY when a name is re-registered with a DIFFERENT type/file/line ('conflicting registrations for the <kind> operation'). There is no `overwrite` parameter.
divergences.r_behavior: operations.R:44-101 register_reduction/register_eltwise default overwrite=FALSE and raise 'conflicting registrations for the <kind> operation: <name>' on ANY second registration of an existing name regardless of whether fn is identical, unless the caller passes overwrite=TRUE. So idempotent re-registration of the same op raises in R where Julia silently succeeds; conversely Julia has no overwrite escape hatch (a genuinely changed op cannot be re-registered without erroring, whereas R's overwrite=TRUE allows it). Different control surface and different default outcome for the same-op case.
divergences.evidence: registry.jl:181-195 vs R/operations.R:52-58,91-97

divergences.name: Op-name character validation on register
divergences.julia_behavior: Op name derives from the Julia type name (registry.jl:180 String(type.name.name)) which is always a valid identifier; Julia never validates op-name characters - the name is structurally constrained by being a type.
divergences.r_behavior: register_reduction/register_eltwise call .assert_name(name) (operations.R:45,84), so a custom op registered with a name containing '/', ':', ',' etc. is rejected ('forbidden character(s)') - see test-operations-registry.R:50-52 register_reduction('a/b', identity) -> 'forbidden'. In dafr a custom op name is a free-form string, so this guard can fire; in Julia the analogous situation cannot arise. Low impact (op names are identifiers in practice) but a behavioral asymmetry.
divergences.evidence: registry.jl:180 vs R/operations.R:45,84 + tests/testthat/test-operations-registry.R:50-52

confirmed_parity: Storage type ALLOW-LIST at the query layer: dafr accepts the full Julia dtype name set Bool/Int8-64/UInt8-64/Float32/Float64/String including lowercase aliases (operations.R:436-468 .NUMBER_TYPES + .JULIA_TYPE_CANONICAL; query_eval.R:558 error lists all), matching Julia DTYPE_BY_NAME (operations.jl:215+). No allowed type-NAME is rejected by dafr at parse/validate time.

Integer InexactError range checks per target type are correct (operations.R:475-541 .INT_TYPE_RANGES + .check_inexact_int/.check_inexact_bool) and match Julia's InexactError on out-of-range / fractional integer casts, including UInt overflow and negative-into-UInt.

String-input support is restricted to exactly Count and Mode reductions on both sides: dafr op_dispatch.R:56-61 accepts_string_input=TRUE only for Mode/Count; Julia supports_strings true only for Count (operations.jl:1056) and Mode (operations.jl:1116). All other ops reject String input with matching 'unsupported input type: String' wording.

Matrix key is axis-order-insensitive in both: Julia MatrixKey doc 'axes order does not matter' (keys.jl:33-36) + matrices_set relayout swap (formats.jl:165-167); dafr stores/relayouts both orientations (cache.R matrix keys + relayout handling).

Op registry storage + lookup + listing is equivalent: register_reduction/register_eltwise/get_*/registered_* (operations.R:44-203) mirror Julia's ELTWISE/REDUCTION_REGISTERED_OPERATIONS dicts (registry.jl:146-196). Built-in op set matches (Sum,Mean,Max,Min,Count,Var,Std,VarN,StdN,Median,Quantile,GeoMean,Mode reductions; Log,Abs,Exp,Sqrt,Round,Clamp,Convert,Fraction,Significant eltwise).

Conflict-error MESSAGE template matches Julia byte-for-byte: 'conflicting registrations for the <kind> operation: <name>\nfirst in: <file>:<line>\nsecond in: <file>:<line>' (operations.R:52-58,91-97 vs registry.jl:186-191), with source-location capture (operations.R:16-24).

Per-op `type` parameter policy matches Julia: Sum/Count number; Mean/Median/Var/Std/VarN/StdN/GeoMean/Quantile/Log/Fraction float-only; Min/Max/Mode/Significant no `type`; Convert required number (op_dispatch.R:39-120, cross-checked to operations.jl parse_*_type_value usage).
notes:
The three NAMED R files (classes.R, op_dispatch.R, options.R) only contain a sliver of this subsystem: classes.R is S7 reader/writer class scaffolding (not types/keys/registry at all); options.R is unrelated runtime options; op_dispatch.R is the per-op param/type/string-input validator table. The actual storage-type system lives in R/operations.R (.cast_to_type, .NUMBER_TYPES, .INT_TYPE_RANGES, .check_inexact_*), R/files_io.R (.dtype_* on-disk mapping), R/files_daf_read.R (read-side eltype->R type), and R/query_eval.R (IfMissing/type coercion). The key/name grammar lives in R/utils.R (.assert_name, .FORBIDDEN_NAME_CHARS) and R/cache.R (':'-joined cache keys). The registry lives in R/operations.R. I read all of these.

Two highest-value findings the existing parity docs likely under-weight:
1) The NAME-GRAMMAR divergence is real and structural (dafr's ':'-joined cache keys force forbidding ':'/','; Julia uses tuple CacheKeys and forbids nothing). It is a hard write-time rejection of names Julia stores fine, NOT just a cosmetic message difference. The dev/notes audit (2026-05-03-audit-r-quirks.md) mentions dafr forbids '' for axes but frames it as an internal invariant, not as a Julia divergence.
2) The Float32 + narrow/unsigned-int STORAGE gap: dafr reads all 11 eltypes but can only WRITE 5 (Bool/Int32/Int64/Float64/String). A UInt8 or Float32 store silently changes eltype (and Float32 changes precision) on dafr write-back. This is inherent to R lacking those storage types, so it is a true narrowing rather than a fixable bug, but it should be documented as a round-trip fidelity gap.

I could not RUN either side (read-only), so the empty-axis-name probe (TKR-03) and the Sum/Round/Abs eltype probes are written so the harness can confirm whether the eltype/empty-name divergence actually fires; the name-grammar and Float32-precision divergences are high-confidence from static reading alone.

divergences.name: description() omits per-property dtype/shape/density detail lines
divergences.julia_behavior: description() renders each vector as '<name>: <len> x <Type> (Dense|Sparse[; nnz (pct%) true])' and each matrix as '<name>: <rows> x <cols> x <Type> in Columns|Rows (Dense|Sparse)'. E.g. for example_cells_daf(): 'age: 95 x UInt32 (Dense)', 'is_lateral: 683 x Bool (Dense; 438 (64%) true)', 'UMIs: 856 x 683 x UInt8 in Columns (Dense)'.
divergences.r_behavior: dafr description() (R/readers.R:506-524) prints ONLY the bare property name: 'age', 'is_lateral', 'UMIs' - with no length, dtype, layout, density, or true-count suffix. The example_data.R docstrings (R/example_data.R:133,149,165) explicitly claim cat(description(d)) 'Mirrors example_data.jl jldoctest', but the emitted text does not match the documented contract. tests/testthat/test-example-data.R never asserts the full description() string, so this is untested.

divergences.name: Chain description() header: type label and missing 'chain:' member block
divergences.julia_behavior: For a WriteChain, description() emits 'type: Write Chain' (or 'ReadOnly Chain') followed by a 'chain:' block listing each member daf as '- MemoryDaf cells!' / '- MemoryDaf metacells!' (when not deep). See example_chain_daf() doctest.
divergences.r_behavior: dafr WriteChainDaf has no format_description_header override, so it falls back to the default 'type: WriteChainDaf' (the R class name, R/readers.R:604-607) and emits NO 'chain:' block listing the underlying member dafs. So example_chain_daf() description diverges in both the type line and the omitted chain-member list.
divergences.evidence: Julia: DataAxesFormats.jl/src/chains.jl:807-830 (format_description_header pushes 'type: Write Chain' + 'chain:' + '- <brief(daf)>'). dafr: no format_description_header method for WriteChainDaf in R/chain_daf.R; default at R/readers.R:604-607.

divergences.name: Vector/matrix dtype width: R integer (32-bit signed) vs Julia UInt32/UInt8
divergences.julia_behavior: cast_vector narrows Float32 -> UInt32 then Int32 (age -> UInt32). cast_matrix narrows to UInt8 then UInt16 (UMIs -> UInt8, 1 byte). description() shows 'UInt32'/'UInt8'.
divergences.r_behavior: dafr .cast_vector narrows to R integer (32-bit SIGNED) for age; .cast_matrix uses storage.mode<-'integer' (32-bit signed) for UMIs (R/example_data.R:16-37). Data values are identical, but the stored dtype is wider and signed. This is an inherent R limitation (no unsigned/narrow int types), and is the root cause of the description() dtype-label divergence above for these properties. Not a data error, but downstream code that round-trips example data to a typed FilesDaf/H5df store and compares dtype labels would see UInt32/UInt8 vs Int32 mismatches.
divergences.evidence: Julia: example_data.jl:146-198 cast_vector/cast_matrix. dafr: R/example_data.R:16-37 .cast_vector/.cast_matrix.

notes: Scope clarification: this audit's primary deliverable is (a) example_data content parity and (b) the top-level export-surface inventory. The 106 raw 'unmatched' Julia exports break down as: ~60 are Julia type-system constructs/aliases with no meaningful R analogue (StorageFloat, StorageInteger, StorageScalar, AxisKey, DataKey, MatrixKey, ScalarKey, VectorKey, PropertyKey, TensorKey, DataSpecification, AxisSpecification, Query, QuerySequence, QueryString, QueryData, ContractAxes/Axis/Data/Expectation, ViewAxes/Axis/Data/Datum, PlannedAxis/Matrix/Vector, FrameColumn(s), CacheGroup, MergeAction/Data/Datum, FormatReorderPlan, etc.) - these are intentionally absent in R and should NOT be counted as gaps; ~25 are conversion/type-introspection helpers (float_type_for, int_type_for, sum_type_for, unsigned_type_for, parse_*_type_value, supports_strings, reduction_result_type, compute_eltwise, compute_reduction, error_invalid_parameter_value, named_tuple_as_pairs, pairs_as_dict) owned by the operations/registry subsystem agents; and the remainder are genuine feature gaps owned by OTHER subsystem agents (H5df, ZipDaf, the empty-allocation writer family, LazySparse selection constructors, mmap-zip low-level helpers patch/shrink/reserve/remove_entries/try_mmap_entry_as). I surfaced those in missing_in_r so the surface gap is recorded, but defer their behavioral semantics to the owning audits to avoid double-counting. The ONE finding squarely inside the exports-example subsystem that prior parity docs appear to have missed is the description() detail-line divergence: dafr description() prints bare property names and omits the '<len> x <Type> (Dense; nnz%)' / '<r> x <c> x <Type> in Columns (Dense)' suffix that the Julia example_data doctests are the canonical fixtures for, AND the chain description() omits both the 'Write Chain' type label and the 'chain:' member-list block. The example_data.R docstrings claim to 'Mirror' those doctests but the output does not match, and no test pins the full string. Probes exdata-01/02 expose this directly; exdata-03/04 lock in that the underlying DATA is fully equivalent so the divergence is formatting + R dtype-width only.

narrowed.name: FilesDaf dense/sparse read of UInt32 values > 2^31-1
narrowed.what_is_missing: R/files_io.R:329-332 .read_bin_dense reads UInt32 with readBin(what="integer", size=4L, signed=TRUE). Base R has no unsigned 32-bit integer; any UInt32 stored value above 2147483647 (e.g. 3e9, or UInt32 max 4294967295) is read back as a negative int32 or NA. dafr cannot WRITE such values (its writeBin path goes through as.integer which caps at 2^31-1), but a Julia-written FilesDaf storing a full-range UInt32 column, read by dafr, silently yields wrong values. UInt8 (signed=FALSE) and UInt16 (signed=FALSE) are correct because they fit signed int32; only UInt32 uses signed=TRUE. The R7 audit (NEXT_AUDIT.md 'What this audit did NOT cover') explicitly never round-tripped Float32/Int8/Int16/UInt8/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64 from a real-Julia fixture, so this path was never exercised with out-of-int32-range data. The fix shape mirrors the Int64/UInt64 branches (lines 333-338): read as 8-byte... no - for UInt32 read the 4 bytes as unsigned and promote to double or bit64 when > 2^31-1.

narrowed.name: Round op result-type integer-preservation for integer input with integer bounds (Clamp/Round dtype)
narrowed.what_is_missing: Julia's Clamp (operations.jl type_for_clamp, ~line 562) keeps integer output when input is integer AND both min/max are integer-valued, else promotes; R .op_clamp only applies a dtype when an explicit `type=` is given and otherwise leaves storage as-is. This is a result-dtype subtlety (not a value error) but can surface as a kind_mismatch in differential output. Lower confidence; flagged for a probe rather than asserted as a bug.

divergences.name: Quantile vs Median NaN handling inconsistency
divergences.julia_behavior: Julia computes both Median and Quantile via sparse_median/sparse_quantile (sort-based, NaN sorts to a defined position); both Median and Quantile p 0.5 are the SAME operation and produce the same value/behavior on a NaN-containing vector.
divergences.r_behavior: R/operations.R:.op_median (line 938-940) has a NaN short-circuit returning NaN, but .op_quantile (line 944-962) has NO such short-circuit and calls stats::quantile(x, p, na.rm=FALSE) which ERRORS on NaN ('missing values and NaN's not allowed if na.rm is FALSE'). So `@ cell : with_nan >> Median` returns NaN while `@ cell : with_nan >> Quantile p 0.5` ERRORS in R - two queries that are semantically the same operation diverge from each other within R, and at least one diverges from Julia. The grouped path (query_eval.R:3001-3005) uses stats::quantile for BOTH Median and Quantile, so grouped `>> Median` on a NaN group ALSO errors, inconsistent with scalar Median. NOTE: Round-4 doc claims `with_nan >> Quantile p 0.5` 'agrees' with Julia - that can only be true if Julia also errors on Quantile-of-NaN, which would then make scalar Median (returns NaN) the divergent one. Either way there is an unresolved Median/Quantile inconsistency the docs did not flag.

divergences.name: Exp / Sqrt eltwise operations accepted by R, absent in Julia
divergences.julia_behavior: Julia operations.jl exports exactly 20 ops (Abs, Clamp, Convert, Count, Fraction, Log, Max, Median, Mean, GeoMean, Min, Mode, Quantile, Round, Significant, Std, StdN, Sum, Var, VarN). There is NO Exp and NO Sqrt operation; `% Exp` / `% Sqrt` in a query is an unknown operation and Julia rejects it.
divergences.r_behavior: R registers Exp (.op_exp) and Sqrt (.op_sqrt) as eltwise ops (operations.R:1040-1041) AND gives them .OP_META entries (op_dispatch.R:114-119), so `@ cell : score % Exp` and `% Sqrt` are accepted and evaluated by dafr. Per project policy (Julia authoritative), R is too lenient: these should be rejected in the query DSL. Low severity (extra functionality, not a wrong answer) and the docs never recorded it.

probes.description: Differential read of a full-range UInt32 column from a real-Julia-written FilesDaf. Build in Julia a FilesDaf with a cell axis and a UInt32 vector containing a value above 2^31-1; read it in dafr and compare. dafr will return a negative int32 / NA; Julia returns the unsigned value.
probes.query_or_snippet: Julia: set_vector!(daf, "cell", "big_u32", UInt32[1, 2147483648, 4294967295, 0, 100]); save to FilesDaf. R: get_vector(open_daf(path), "cell", "big_u32") -- expect c(1, 2147483648, 4294967295, 0, 100); dafr likely returns c(1, NA/-2147483648, NA/-1, 0, 100).
probes.expects: Julia: [1, 2147483648, 4294967295, 0, 100] (UInt32). dafr: corrupted (negative/NA) for the two large values.

probes.description: Run Median and Quantile p 0.5 on the same NaN-containing vector through both languages and compare not just to Julia but to each other within R. Exposes the .op_median-has-NaN-shortcut / .op_quantile-does-not asymmetry.
probes.query_or_snippet: Fixture with_nan = [1.0, NaN, 3.0, NaN, 5.0]. Queries: `@ cell : with_nan >> Median`  and  `@ cell : with_nan >> Quantile p 0.5`  and grouped `@ cell : with_nan / type >> Median`.
probes.expects: If Median and Quantile p 0.5 are the same operation, both should agree in each language. dafr: Median -> NaN, Quantile p 0.5 -> ERROR (stats::quantile na.rm=FALSE). Grouped Median -> ERROR. Divergence is the cross-query inconsistency within dafr plus the dafr-vs-Julia mismatch on whichever Julia does not error/agree on.

probes.description: Apply % Exp and % Sqrt in the query DSL. R evaluates them; Julia rejects them as unknown operations.
probes.query_or_snippet: `@ cell : score % Exp`  and  `@ cell : score % Sqrt`  and  `@ cell @ gene :: frac % Sqrt`.
probes.expects: Julia: parse/eval error (unknown operation Exp/Sqrt). dafr: returns the exp()/sqrt() of the values.

probes.description: Same UInt32 issue but via the sparse FilesDaf read path (files_daf_read.R fills integer(n) then writes nzval read with the same .read_bin_dense signed=TRUE). Confirms the sparse path is affected identically to dense.
probes.query_or_snippet: Julia: store a mostly-zero UInt32 cell vector with a couple of entries above 2^31-1 so it sparsifies; save to FilesDaf. R: get_vector(...) and compare the nonzero entries.
probes.expects: Julia: correct unsigned values at the nonzero positions. dafr: corrupted (negative/NA) for entries above 2^31-1.
probes.targets_finding: FilesDaf UInt32 read (narrowed item #1, sparse variant)

notes:
Methodology: read FINDINGS.md (all rounds 1-6 + E re-sweep), FINDINGS_R7.md, NEXT_AUDIT.md, then located each documented fix in the current 0.4.4 R source and confirmed it is present and wired into the live call paths. The overwhelming majority of documented findings are genuinely fixed - the central validator (op_dispatch.R/.OP_META) and the .demote_int64 / .cmp_ordering / .promote_int64_for_fractional_cmp / .check_inexact_int / .resolve_named_numeric helpers are all in place and called from every dispatcher. No regressions of previously-fixed findings were found; the documented 'still divergent' items (E1 Median NaN+Inf, C10 regex ~ ., E5/B10 square-matrix pick, D2 1-ulp, D4 ±1e309) remain exactly as documented.

Two genuinely new (doc-missed) findings: (1) HIGH VALUE - FilesDaf UInt32 dense+sparse read uses signed=TRUE, silently corrupting UInt32 values above 2^31-1 read from a real-Julia-written store; the R7 audit explicitly never exercised non-int32-range unsigned dtypes from a Julia fixture. (2) Exp/Sqrt are R-only operations Julia lacks (lenient-vs-strict). Plus a semantic-edge inconsistency: .op_median has a NaN short-circuit but .op_quantile and the grouped Median/Quantile path (stats::quantile na.rm=FALSE) do not, so Median and Quantile-p-0.5 (same operation) diverge from each other in dafr on NaN input.

Caveat: I could not locate TanayLabUtilities' sparse_median/sparse_quantile source on this box (slow network FS), so the exact Julia NaN-on-Quantile behavior is unconfirmed; probe P2 is framed to resolve whether Julia errors, returns NaN, or returns a finite value, and whether the divergence is dafr-vs-Julia or a dafr-internal Median/Quantile inconsistency. All probes are runnable on the existing dev/adversarial-parity fixture (with_nan, u32_count, score, type) extended with a Julia-side large-UInt32 column for P1/P4.
